evidence.effect: Physicians did not rate semantic-retrieval RAG responses as superior to those from Mixtral without retrieval across the rated dimensions (no numbers in abstract). Semantic retrieval did improve guideline selection.
evidence.tradeoff: Retrieval mechanisms often produced answers with linguistic inconsistencies. The performance deficit and error susceptibility were mainly attributed to limits of automated chunk splitting.
evidence.quote: However, while the semantic retrieval enhanced the guideline selection process, physicians did not rate its responses as superior in terms of medical and content accuracy, case relevance, factual integrity, and overall usability when compared to those from the Mixtral model without a retrieval mechanism.

evidence.title: The Impact of Access to Clinical Guidelines on LLM-Based Treatment Recommendations for Chronic Hepatitis B
evidence.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-4 without context, relying on its internal (training) knowledge
evidence.outcome: Coherence of treatment recommendations with the 2024 WHO CHB guidelines, rated by seven physicians; also preciseness/clarity, completeness, textual correctness
evidence.effect: Guideline coherence rose from 51% to 91%; preciseness and clarity +54%, completeness of incorporating case vignette information +24%, textual correctness +12%
evidence.quote: Using GPT-4 with context increased the coherence of the treatment recommendations with the new 2024 guidelines from 51% to 91% compared to GPT-4 without context.

evidence.title: Application of NotebookLM, a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation, for lung cancer staging
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-4o with the reference knowledge supplied directly in the prompt (no RAG), and GPT-4o without the reference knowledge
evidence.outcome: Lung cancer staging accuracy on 100 fictional cases
evidence.effect: NotebookLM (RAG) 86% accuracy vs GPT-4o 39% with REK in prompt and 25% without REK
evidence.quote: NotebookLM achieved 86% diagnostic accuracy in the lung cancer staging experiment, outperforming GPT-4o, which recorded 39% accuracy with the REK and 25% without it.

evidence.title: Retrieval-augmented ChatGPT-4o improves accuracy but reduces readability in hip arthroscopy patient education
evidence.venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
evidence.comparator_used: standard ChatGPT-4o without retrieval-augmented 'deep research' mode
evidence.outcome: accuracy, comprehensiveness, clarity, and readability of hip arthroscopy patient-education responses
evidence.effect: Accuracy: 4.7 ± 0.4 vs. 4.0 ± 0.5; p = 0.012. Comprehensiveness: 4.8 ± 0.3 vs. 3.9 ± 0.6; p < 0.001. Clarity: 4.4 ± 0.5 vs. 4.6 ± 0.4; p = 0.048. Readability Likert scores were comparable (p = 0.729), but FKGL and FRES favoured the standard model (both p < 0.001).
evidence.tradeoff: Reduced clarity and objective readability versus the standard model; FKGL and FRES favoured the standard model (both p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Deep research provides superior scientific rigour, whereas the standard model offers better readability.

evidence.title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Large Language Models for Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: Clinical Accuracy and Efficiency
evidence.comparator_used: Native (non-RAG) counterparts of three LLMs, benchmarked in the authors' previous study on the same question set
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on infective endocarditis prophylaxis questions
evidence.effect: RAG's impact on accuracy varied by model; no pooled effect size or per-model figures given in the abstract
evidence.quote: RAG's impact on accuracy varied by model.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language model clinical reasoning in glaucoma using retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.venue: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research
evidence.comparator_used: Matched non-RAG counterparts of the same models (GPT, Gemini, Grok without RAG), i.e. training knowledge alone
evidence.outcome: Composite score of medical accuracy, key point coverage and logical completeness in glaucoma cases (human-rating sensitivity analysis); safety audit also reported as more safety-aware
evidence.effect: Composite RAG advantage: GPT mean difference=0.119 (95% CI: 0.068-0.173); Gemini 0.095 (95% CI: 0.030-0.161); Grok 0.110 (95% CI: 0.033-0.194)
evidence.quote: RAG-enhanced models consistently outperformed their matched non-RAG counterparts across evaluation domains.

evidence.title: Retrieval‑augmented large language models for depression screening and suicide risk stratification
evidence.comparator_used: Same three Chinese LLMs (DeepSeek, Qwen, Baichuan) in base configuration without RAG (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Depression detection and suicide risk classification F1, symptom-summary quality (BLEU-2, ROUGE-L), and clinician-rated empathy in RAG-enhanced models
evidence.effect: Qwen3 + RAG depression detection F1 = 0.9107; suicide risk stratification F1 improved by approximately 0.15 vs non-RAG baselines; BLEU-2 relative gains 44.1–207.2%; ROUGE-L relative gains 37.0–94.0%; best configuration reproducibility overall κ = 0.93 (95% CI 0.91–0.95)
evidence.quote: RAG augmentation consistently improved diagnostic performance across datasets.

evidence.title: Configuring large language models to deliver patient-facing explanations of pathology reports
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLM configurations without retrieval augmentation (no retrieval from the curated pathology knowledge base)
evidence.outcome: Pairwise arena preference (Bradley-Terry ranking) of patient-facing pathology explanations
evidence.effect: Retrieval augmentation was associated with improved response preference; the top configuration (larger model plus curated pathology knowledge base retrieval) was strongly preferred over pathologist-written responses. No numeric estimates in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Pairwise arena comparisons indicated that the configuration parameters strongly influenced performance, with both model size and retrieval augmentation associated with improved response preference.

evidence.title: Locally Deployed Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Outpatient Prescription Review: Crossover Study
evidence.comparator_used: Plain AI review without knowledge augmentation (model's own knowledge), run on the same 213 prescriptions
evidence.outcome: Model hallucination rate
evidence.effect: Hallucination rate fell from 19.7% (42/213) to 4.7% (10/213), an absolute reduction of 15.0 percentage points (relative reduction 76.2%; P<.001)
evidence.quote: Knowledge augmentation reduced the model hallucination rate from 19.7% (42/213 prescriptions) to 4.7% (10/213), an absolute reduction of 15.0 percentage points (relative reduction 76.2%; P<.001).

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs for Mental Health: Quantifying the Incremental Contribution of Retrieval Within a Layered Safety Architecture
evidence.comparator_used: RAG-disabled mode of the same six LLMs (parametric knowledge only) within the Wysa DMHI
evidence.outcome: Intent detection performance (accuracy, recall, precision, F1) for multi-class intents such as self-harm, abuse and panic
evidence.effect: No numeric values given in the abstract; RAG-enabled mode is reported to improve accuracy, consistency and safety, with differences tested for statistical significance
evidence.tradeoff: RAG caused a rise in false alarms (lower precision); flagged cases are routed to additional review rather than acted on directly
evidence.quote: Overall, these findings support RAG as a promising approach to improve the accuracy, consistency and safety of LLM-driven DMHIs.

evidence.title: RadOncRAG: A Novel Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Improves Large Language Model Benchmark Performance in Radiation Oncology
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot LLM answering without retrieval (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on 298 scorable ACR 2021 radiation oncology in-training exam questions
evidence.effect: Gemini-2.0 improved 6.7% (to 79.2%), Llama-3-70b 8.4% (to 75.8%), GPT-4o 5.7% (to 85.6%) with RAG; top reasoning models (GPT-4o1, o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1) had no improvement or detriment with RAG. Gains in clinical, biology and physics domains.
evidence.tradeoff: RAG workflows and reasoning models incurred higher computational costs.
evidence.quote: Top scoring reasoning models surpassed graduating resident averages by 17.7%-20% (P < .01), but had no improvement or detriment with RAG.

evidence.title: Superhuman performance on urology board questions using an explainable language model enhanced with European Association of Urology guidelines
evidence.venue: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o and Uro_Chat without retrieval (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Mean rate of correct answers (RoCA) on 200 European Board of Urology in-service assessment questions over 10 runs
evidence.effect: UroBot-4o (RAG with 2023 EAU guidelines) 88.4% vs GPT-4o zero-shot 77.6% (+10.8%); highest inter-run agreement (Fleiss' kappa 0.979); urologists' published average 68.7%
evidence.quote: UroBot-4o achieved the highest RoCA, with an average of 88.4%, outperforming GPT-4o (77.6%) by 10.8%.

evidence.title: Grounding Large Language Models in Clinical Evidence: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Querying UK NICE Clinical Guidelines
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLMs without retrieval augmentation (no RAG)
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness (answer supported by source text) on 70 curated question-answer pairs
evidence.effect: Faithfulness increased by 64.7 percentage points to 99.5% for RAG-enhanced O4-Mini
evidence.quote: Faithfulness, the measure of whether an answer is supported by the source text, was increased by 64.7 percentage points to 99.5% for the RAG-enhanced O4-Mini model and significantly outperformed the medical-focused Meditron3-8B LLM, which scored 43%.

evidence.title: Medical QA dialogue datasets in RAG systems performance evaluation and ChatGPT optimization
evidence.comparator_used: Direct prompting of ChatGPT-3.5 without retrieval (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Generation quality (ROUGE-1-f, BERTScore_F1) in Chinese clinical question answering; expert-rated readability, accuracy and authenticity
evidence.effect: ROUGE-1-f +12.6%, BERTScore_F1 +1.5% (p < 0.05); expert evaluation improvements in readability, accuracy, and authenticity (all p < 0.001)
evidence.quote: Experimental results show that dialogue-based retrieval significantly improves generation quality relative to direct prompting (e.g., ROUGE-1-f: +12.6%, BERTScore_F1: +1.5%, p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Large language models answering structured questions on external cervical resorption: a comparative study
evidence.comparator_used: Four base LLM configurations without document grounding (ChatGPT-5, Gemini, Claude, Mistral) versus two document-grounded RAG configurations (NotebookLM, Perplexity Pro)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy (error rate) on 46 dichotomous ECR questions
evidence.effect: Model configuration significantly influenced performance (p = 0.050). The RAG tool NotebookLM had the lowest estimated error rate (3.0%), followed by the base model Gemini (4.0%). The base model Claude had the highest (12.0%). Overall accuracy was 90.8%. The abstract gives no error rate for Perplexity Pro.
evidence.quote: Model configuration significantly influenced performance (p = 0.050), with NotebookLM and Gemini showing the lowest estimated error rates (3.0% and 4.0%, respectively), while Claude demonstrated the highest error rate (12.0%).

evidence.title: MedFabric: Gold Evidence Hides the Difficulty of Word-Level Medical Fabrication Detection
evidence.comparator_used: No-evidence baseline (the LLM's own knowledge alone), with gold versus wrong retrieved passages
evidence.outcome: Macro F1 for fabrication detection by a strong LLM, by evidence condition
evidence.effect: Scores 91% with the gold passage, but 35% with a wrong passage, which is below its own no-evidence baseline
evidence.tradeoff: Incorrect retrieved evidence makes detection worse than having no evidence, a new failure mode
evidence.quote: Our central finding is that detection is governed by evidence correctness rather than fabrication subtlety, since a strong LLM scores 91% with the gold passage but falls to 35%, below its own no-evidence baseline, under a wrong one, a pattern that holds on two benchmarks at two model scales.

evidence.title: Effects of Cross-lingual Evidence in Multilingual Medical Question Answering
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline without external evidence (model parametric knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Multilingual medical QA accuracy
evidence.effect: No numbers in the abstract. Web-retrieved English evidence was most beneficial for high-resource languages. For low-resource languages, combined English and target-language retrieval gave accuracy comparable to high-resource languages. External knowledge did not improve performance systematically.
evidence.quote: These findings challenge the assumption that external knowledge systematically improves performance and reveal that effective strategies depend on both the source of language resources and on model scale.

evidence.title: Investigating LLM Capabilities on Long Context Comprehension for Medical Question Answering
evidence.comparator_used: Full long-context patient/document content supplied without retrieval, across varying content size and relevance settings
evidence.outcome: Medical long-context QA comprehension in single- vs multi-document datasets
evidence.effect: No numbers in the abstract; RAG excels in challenging cases, with best settings differing between single- and multi-document QA datasets, but is limited in temporal reasoning cases
evidence.tradeoff: Limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning
evidence.quote: Our quantitative analysis reveals challenging cases where RAG excels while still showing limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning.

evidence.title: Implementing a context-augmented large language model to guide precision cancer medicine
evidence.comparator_used: LLM-only (training knowledge alone, no retrieved context)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of biomarker-driven treatment recommendations across 234 therapy-biomarker relationships
evidence.effect: LLM-only 62–75% accuracy; RAG-LLM 79–91% with an unstructured database and 94–95% with a structured database. Structured augmentation also raised precision (49% to 80%) and F1-score (57% to 84%) compared with unstructured augmentation. On actual oncologist queries, RAG-LLM achieved 81–90% accuracy.
evidence.tradeoff: Further work is needed to generate reliable responses for ambiguous or unsupported clinical scenarios.
evidence.quote: While LLM-only achieved 62–75% accuracy in biomarker-driven treatment recommendations, RAG-LLM achieved 79–91% accuracy with an unstructured database and 94–95% accuracy with a structured database.

evidence.title: Semantic Clinical Artificial Intelligence vs Native Large Language Model Performance on the USMLE
evidence.comparator_used: Same Llama models (13B, 70B, 405B) without SCAI RAG, i.e. native LLM using training knowledge alone
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on USMLE Step 1, 2 and 3 sample questions versus the answer key
evidence.effect: SCAI RAG significantly improved the 13B model on Steps 1 and 3, the 70B model on Step 2, and the 405B model on Step 3. The 13B model with RAG passed Step 3 (74 correct, 60.2%). 70B with RAG: 92.0% Step 1, 79.6% Step 2, 91.1% Step 3. 405B with RAG: 90.8% Step 1, 84.5% Step 2, 95.1% Step 3. The 70B and 405B models passed all steps with and without RAG.
evidence.quote: Significant improvements associated with SCAI RAG were found for the 13B model on Steps 1 and 3, the 70B model on Step 2, and the 405B parameter model on Step 3.

evidence.title: Curated retrieval-augmented generation for dental traumatology
evidence.comparator_used: Base model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) without the curated knowledge base, and eight commercial LLMs (and three frontier LLMs in Study 2) answering from their training knowledge alone
evidence.outcome: Modal accuracy on 99 binary dental traumatology questions; valid rationale rate; confabulated rationales; specialist rubric score
evidence.effect: Modal accuracy 96.0% (95% CI 90.1-98.4) vs best commercial comparator GPT-5.5 87.9% (paired difference +8.1 pp, 95% CI +2.9 to +14.9; p_Holm = 0.013). Valid rationale rate 49.5% to 98.0% for the base model with the knowledge base; confabulations 0 vs 21. Study 2: 82.1/92 vs Claude Opus 4.5 72.6 (+9.6 points, exact Wilcoxon p = 0.016), Gemini 2.5 Pro 60.3, GPT-4.1 50.4; all seven evaluators ranked DT-RAG first (Kendall's W = 0.97).
evidence.quote: The curated knowledge base elevated the base model from 49.5% to 98.0% valid rationale rate, eliminating confabulations in this evaluation (0 vs 21).

evidence.title: Adapting and Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Self-Management: A Divide and Conquer Framework
evidence.comparator_used: MLLMs without RAG (model knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Performance on the AIS domain knowledge assessment task
evidence.effect: RAG substantially improved models' performances; no numbers reported in the abstract
evidence.quote: Results showed varying effectiveness of visual prompting across different architectures, while RAG substantially improved models' performances on the knowledge assessment task.

evidence.title: Improving access to rare-disease knowledge: A retrieval-augmented question answering framework for Wilson's disease
evidence.comparator_used: LLMs answering without retrieval grounding (comparison implied in abstract; baseline not detailed)
evidence.outcome: biological accuracy and clinical relevance of answers to Wilson's disease questions
evidence.effect: Retrieval grounding substantially improves biological accuracy and clinical relevance; ~7B-parameter models perform competitively when paired with the retrieval pipeline (no numeric values in abstract)
evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that retrieval grounding substantially improves biological accuracy and clinical relevance, and that smaller, deployable language models (on the order of 7B parameters) can perform competitively when paired with a well-designed retrieval pipeline.

evidence.title: When Cases Get Rare: A Retrieval Benchmark for Off-Guideline Clinical Question Answering
evidence.comparator_used: Same models without retrieval (parametric knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Correct answers on OGCaReBench (free-form off-guideline clinical questions)
evidence.effect: Best baseline GPT-5.2 without retrieval answered 56% correctly; augmenting with retrieved medical articles improved performance up to 82% (using GPT-5.2)
evidence.quote: Augmenting models with retrieved medical articles improves this performance to up to 82% (using GPT-5.2) highlighting the importance of evidence-grounding for real-world medical reasoning tasks.

evidence.title: Custom Large Language Models Improve Accuracy: Comparing Retrieval Augmented Generation and Artificial Intelligence Agents to Noncustom Models for Evidence-Based Medicine
evidence.venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
evidence.comparator_used: Base (non-custom) LLMs without RAG, answering from training knowledge alone
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of answers to 100 questions based on the 2022 AAOS ACL guidelines, blindly rated by two fellowship-trained surgeons
evidence.effect: All noncustom models started below 60% accuracy; RAG improved every model by an average 39.7%; best RAG model was Llama3 70b at 94%
evidence.quote: Applying RAG improved the accuracy of every model by an average 39.7%.

evidence.title: Healthier LLMs: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Public Health Question Answering
evidence.comparator_used: LLMs used without retrieval (no retrieved context)
evidence.outcome: Multiple-choice accuracy on PubHealthBench
evidence.effect: Providing retrieved context substantially increases multiple-choice accuracy across a diverse set of LLMs, enabling smaller open-weight models to match or outperform larger models used without retrieval
evidence.quote: Providing retrieved context substantially increases multiple-choice accuracy across a diverse set of LLMs, enabling smaller open-weight models to match or outperform larger models used without retrieval, with gains primarily driven by retrieval quality and careful context selection.

evidence.title: Improving Health Literacy through Lay Summarization of Radiological Reports: An Evaluation of BioNER and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence.comparator_used: Standard LLM generation without retrieval (few-shot and fine-tuned Qwen and BioBART)
evidence.outcome: Quality, factual consistency and readability of lay summaries
evidence.effect: RAG alone offered no benefit; the abstract gives no numbers. Combining RAG with NER degraded performance in few-shot settings but improved readability when fine-tuned.
evidence.tradeoff: Irrelevant retrieved terms can introduce hallucinations.
evidence.quote: Results show that NER consistently improves readability and overall quality, while RAG alone offers no benefit and can introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms.

evidence.title: A Comparative Performance Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in Gynecologic Oncology
evidence.comparator_used: Non-RAG baseline (same LLM, DeepSeek-R1-0528, without retrieval)
evidence.outcome: Expert-graded response performance on cervical cancer management and gynecologic oncology surgery question sets
evidence.effect: RAG systems generally outperformed the non-RAG baseline; largest gains on complex surgical questions, modest and heterogeneous improvements on guideline-based cervical cancer management questions. No numeric values given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Across domains, RAG systems generally outperformed the non-RAG baseline.

evidence.title: An automatic consult reply system for therapeutic plasma exchange using retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.comparator_used: Three non-RAG GPT-series model configurations (conventional LLMs without retrieval of the 2023 ASFA guideline content)
evidence.outcome: Item-level accuracy for diagnosis, ASFA category, grade, insurance applicability, plasma volume and replacement fluid, plus reproducibility across repeated runs
evidence.effect: RAG configurations consistently outperformed non-RAG baselines across items, with the largest gains in plasma-volume calculation and ASFA classification; reproducibility was markedly higher with RAG across repeated runs (no numeric values given in the abstract)
evidence.quote: RAG configurations consistently outperformed non-RAG baselines across items, with the largest gains in plasma-volume calculation and ASFA classification.

evidence.title: Domain-Specific Knowledge Graphs in RAG-Enhanced Healthcare LLMs
evidence.comparator_used: No-RAG baseline (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on domain-specific probes across seven LLMs
evidence.effect: Scope-matched retrieval gave the most consistent gains, especially for smaller/mid-sized models, while larger models frequently matched or exceeded KG-RAG with No-RAG on Probe 1. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Broad or unioned retrieval sources can introduce distractors that reduce accuracy.
evidence.quote: Larger models frequently match or exceed KG-RAG with a No-RAG baseline on Probe 1, indicating strong parametric priors, whereas smaller/mid-sized models benefit more from well-scoped retrieval.

evidence.title: Dissecting Neuro-Symbolic Quality Assurance for Synthetic Oncology Data Generation
evidence.comparator_used: Same generators without retrieval augmentation
evidence.outcome: Gate compliance of generated synthetic records, per generator
evidence.effect: Improved gate compliance by 12.5 percentage points for one generator, had no measurable effect for a second, and collapsed output in a third.
evidence.tradeoff: Output collapse in one generator; the effect is strongly model-dependent, so retrieval needs per-model evaluation.
evidence.quote: Retrieval augmentation is strongly model-dependent: it improves gate compliance for one generator by 12.5 percentage points, has no measurable effect for a second, and collapses output in a third.

evidence.title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-3.5, GPT-4 (training knowledge alone) and Microsoft's Prometheus, on 19 DLBCL questions rated by eight reviewers
evidence.outcome: Reviewer-rated accuracy and relevance (3-point scale); hallucination frequency
evidence.effect: RAG model had higher average scores and the most top scores across questions on accuracy and relevance. GPT-4 was closer to RAG on relevance than on accuracy. GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 had more answers with hallucinations (non-existent references, inaccurate clinical answers) than the other LLMs. No numeric scores are given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: RAG did not lead on readability: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 had the highest readability scores.
evidence.quote: On accuracy and relevance, the RAG model outperformed other models with higher scores on average and the most top scores across questions.

evidence.title: Swedish Medical LLM Benchmark: development and evaluation of a framework for assessing large language models in the Swedish medical domain
evidence.comparator_used: LLMs without RAG (model knowledge alone), as implied by the abstract; the comparator is not explicitly described
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on clinical knowledge questions in the Swedish medical benchmark
evidence.effect: Improved accuracy for clinical knowledge questions; no numbers given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Hybrid systems incorporating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improved accuracy for clinical knowledge questions, highlighting promising directions for safe implementation.

evidence.title: RESPECT: a conversational AI system for informed consent with accuracy, safety, and stakeholder-centered evaluation
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-4 (LLM answering without RAG grounding in the consent documents)
evidence.outcome: Safety (appropriate refusal rate) and utility (answering legitimate questions), plotted as a Refusal-Utility Curve
evidence.effect: RESPECT had significantly higher appropriate refusal rates than GPT-4 but reduced utility; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Reduced utility in answering legitimate questions
evidence.quote: RESPECT demonstrated significantly higher appropriate refusal rates compared to GPT-4, but at the cost of reduced utility in answering legitimate questions.

evidence.title: Generative artificial intelligence and non-pharmacological bias: an experimental study on cancer patient sexual health communications
evidence.comparator_used: Bot1 (standard GPT-3.5 without retrieval) vs Bot2 (GPT-3.5 with retrieval from two clinical guidelines via DocsBot)
evidence.outcome: Proportion of responses recommending consultation vs pharmacological interventions for cancer survivors' sexual health questions
evidence.effect: Consultation was more prevalent than pharmacological interventions in both bots: OR 47.3 (p<0.001) in Bot1 and OR 97.2 (p<0.001) in Bot2; no direct statistical test between bots reported
evidence.tradeoff: Guideline retrieval did not correct the bias; guideline recommendations were not reflected in responses and the bias toward non-pharmacological advice persisted.
evidence.quote: Despite the lack of reflection on guideline recommendations, 'consultation' was significantly more prevalent in both bots' responses compared with pharmacological interventions, with ORs of 47.3 (p<0.001) in Bot1 and 97.2 (p<0.001) in Bot2.

evidence.title: A context-augmented large language model for accurate precision oncology medicine recommendations
evidence.comparator_used: LLM-only approach relying on the model's general knowledge, without retrieval from MOAlmanac
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of biomarker-driven treatment recommendations
evidence.effect: RAG-LLM achieved up to 95% accuracy on synthetic queries and 93% on real-world queries from practicing oncologists; the abstract gives no LLM-only figures
evidence.quote: Our RAG-LLM achieved up to 95% accuracy on synthetic queries and 93% on real-world queries collected from practicing oncologists.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Evidence-Based Clinical Question Answering
evidence.comparator_used: No retrieved context (model's own knowledge) on previously incorrect items; also compared gold-source abstract, top-3 semantically ranked PubMed abstracts, and random abstracts
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on previously incorrect items after retrieval-augmented prompting
evidence.effect: Gold-source abstract raised accuracy to 0.79; top 3 PubMed abstracts (ranked by semantic relevance) improved accuracy to 0.23; random abstracts reduced accuracy (0.10, within temperature variation). Effects mirrored in GPT-4o-mini.
evidence.tradeoff: Benefit depends on retrieval quality: top-3 retrieval gave only modest gains (0.23) compared with the gold abstract (0.79), and random abstracts lowered accuracy.
evidence.quote: When we incorporate retrieval-augmented prompting, providing the gold-source abstract raises accuracy on previously incorrect items to 0.79; providing top 3 PubMed abstracts (ranked by semantic relevance) improves accuracy to 0.23, while random abstracts reduce accuracy (0.10, within temperature variation).

evidence.title: Boosting GPT models for genomics analysis: generating trusted genetic variant annotations and interpretations through RAG and Fine-tuning
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-4o/GPT-4 without retrieval (training knowledge alone), and fine-tuning on variant annotation data
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of variant annotation and interpretation; factual knowledge injection (data volume, accuracy, cost-effectiveness)
evidence.effect: RAG integrated 190 million variant annotations into GPT-4o and gave accurate annotations; RAG outperformed fine-tuning in factual knowledge injection in terms of data volume, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness (no numeric accuracy figures in the abstract)
evidence.quote: Our project also revealed that RAG outperforms fine-tuning in factual knowledge injection in terms of data volume, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness.

evidence.title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Radiology Guidelines
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.comparator_used: Standalone LLM without retrieval (also compared with an enhanced iterative RAG system)
evidence.outcome: Factual accuracy, completeness and clinical usefulness of answers to 79 radiology guideline queries
evidence.effect: Enhanced RAG vs standalone LLM: factual accuracy 0.89 vs. 0.68; completeness 4.20 vs. 3.05 (5-point Likert); usefulness 3.99 vs. 3.09 (5-point Likert). Both RAG systems significantly outperformed the standalone LLM in all metrics.
evidence.tradeoff: Opportunities remain to improve retrieval accuracy and reduce hallucinations; further validation is needed before clinical deployment.
evidence.quote: Both RAG systems significantly outperformed the standalone LLM in all metrics, with the enhanced model achieving the highest scores: Factual accuracy (0.89 vs. 0.68), completeness (4.20 vs. 3.05 on a 5-point Likert scale), and usefulness (3.99 vs. 3.09 on a 5-point Likert scale).

evidence.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models and Prompt Engineering Strategies in Microsatellite Instability Cancers: Evaluation Study
evidence.comparator_used: Vanilla, chain-of-thought and reflection-of-thoughts prompting without retrieval (model's internal knowledge), across GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Claude Opus 4
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on MSI cancer benchmark questions (especially complex decision-making tasks), safety (fabrication vs refusal) and error composition
evidence.effect: RAG was the most effective intervention and significantly improved accuracy in complex decision-making tasks; it shifted safety from high-risk fabrications to safer refusals. No numeric values given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Introduced false refusals (safety-utility trade-off); the main bottleneck moved from knowledge deficits to retrieval failures, making retrieval precision and knowledge base quality critical.
evidence.quote: The integration of RAG proved to be the most effective intervention.

evidence.title: Facet-Level Tracing of Evidence Uncertainty and Hallucination in RAG
evidence.comparator_used: LLM-only generation without retrieval, compared with Strict RAG (exclusive reliance on retrieved evidence) and Soft RAG (retrieved evidence plus parametric knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Hallucination and retrieval-generation misalignment (relevant evidence retrieved but not correctly integrated), assessed at facet level across medical QA and HotpotQA
evidence.effect: No numeric effect in the abstract. Hallucinations remain common in RAG even when relevant documents are retrieved. Failures are attributed more to how evidence is integrated during generation than to retrieval accuracy.
evidence.tradeoff: New failure modes under RAG: evidence absence, evidence misalignment, and prior-driven overrides, where parametric knowledge overrides retrieved evidence. These remain hidden under answer-level evaluation.
evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that hallucinations in RAG systems are driven less by retrieval accuracy and more by how retrieved evidence is integrated during generation, with facet-level analysis exposing systematic evidence override and misalignment patterns that remain hidden under answer-level evaluation.

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models GPT-4o, llama 3.1, and qwen 2.5 for cancer genetic variant classification
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt-engineered LLM without retrieval (model knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of cancer genetic variant classification
evidence.effect: RAG further enhanced performance beyond prompt engineering; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Prompt engineering significantly improved accuracy, while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further enhanced performance.

evidence.title: Nursing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Retrieval augmented generation for nursing question answering with large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Conventional large language models (ChatGLM2-6B and LLaMA2-7B) answering without retrieval, relying on their own training knowledge
evidence.outcome: Semantic fidelity (ROUGE-L) and clinical correctness (accuracy) on 1,000 expert-verified nursing question-answer pairs
evidence.quote: For ChatGLM2-6B, ROUGE-L increased from (30.73 ± 1.48) % to (64.27 ± 0.27) %, and accuracy increased from (49.08 ± 0.92) % to (75.83 ± 0.35) %.

evidence.title: Impact of guideline-based prompting on the large language model performance in dental trauma management clinical decision-making
evidence.comparator_used: Same models answering without the uploaded guideline document (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Open-ended question score, guideline concordance, and multiple-choice accuracy on dental trauma questions
evidence.effect: OEQ median scores with guideline: DeepSeek 32, ChatGPT 30, Gemini 30; without guideline: 26, 20, 23 respectively. MCQ accuracy 100% for all models with guideline vs 81.2% to 100% without.
evidence.quote: Guideline-based prompting improved guideline concordance and overall performance, particularly for open-ended dental trauma questions.

evidence.title: Retrieval‑Augmented Clinical Question‑Answering System for Bariatric Surgery Built on the ASMBS Textbook: From Good to Great
evidence.comparator_used: Raw LLMs with no retrieval (training knowledge alone): GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4 and GPT-5
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on a 200-question bariatric surgery benchmark drawn from ASMBS textbook end-of-chapter questions
evidence.effect: GPT-5: 94.0% with RAG (188/200) vs 87.0% raw (+7.0 pp; +14 questions). GPT-4: 89.5% vs 81.0% (+8.5 pp; +13 questions). GPT-4o-mini: 84.5% vs 70.5% (+14.0 pp; +28 questions).
evidence.tradeoff: Errors remained: 12 incorrect GPT-5 + RAG answers showed evidence-level mismatch, polarity errors in EXCEPT-type questions, scope misinterpretation, and retrieval salience bias. Procedural technique and complications management stayed at 88.9% each. Cost and latency were not reported.
evidence.quote: Textbook-augmented RAG produced consistent and significant accuracy gains across all models.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Evidence-Informed Guidance on Cannabidiol Use in Older Adults
evidence.comparator_used: Standalone LLMs without retrieval (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Caution and guideline alignment of cannabidiol recommendations for older adults, across 64 scenarios and three automated evaluation strategies
evidence.effect: Retrieval-augmented models consistently produced more cautious and guideline-aligned recommendations than standalone models, with the ensemble retrieval approach performing best; no numeric effect sizes reported in the abstract
evidence.quote: Across three automated evaluation strategies, retrieval-augmented models consistently produced more cautious and guideline-aligned recommendations than standalone models, with the ensemble approach performing best.

evidence.title: TrialCode Agent: LLM-Assisted Clinical Code-Set Construction for Trial Emulation
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline pipeline (LLM without retrieval) compared with Hybrid biomedical RAG
evidence.outcome: Exact-code F1 against expert-built reference code sets
evidence.effect: Hybrid biomedical RAG improved aggregate F1 only for Qwen; GPT-5.5 RxNorm F1 rose from 0.320 to 0.909. Claude and GPT-5.5 had their best aggregate results with Baseline.
evidence.tradeoff: Retrieval did not consistently improve exact-code performance. Macro-averaged criterion-level gains came with lower micro-averaged aggregate performance.
evidence.quote: Hybrid biomedical RAG improved aggregate F1 only for Qwen but increased GPT-5.5 RxNorm F1 from 0.320 to 0.909.

evidence.title: Trustworthy agentic genomics through versioned skill libraries
evidence.comparator_used: Model reasoning from its own knowledge without retrieval (also contrasted with the executed skill)
evidence.outcome: Phenotype accuracy and lethal-class errors
evidence.effect: Retrieval raised phenotype accuracy but increased lethal-class errors; the abstract gives no numbers.
evidence.tradeoff: Retrieval increased lethal-class errors, a new safety failure mode.
evidence.quote: Letting the model reason was stochastic and unsafe, and grounding it in the correct guidelines by retrieval paradoxically increased lethal-class errors.

evidence.title: Rapidly Benchmarking Large Language Models for Diagnosing Comorbid Patients: Comparative Study Leveraging the LLM-as-a-Judge Method
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-4o 05-13 without RAG (no retrieved reference ranges from the American Board of Internal Medicine)
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic hit rate on MIMIC-IV admissions
evidence.effect: RAG improved the hit rate of GPT-4o 05-13 by an average of 0.8% (P<.006)
evidence.quote: Finally, RAG significantly improved the hit rate of GPT-4o 05-13 by an average of 0.8% (P<.006).

evidence.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Extract and Translate Medical Information in Doctors' Notes for Health Records and Diagnostic Billing Codes
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot and few-shot prompting without retrieval
evidence.outcome: Discovery of unseen codes and overall coding accuracy
evidence.effect: RAG enabled limited discovery of unseen codes but reduced overall accuracy; no numbers reported in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Frequently saturated context windows, reducing overall accuracy
evidence.quote: While RAG enabled limited discovery of unseen codes, it frequently saturated context windows, reducing overall accuracy.

evidence.title: Bridging the Knowledge-Action Gap by Evaluating LLMs in Dynamic Dental Clinical Scenarios
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLMs without RAG (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Hallucinations in static tasks and performance in dynamic multi-turn clinical workflows
evidence.effect: RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks; efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation (no numbers given in the abstract)
evidence.tradeoff: In dynamic workflows RAG sometimes degraded performance; external knowledge alone could not bridge the reasoning gap without domain-adaptive pre-training
evidence.quote: While RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks, its efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence reliability in implant dentistry: A comparative analysis of clinical accuracy and hallucination patterns across multiple language models
evidence.comparator_used: Conventional LLMs without retrieval (GPT-4o, Model 4.1, Model 4.5) answering the same 15 implant dentistry questions
evidence.outcome: Clinical accuracy and fabrication of references and statistics
evidence.effect: ScholarQA and OpenEvidence: 80.0% accuracy with 0% fabrication. GPT-4o: 82% reference fabrication and 85.7% statistical fabrication. Unprompted GPT-4o accuracy was 33.3%.
evidence.tradeoff: RAG systems avoided fabricated references but still generated incorrect interpretations. They gained little from evidence-based prompting: OpenEvidence rose to 86.6% and ScholarQA fell to 73.3%.
evidence.quote: ScholarQA and OpenEvidence both achieved high accuracy (80.0%) with 0% fabrication, while GPT-4o showed high rates of reference (82%) and statistical (85.7%) fabrication.

evidence.title: A Systematic Study of Retrieval Pipeline Design for Retrieval-Augmented Medical Question Answering
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot LLM without retrieval (parametric knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Zero-shot medical question answering accuracy on MedQA USMLE
evidence.effect: Retrieval augmentation significantly improved zero-shot performance; best configuration (dense retrieval with query reformulation and reranking) reached 60.49% accuracy
evidence.tradeoff: A clear tradeoff between retrieval effectiveness and computational cost; simpler dense retrieval configurations gave strong performance with higher throughput
evidence.quote: Results show that retrieval augmentation significantly improves zero-shot medical question answering performance.

evidence.title: CARE-RAG - Clinical Assessment and Reasoning in RAG
evidence.comparator_used: Not stated in the abstract; the study evaluates model responses when authoritative WET guideline passages are provided, with no explicit no-retrieval arm described
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, consistency and fidelity of reasoning on clinician-vetted WET guideline questions
evidence.effect: No numbers reported in the abstract; errors persist even when authoritative passages are provided, while RAG can constrain outputs
evidence.tradeoff: Retrieving the right evidence does not guarantee correct reasoning, so safe deployment requires assessing reasoning as rigorously as retrieval
evidence.quote: In evaluating model responses to curated clinician-vetted questions, we find that errors persist even when authoritative passages are provided.

evidence.title: Cardiology knowledge assessment of retrieval-augmented open versus proprietary large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Same 14 LLMs answering without RAG (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy (percent correct) on 449 ACCSAP cardiology board-style multiple-choice questions
evidence.effect: All models improved after RAG using a 123-document guideline and textbook knowledge base; e.g., Mistral Large 2 reached 78.0% (95% CI: 73.9-81.5) with RAG, comparable to GPT 4o. RAG was reported as particularly beneficial for smaller models.
evidence.quote: After RAG, all models improved, and open-weight models like Mistral Large 2 (78.0%, 95% CI: 73.9-81.5) performed comparably to proprietary alternatives like GPT 4o.

evidence.title: Retrieval-augmented Claude Opus 4.7 and generative pretrained transformer 5.5 surpass human performance on the nuclear cardiology board preparation exam (and Claude drafts a paper about it)
evidence.venue: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
evidence.comparator_used: Prior published results for GPT-4o without domain context (63.1%); a different, older model, so not a same-model comparison
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on the 168-question 2023 ASNC Board Preparation Exam
evidence.effect: Claude Opus 4.7 with RAG 86.3% ± 1.4% (text 88.8%, image 73.3%); GPT-5.5 with RAG 86.7% ± 2.2% (text 88.5%, image 77.0%); vs GPT-4o without context 63.1%, a 23-percentage-point improvement; both exceeded the human FIT mean of 78.0%
evidence.tradeoff: GPT-5.5 refused a mean of 12.2 questions (7.3%) per iteration due to safety filters. The gain also reflects the model upgrade over 18 months, so RAG is not isolated from model generation.
evidence.quote: Compared to GPT-4o without context (63.1%), this represents a 23-percentage-point improvement in 18 months.

evidence.title: From RAGs to riches: Utilizing large language models to write documents for clinical trials
evidence.comparator_used: Off-the-shelf large language model without retrieval augmentation (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Quality of generated clinical trial protocol sections across four dimensions (clinical thinking and logic; transparency and references; medical terminology; content relevance)
evidence.effect: Off-the-shelf LLM scored ≈40% or less on clinical thinking and logic and on transparency and references; with RAG these scores increased to ≈80%. Off-the-shelf LLM scored over 80% on content relevance and terminology.
evidence.quote: The use of retrieval-augmented generation substantially improves the writing quality of the large language model, with clinical thinking and logic and transparency and references scores increasing to ≈80%.

evidence.title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
evidence.comparator_used: No grounding (ungrounded prompt) in the fully crossed design
evidence.outcome: Medical sycophancy (model abandoning or accepting a false claim under user pressure)
evidence.effect: Grounding reduced sycophancy but did not eliminate it; no numeric effect size given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Grounding helps, but does not eliminate the behavior.

evidence.title: Advancing Question-Answering in Ophthalmology With Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Benchmarking Open-Source and Proprietary Large Language Models
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot and zero-shot with Chain-of-Thought prompting (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on ophthalmology multiple-choice questions (BCSC and OphthoQuestions)
evidence.effect: GPT-4-turbo accuracy increased by 11.54% on BCSC and by 10.96% on OphthoQuestions; overall improvement of Llama-3 by 23.85%, Gemma-2 by 17.11%, and Mixtral-8 × 7B by 22.11%
evidence.quote: Using RAG, GPT-4-turbo's accuracy increased by 11.54% on BCSC and by 10.96% on OphthoQuestions.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for solving pediatric clinical cases: A Retrieval-Augmented approach utilizing Llama3.2 and structured references
evidence.comparator_used: Standalone Llama3.2 without retrieval (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on 1,713 multiple-choice pediatric clinical questions (MedQA and ADC-Education and Practice)
evidence.effect: 67.78% (1,161/1,713) with RAG vs 46.18% (791/1,713) standalone; p = 1.5e-112; improvement consistent across all pediatric subspecialties
evidence.quote: The RAG-integrated system significantly outperformed standalone Llama3.2, achieving an overall accuracy of 67.78 % (1,161/1,713) compared to 46.18 % (791/1,713) for Llama3.2 alone (p = 1.5e-112).

evidence.title: Deterministic Retrieval-Grounded Language Models for Clinical Counseling: Large-Scale Multilingual Evaluation with Cryptographically Verifiable Pipelines
evidence.comparator_used: Ablated system without retrieval grounding (no retrieved context supplied to the LLM)
evidence.outcome: Clinical fidelity (and overall performance) in counseling responses
evidence.effect: Retrieval grounding contributed significantly to overall performance and was the main driver of clinical fidelity; ablation numbers not given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Ablation experiments demonstrate that retrieval grounding and deterministic safety routing each contribute significantly to overall performance, with the former driving clinical fidelity and the latter driving safety.

evidence.title: Feasibility of retrieval-augmented generation for large language models with Japanese input in radiotherapy
evidence.comparator_used: ChatGPT-4o without Rad-Hub (training knowledge alone, no retrieval)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on multiple-choice questions in three Japanese radiotherapy certification examinations (Medical Physicist, Radiologist, Radiation Oncologist)
evidence.effect: Medical Physicist: 77.0% ± 2.6% to 84.6% ± 1.5%; Radiologist: 74.9% ± 2.0% to 82.1% ± 1.1%; Radiation Oncologist: 55.6% ± 4.4% to 71.7% ± 4.5%; gains ranged from 7.2% to 16.1%
evidence.quote: Accuracy increased from 77.0% ± 2.6% to 84.6% ± 1.5% in the Medical Physicist examination, from 74.9% ± 2.0% to 82.1% ± 1.1% in the Radiologist examination, and from 55.6% ± 4.4% to 71.7% ± 4.5% in the Radiation Oncologist examination.

evidence.title: The Potential Clinical Utility of the Customized Large Language Model in Gastroenterology: A Pilot Study
evidence.comparator_used: Conventional GPT-4o (described as capable of retrieval-augmented generation) without the customized BM25 document retrieval
evidence.outcome: Number of correctly answered clinical questions (15-question Korean gastroenterology benchmark)
evidence.effect: Customized GPT with BM25 retrieval over textbooks answered 8/15 correctly (10/15 after English terminology replacement); conventional GPT-4o scored 14/15; fellow 10/15; expert 15/15
evidence.tradeoff: Judgment-based questions remained a challenge for the customized model; performance depended on Korean vs English terminology in the retrieved documents/questions
evidence.quote: Conventional GPT-4o achieved the highest score among the AI models (14/15).

evidence.title: TurkishMedLLM: A Source-Grounded and Safety-Aware Turkish Medical LLM for Clinical Decision Support and Digital Health Applications
evidence.comparator_used: Base LLM without retrieval and fine-tuned non-RAG configuration
evidence.outcome: Generation quality: RAGAS faithfulness, response relevancy, DeepEval answer relevancy, clinical caution score
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned RAG: faithfulness 0.91, response relevancy 0.88, DeepEval answer relevancy 0.90, clinical caution 0.93; reported as outperforming base LLM and fine-tuned non-RAG (comparator scores not given in abstract)
evidence.quote: In generation-stage evaluation, the fine-tuned RAG configuration achieved a RAGAS faithfulness score of 0.91, response relevancy of 0.88, DeepEval answer relevancy of 0.90, and clinical caution score of 0.93, outperforming the base LLM, base RAG, and fine-tuned non-RAG configurations.

evidence.title: Towards Evaluating the Diagnostic Ability of LLMs
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLMs without RAG (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Rate of missed ground truth conditions that were clearly inferable from the available data (top-performing models GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.5)
evidence.effect: Error rate improved from 0.5% to 0.2% with RAG
evidence.quote: We found that GPT-4o from OpenAI and Claude Sonnet 3.5 from Anthropic were the top performers with them only missing 0.5% of ground truth conditions that were clearly inferable from the available data; RAG further improved this error rate to 0.2%.

evidence.title: Zero-Shot Large Language Models for Long Clinical Text Summarization with Temporal Reasoning
evidence.comparator_used: Base open-source LLMs without retrieval (zero-shot, long-context input)
evidence.outcome: Hallucination and clinical reasoning limitations (temporal progression, rare disease prediction) in long clinical text summarization and diagnosis prediction
evidence.effect: RAG variants showed improvements in hallucination in some cases but did not fully address the limitations; no numeric results in the abstract
evidence.quote: While RAG shows improvements in hallucination in some cases, it does not fully address these limitations.

evidence.title: Can Small Open-Source Language Models With Retrieval-Augmented Generation Match GPT-4 Performance in Breast Cancer Clinical Decision Support?
evidence.comparator_used: Same five LLMs (GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo, Qwen2.5-14B, LLaMA3-8B, OpenBioLLM-8B) without RAG
evidence.outcome: Quality of answers to breast cancer guideline queries (rubric scores and pairwise ranking win rates), with human oncologist validation
evidence.effect: Absolute rubric gains 0.02-0.05 on a five-point scale; relative improvements in head-to-head win rates 16% to 46%; RAG-enhanced Qwen2.5-14B rubric 3.77 vs 3.96 for GPT-4-turbo and pairwise 0.72 vs 0.81
evidence.tradeoff: Absolute rubric gains were modest; human expert scores were more conservative than LLM judge scores (mean 3.81 vs 4.12); performance degraded sharply at higher context volumes
evidence.quote: Human expert scores confirmed RAG superiority but were consistently more conservative than LLM judge scores (mean 3.81 v 4.12 across all metrics).

evidence.title: Domain Fine-Tuning vs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Multiple-Choice Question Answering: A Controlled Comparison at the 4B-Parameter Scale
evidence.comparator_used: No retrieval (model's weight knowledge alone) vs. retrieved MedMCQA explanation passages inserted into the prompt, in both Gemma 3 4B and MedGemma 4B
evidence.outcome: Majority-vote accuracy on MedQA-USMLE 4-option test split
evidence.effect: No statistically significant gain in either model; in the domain-tuned model the point estimate was -1.9 pp (p = 0.16)
evidence.quote: RAG over MedMCQA explanations does not produce a statistically significant gain in either model, and in the domain-tuned model the point estimate is slightly negative (-1.9 pp, p = 0.16).

evidence.title: Development and evaluation of an agentic LLM based RAG framework for evidence-based patient education
evidence.comparator_used: Base LLM without retrieval (base and base+prompt engineering setups)
evidence.outcome: Arabic patient education material generation quality (accuracy, readability, comprehensiveness, appropriateness, safety)
evidence.effect: ARAG-enabled setups yielded the best generation performance for 10/12 LLMs; AceGPT-v2-32B with ARAG and prompt engineering was the highest-performing setup
evidence.tradeoff: Context limits impacted large-context models
evidence.quote: ARAG-enabled setups yielded the best generation performance for 10/12 LLMs.

evidence.title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Framework for Ophthalmology
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLM without the retrieved ophthalmic knowledge base (training knowledge alone); GPT-4 also benchmarked
evidence.outcome: Human ranking score and scientific consensus on 300 ophthalmology clinical questions
evidence.effect: Human ranking score 0.60 vs 0.48 baseline (difference 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.22; P = .02); scientific consensus 84.0% vs 46.5% (difference 37.5%; 95% CI, 29.0%-46.0%; P < .001). Not different from GPT-4: 0.61 (P = .89) and 79.2% (P = .06).
evidence.quote: The retrieval-augmented LLM had a score of 0.60, a difference of 0.12 (95% CI, 0.02-0.22; P = .02) from baseline and not different from GPT-4 with a score of 0.61 (difference = 0.01; 95% CI, -0.11 to 0.13; P = .89).

evidence.title: Agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning reshapes collective reliability under model variability in radiology question answering
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot inference without retrieved evidence (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Cross-model decision dispersion (entropy), robustness of correctness across models, and majority consensus on 169 radiology questions across 34 LLMs
evidence.effect: Median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13; mean robustness of correctness 0.74 vs. 0.81; majority consensus increased overall (P<0.001)
evidence.tradeoff: High agreement did not guarantee correctness; 572 incorrect outputs, 72% rated moderate or high clinical severity (inter-rater kappa=0.02)
evidence.quote: Agentic inference reduced inter-model decision dispersion (median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13) and increased robustness of correctness across models (mean 0.74 vs. 0.81).

evidence.title: RAG-Enhanced Open SLMs for Hypertension Management Chatbots
evidence.comparator_used: Same small language models without RAG (model training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Response clarity and content accuracy in hypertension QA, measured by reference metrics and expert evaluation
evidence.effect: RAG-enhanced SLMs can improve response clarity and content accuracy; newer SLMs like Qwen3 performed strongly even without RAG. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Our findings suggest that RAG-enhanced SLMs can improve response clarity and content accuracy.

evidence.title: TSWAP: A Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Thai Wellness Advisor
evidence.comparator_used: Same backend model family without the knowledge base (no-retrieval probe, 71 questions)
evidence.outcome: Verifiable provider recommendations
evidence.effect: Without the knowledge base the model produced zero verifiable provider recommendations
evidence.quote: without the safety prompt the backend model family produced a full drug-dosing schedule and complied with out-of-scope requests, and without the knowledge base it produced zero verifiable provider recommendations

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models on the Acute Coronary Syndrome Guidelines Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek R1) without RAG, relying on training knowledge alone
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on 38 open-ended ACS guideline-based questions, scored against guideline recommendations with an AI similarity score tool
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o 71.1% without RAG vs 92.1% with RAG (P = 0.017); DeepSeek R1 78.9% without RAG vs 94.7% with RAG (no P value reported for this pair). RAG disproportionately improved lower-scoring questions in DeepSeek R1 and improved scores more evenly in ChatGPT-4o.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o without RAG achieved 71.1% accuracy (95% CI: 55.2%-83.0%), which significantly improved with RAG (P = 0.017).

evidence.title: Performance of Enhanced Large Language Models on Prosthodontic Multiple-Choice Questions
evidence.comparator_used: Base OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1 without enhancement (RAG, ICL and majority voting were tested only as a combined package)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on prosthodontic multiple-choice questions (Chinese C-MCQs and English E-MCQs)
evidence.effect: C-MCQs: significant accuracy improvement for both enhanced models (P < .001). E-MCQs: higher accuracy but not statistically significant (P = .145). Knowledge-based errors in C-MCQs were significantly reduced (P < .008) but only non-significantly reduced in E-MCQs (P = .604).
evidence.quote: Enhanced versions of both DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI o1 achieved significant accuracy improvement compared with their base versions in Chinese-language multiple-choice questions (C-MCQs) (P < .001).

evidence.title: Guideline-anchored retrieval-augmented generation outperforms baseline and literature-only configurations in gynecologic oncology decision support: A pre-integration benchmark
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline GPT-5 without retrieval (training knowledge alone); OpenEvidence literature-anchored clinical AI also compared
evidence.outcome: Modified Generative Performance Score (mGPS; guideline concordance plus hallucination penalty) on 50 gynecologic oncology cases, scored by three gynecologic oncologists
evidence.effect: mGPS 0.83 (SD 0.26) for NCCN-anchored GPT-RAG vs 0.65 (SD 0.31) for baseline GPT-5 (W = 189.5, Z = -3.42, P < .001, r = 0.49) and 0.70 (SD 0.27) for OpenEvidence (W = 254.0, Z = -2.64, P = .008); mixed-effects OR 3.74 (95% CI 1.57-8.90) for GPT-RAG
evidence.quote: GPT-RAG exceeded baseline (W = 189.5, Z = -3.42, P < .001, r = 0.49) and OpenEvidence (W = 254.0, Z = -2.64, P = .008); OpenEvidence and baseline did not differ (P = .22).

evidence.title: Comparison of Large Language Models' Performance on 600 Nuclear Medicine Technology Board Examination-Style Questions
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLMs without RAG (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Overall accuracy on 600 nuclear medicine technology board-style questions across 15 topics
evidence.effect: With RAG, overall accuracy was 0.787 (openai_nvidia_gpt-4o_final), 0.783 (openai_mxbai_gpt-4o_final), 0.773 (Anthropic Opus) and 0.750 (Google Gemini 1.5 Pro); the Llama3 ollama_llama3 model without RAG had the lowest accuracy. The abstract gives no matched without-RAG scores.
evidence.quote: This study also demonstrates that adding a RAG workflow can increase the accuracy of an off-the-shelf model.

evidence.title: A Self-Controlled Benchmark of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models on Clinical Guideline Questions
evidence.comparator_used: Same base LLMs queried without guideline access (paired within-model design); also standard LLMs vs RAG-enhanced Custom GPT
evidence.outcome: Accuracy (condition-blind LLM judge and human ratings) and content-level hallucination rate on German S3 oral cavity carcinoma guideline questions
evidence.effect: Judge: hallucination fell from 42% to 4%; pooled accuracy +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); +0.48 (95% CI 0.22-0.73) after length adjustment; human ratings +0.61 (95% CI 0.49-0.74). Citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89%; retrieval recall@5 92%. Accuracy gain significant in Mistral, Qwen3 and GPT-OSS, directional in DeepSeek and GPT-5.
evidence.tradeoff: Accuracy gains were small or non-significant for already-strong base models; residual hallucination still requires human oversight; experts could identify retrieval-augmented answers with 98.5% accuracy, compromising blinding of human raters.
evidence.quote: On the judge, content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4% and accuracy rose by a pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); the accuracy gain persisted after adjustment for response length (+0.48, 95% CI 0.22-0.73), which retrieval shortened rather than lengthened.

evidence.title: MRAG: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Bio-medicine
evidence.comparator_used: LLMs without retrieval augmentation (no RAG), i.e. the model's own knowledge
evidence.outcome: LLM reliability across MRAG benchmark tasks (English and Chinese medical QA, corpus of Wikipedia and PubMed)
evidence.effect: RAG enhances LLM reliability across MRAG tasks; RAG also improves usefulness and reasoning quality for long-form questions (no numeric values given in the abstract)
evidence.tradeoff: LLM responses may become slightly less readable for long-form questions with RAG.
evidence.quote: (a) RAG enhances LLM reliability across MRAG tasks.

evidence.title: Evaluation of LLMs accuracy and consistency in the registered dietitian exam through prompt engineering and knowledge retrieval
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot, CoT and CoT-SC prompting without retrieval
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on Registered Dietitian exam questions by proficiency level
evidence.effect: RAP was particularly effective for GPT-4o on Expert level questions; overall, GPT-4o with CoT-SC outperformed the other approaches, including RAP; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: RAP was particularly effective for GPT-4o to answer Expert level questions.

evidence.title: Guideline-augmented large language models for contraindication screening in interventional spine care
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLM classification without retrieval (training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of contraindication classification (no contraindication, relative, absolute) across three LLMs; weighted kappa; relative contraindication detection
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 85.8%-87.1% at baseline to 92.5%-98.4% with RAG (all p < 0.05). Weighted kappa rose from 0.885-0.913 to 0.949-0.990. Relative contraindication detection rose from 42.1%-56.1% to 59.6%-93.0%. Absolute contraindication safety catch rates stayed at 99.0%-100.0% in all conditions.
evidence.quote: Baseline accuracy ranged from 85.8% to 87.1% across models and improved to 92.5% to 98.4% with RAG (all p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Natural Language Processing and Large Language Model-Based Automated AO/OTA Classification of Proximal Femoral Fractures: A MIMIC-IV Retrospective Study
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot prompting without retrieval (model's training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and F1 for AO/OTA 31A vs 31B classification on a balanced test set of 70 cases
evidence.effect: RAG-LLM accuracy 94.29% (F1 = 94.29%) vs zero-shot accuracy 94.29% (F1 = 94.28%)
evidence.quote: The comparable performance between zero‑shot and RAG models suggests that modern LLMs already possess inherent knowledge of AO/OTA classification, though RAG may offer advantages in more nuanced tasks.

evidence.title: Optimising the clinical application of rheumatology guidelines using large language models: a retrieval-augmented generation framework integrating EULAR and ACR recommendations
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLM (ChatGPT-o3-mini) without context retrieval (baseline, training knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Answer quality (relevance, factual accuracy, safety, completeness, conciseness) and preference between RAG and baseline responses
evidence.effect: LLM-as-a-judge: RAG significantly outperformed baseline across all criteria (P < .001); RAG preferred in 92.8% of comparisons by the LLM judge and 71.2% to 74.8% by human evaluators (P < .001); manual evaluation confirmed significance for accuracy, safety, and completeness (P < .001)
evidence.quote: The LLM-as-a-judge evaluation showed the RAG system significantly outperformed the baseline across all criteria (P < .001).

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in the Classification of Inborn Errors of Immunity
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLMs without retrieval/data augmentation
evidence.outcome: IEI classification F1 score across all models
evidence.effect: Retrieval strategies improved average F1 across all models (specific values not given in the text; shown as formula placeholders)
evidence.quote: The results also showed that retrieval strategies improved the average classification performance, increasing the F1 score from [Formula: see text] to [Formula: see text] across all models.

evidence.title: Safety and accuracy follow different scaling laws in clinical large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Closed-book prompting (zero-shot) with no supplied evidence
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, high-risk error, evidence contradiction and dangerous overconfidence across 34 local LLMs on RadSaFE-200
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 73.5% to 94.1%; high-risk error 12.0% to 2.6%; contradiction 12.7% to 2.3%; dangerous overconfidence 8.0% to 1.6%
evidence.tradeoff: The benefit came from clinician-defined clean evidence. Standard RAG and agentic RAG did not reproduce this safety profile.
evidence.quote: Clean evidence produced the strongest improvement, increasing mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1%, while reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6%, contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%, and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.

evidence.title: Enhancing Large Language Models for Improved Accuracy and Safety in Medical Question Answering: Comparative Study
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Vicuna-13B, ChatGLM-6B) answering without Med-RISE retrieval augmentation. Med-RISE is a bundled package of query rewriting, local and real-time retrieval, summarization and a fact and safety filter, so the effect is not isolated to retrieval.
evidence.outcome: Answer accuracy and hallucination rate on MedQA, PubMedQA, MedMCQA and EYE500
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved by 9.8% to 16.3% (mean 13%, SD 2.3%): GPT-3.5 16.3%, GPT-4 12.9%, Vicuna-13B 13%, ChatGLM-6B 9.8%. Hallucinations fell by 11.8% to 18% (mean 15.1%, SD 2.8%): factuality hallucinations down 13.5%, faithfulness hallucinations down 5.8%.
evidence.quote: The integration of Med-RISE with each LLM led to a substantial increase in accuracy, with improvements ranging from 9.8% to 16.3% (mean 13%, SD 2.3%) across the 4 datasets.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Readability Classification: A Variability Analysis of Sources and Metrics
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLM responses without grounding (model's own knowledge) versus a Wikipedia-grounded condition
evidence.outcome: Readability classification of LLM outputs across systems and metrics, in English and Portuguese
evidence.effect: 1,120 data points from seven systems, five readability metrics. Systems were statistically homogeneous at baseline but significantly heterogeneous under Wikipedia grounding. Metric variability was significant in all conditions. No overall direction of readability change or numeric effect size is given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Grounding on a verified source produced inconsistent readability across systems, so readability was not reliably preserved or improved. The metrics are not interchangeable, so the apparent effect depends on which metric is used.
evidence.quote: Although retrieval grounding is commonly used to improve accuracy, our findings show a trade-off: verified-source grounding can yield inconsistent readability.

evidence.title: Performance of latest AI models, RAG, and MCP on lung cancer-related questions
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLMs (Qwen3, GPT-4.1, Grok-3) answering without RAG
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on lung cancer guideline questions (50 questions)
evidence.effect: RAG significantly improved accuracy, with statistical differences versus baseline LLMs. Baseline accuracy was GPT 48%, Grok 44%, Qwen 40%. The abstract does not give RAG accuracy figures.
evidence.quote: However, implementing RAG (LLM-RAG) or MCP (LLM-MCP) significantly improved accuracy, with statistical differences observed between baseline LLMs and their RAG- or MCP-enhanced counterparts.

evidence.title: Compliance and factuality of large language models for clinical research document generation
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLMs such as GPT-4o generating ICFs from trial protocols without the retrieval-augmented, human-in-the-loop pipeline
evidence.outcome: Regulatory compliance and factual accuracy of LLM-generated informed consent forms
evidence.effect: Baseline GPT-4o reached 70%-80% compliance with factual errors in 18%-43% of cases; InformGen reached nearly 100% regulatory compliance and over 90% factual accuracy
evidence.quote: In contrast, InformGen substantially improved outputs, achieving nearly 100% regulatory compliance and over 90% factual accuracy, as validated by 5 domain-expert annotators.

evidence.title: Locally-deployed vs. cloud-based AI in healthcare: evaluating DeepSeek-R1:8b, DeepSeek-R1, and ChatGPT o3-mini-high for complex medical diagnostics
evidence.comparator_used: Same models without knowledge-base augmentation (DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-R1:8b, ChatGPT o3-mini-high alone)
evidence.outcome: MedQA diagnostic accuracy (1,000 questions)
evidence.effect: For DeepSeek-R1, knowledge-base augmentation significantly reduced accuracy by 4.36% (p=0.0002); no significant benefit was observed for the other models.
evidence.tradeoff: No consistent accuracy gain, and one model (DeepSeek-R1) lost accuracy with augmentation.
evidence.quote: Knowledge-base augmentation did not consistently improve performance; for DeepSeek-R1, it significantly reduced accuracy by 4.36% ( p=0.0002 ), while no significant benefit was observed for the other models.

evidence.title: Retrieval-augmented generation enhances large language model performance on the Japanese orthopedic board examination
evidence.venue: Journal of orthopaedic science : official journal of the Japanese Orthopaedic Association
evidence.comparator_used: Same models (GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, o1-preview) without RAG, relying on training knowledge alone
evidence.outcome: Overall accuracy on the 2024 Japanese Orthopedic Specialist Examination
evidence.effect: GPT-3.5 Turbo 29% without RAG vs 28% with RAG; GPT-4o 62% to 72%; o1-preview 67% to 84%
evidence.tradeoff: GPT-3.5 Turbo mainly failed to apply the retrieved data. GPT-4o and o1-preview still erred when the database lacked relevant information or on image-based questions.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o rose from 62 % to 72 %, while o1-preview increased from 67 % to 84 %.

evidence.title: Automated Prediction of Radiological Protocols Using Retrieval Augmented Generation
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.comparator_used: Fine-tuned Llama 3.2 3B without retrieval augmentation (non-RAG), site-specific models
evidence.outcome: Macro F1 and weighted F1 for radiological protocol classification across three Mayo Clinic sites
evidence.effect: RAG improved macro F1 at Arizona (Δ=0.0306, p=0.0074) and Florida (Δ=0.0245, p=0.0217) with equivalent weighted F1; at Rochester there was no macro F1 improvement and weighted F1 was significantly degraded (Δ=-0.0180, p=1.0000).
evidence.tradeoff: Site-specific heterogeneity, so site-specific tuning may be necessary. RAG also introduced an abstention mechanism with low baseline rates (1-2.5%).
evidence.quote: Paired bootstrap analyses revealed that RAG improved macro F1 at two of three sites (Arizona:: Δ =0.0306, p=0.0074; Florida: Δ =0.0245, p=0.0217) while maintaining equivalent weighted F1.

evidence.title: Performance of GPT-4o combined with retrieval-augmented generation on nutritionist licensing exam questions
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-4o without retrieval (training knowledge alone), plus GPT-4o-mini
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and response consistency on 599 Japanese registered dietitian exam questions, each answered five times
evidence.effect: Accuracy 83.5% ± 0.3% (GPT-4o-RAG) vs 82.1% ± 1.0% (GPT-4o), p = 0.12, not significant; response consistency 97.3% vs 91.2-95.2%, p < 0.001; variance significantly lower with RAG
evidence.tradeoff: GPT-4o-RAG showed limited performance on numerical questions; incorrect answers were more often associated with numerical terms. No cost or latency was reported.
evidence.quote: While the accuracy improvement of GPT-4o-RAG over GPT-4o was not statistically significant (p = 0.12), it exhibited significantly lower variance and higher response consistency (97.3% vs. 91.2-95.2%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Does Domain-Specific Retrieval Augmented Generation Help LLMs Answer Consumer Health Questions?
evidence.comparator_used: Vanilla LLMs answering from training knowledge alone, with no retrieval, across four open-source LLMs on the NIDDK portion of MedQuAD
evidence.outcome: Quality of answers to consumer health questions (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, LLM-based evaluation and clinical validation)
evidence.effect: Vanilla LLMs consistently outperformed RAG variants on quantitative metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) and qualitative assessments; retrieval Precision@5 = 0.15. RAG was competitive in scientific consensus and harm reduction.
evidence.tradeoff: Low retrieval precision (Precision@5 = 0.15) meant RAG did not help. The authors conclude that simple retrieval and prompt engineering are not enough and that medical-specific RAG infrastructure is needed.
evidence.quote: Surprisingly, we find that vanilla LLM approaches consistently outperform RAG variants across both quantitative metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) and qualitative assessments.

evidence.title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering
evidence.comparator_used: Vanilla prompting (no retrieval)
evidence.outcome: Average accuracy on the retrospective case-based question set
evidence.effect: DocRAG 62.47% vs Vanilla 52.67%
evidence.quote: On the retrospective case-based question set, GraphRAG also showed the strongest overall performance, with an average accuracy of 71.12%, compared with 62.47% for DocRAG, 54.20% for CoT, 52.67% for Vanilla, and 52.54% for RoT.

evidence.title: MedMeta: A Benchmark for LLMs in Synthesizing Meta-Analysis Conclusion from Medical Studies
evidence.comparator_used: Parametric-only approach relying on the model's internal knowledge (no retrieved abstracts)
evidence.outcome: Quality of meta-analysis conclusions generated by LLMs (LLM-as-a-judge score, 1-5 scale)
evidence.effect: Golden-RAG consistently and significantly outperformed Parametric-only across models; even under ideal RAG conditions performance was only ~2.7/5.0
evidence.tradeoff: New failure mode: in stress tests all models failed to identify and reject negated evidence, a vulnerability in RAG systems. The RAG condition used ground-truth (golden) abstracts.
evidence.quote: Our findings underscore the critical importance of information grounding: the Golden-RAG workflow consistently and significantly outperforms the Parametric-only approach across models.

evidence.title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 general LLMs without domain-specific retrieval (DocOA combines RAG with instructional prompts, so the effect of RAG is not isolated)
evidence.outcome: Performance in the osteoarthritis domain, including personalized treatment recommendations, on objective and human evaluations
evidence.effect: DocOA showed 'significant improvements' over GPT-3.5 and GPT-4; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: However, DocOA showed significant improvements.

evidence.title: Improving electronic health record processing of large language models via retrieval-augmented generation: A case study on dietary supplements
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.comparator_used: LLMs without retrieval (model knowledge alone)
evidence.outcome: Dietary supplement information extraction from EHRs (entity recognition, triple extraction, usage classification)
evidence.effect: RAG enhances LLM performance on DS information extraction; task-aligned retrieval outperforms reliance on model size or specialization (no numeric values in the abstract)
evidence.quote: We demonstrate that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances LLMs for dietary supplement (DS) information extraction.

evidence.title: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation versus long-context input for clinical reasoning over electronic health records
