evidence.title: Human-AI collectives most accurately diagnose clinical vignettes
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
evidence.comparator_used: single LLMs and LLM ensembles (AI output alone), and also single physicians and physician collectives
evidence.outcome: accuracy of open-ended differential diagnosis on text-based case vignettes
evidence.effect: Hybrid collectives of physicians and LLMs outperformed single LLMs and LLM ensembles; the abstract gives no numeric effect sizes. The result held across medical specialties and levels of professional experience.
evidence.quote: We show that hybrid collectives of physicians and LLMs outperform both single physicians and physician collectives, as well as single LLMs and LLM ensembles.

controls.question: Should we have several role-specialised LLM agents debate to consensus before a clinical decision, rather than relying on one model?
controls.control: Use multiple role-specialised LLM agents that debate or deliberate to consensus before producing a diagnosis, plan, or allocation.
controls.comparator: Single LLM agent answering in one pass
controls.aim: Improve diagnostic and planning accuracy through contested reasoning
controls.family_label: LLM-as-judge, self-consistency, second-model or second-vendor verification, ensembles, multi-agent debate
tradeoffs: Aligned agents only partially moderated bias without fully converting a biased counterpart; even aligned agents showed intrinsic framework biases (left-leaning tendencies); deliberation navigates rather than resolves Arrow's constraints

evidence.title: Beyond Arrow's Impossibility: Fairness as an Emergent Property of Multi-Agent Collaboration
evidence.comparator_used: Each agent's allocation in isolation (single agent), aligned or unaligned/adversarial
evidence.outcome: Fairness/ethical adequacy of triage allocation
evidence.effect: Qualitative: neither agent's allocation was ethically adequate alone, but the joint final allocation after three debate rounds could satisfy fairness criteria neither reached alone; no numbers reported in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Aligned agents only partially moderated bias without fully converting a biased counterpart; even aligned agents showed intrinsic framework biases (left-leaning tendencies); deliberation navigates rather than resolves Arrow's constraints
evidence.quote: We find that alignment systematically shapes negotiation strategies and allocation patterns, and that neither agent's allocation is ethically adequate in isolation, yet their joint final allocation can satisfy fairness criteria that neither would have reached alone.

evidence.title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
evidence.comparator_used: Single generalist LLMs
evidence.outcome: Harm potential / safety performance of consultation recommendations (NOHARM benchmark)
evidence.effect: Multi-agent AI teaming 'further improving performance in generalist models'; no numeric effect given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Harm potential was not uniform across systems, with clinical AI tools outperforming generalist LLMs, and multi-agent AI teaming further improving performance in generalist models.

controls.question: Should we prompt the LLM to review and correct its own answer before returning it?
controls.control: Prompt the LLM to re-evaluate and revise its own answer, for example with chain-of-verification.

controls.aim: Reduce errors and hallucinations without adding a second model
controls.family_label: LLM-as-judge, self-consistency, second-model or second-vendor verification, ensembles, multi-agent debate

evidence.title: Multi-Agent Dynamic Refinement Outperforms Static RAG in Clinical Reasoning for Complex Nephrology Cases
evidence.comparator_used: LLM with static guideline-based RAG and no iterative self-critique (Model B)
evidence.outcome: Clinical reasoning score in longitudinal nephrology cases
evidence.effect: Human evaluation (20-point scale): Model C (RAG plus iterative self-critique and refinement) 17.2 vs Model B 16.2 (P < 0.001). AI panel: 14.7 vs 14.3 (P = 0.01). Model C was also a multi-agent framework, so the self-critique effect is confounded with the agent decomposition.
evidence.quote: Static knowledge retrieval alone fails to enhance frontier LLM performance in longitudinal medical reasoning.

evidence.title: Can Large Language Models Self-Correct in Medical Question Answering? An Exploratory Study
evidence.comparator_used: Standard chain-of-thought prompting (first answer) vs iterative self-reflection loop, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on medical multiple-choice QA (MedQA, HeadQA, PubMedQA)
evidence.effect: Modest gains on MedQA; limited or negative benefits on HeadQA and PubMedQA; more reflection steps did not guarantee better performance; no numeric values in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Self-reflection could introduce new errors or leave errors uncorrected; the abstract reports negative benefit on some datasets but no figures.
evidence.quote: Our results show that self-reflective prompting does not consistently improve accuracy and its impact is highly dataset- and model-dependent: it yields modest gains on MedQA but provides limited or negative benefits on HeadQA and PubMedQA, and increasing the number of reflection steps does not guarantee better performance.

evidence.title: Chain-of-verification prompting for NIH stroke scale extraction using small and frontier large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline prompt (first answer, no self-verification step)
evidence.outcome: NIHSS subscore exact-match accuracy, subscore MAE, total score MAE and total exact accuracy
evidence.effect: Small models: subscore accuracy 65.0 ± 10.9% vs 53.2 ± 10.0% at baseline; subscore MAE 0.55 ± 0.21 vs 0.84 ± 0.22; total MAE 4.84 ± 2.30 vs 7.19 ± 3.54 (all p < 0.001); total exact accuracy stayed modest at 9.6 ± 15.7%. Frontier models: no significant group-level change.
evidence.quote: CoVe prompting substantially improves NIHSS extraction in small LLMs while producing negligible effects in frontier models.

evidence.title: Med-HEAL: Analyzing and Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical LLMs with Hallucination-Aware In-Context Learning
evidence.comparator_used: Original first answer from the model without self-critique
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on open-ended EHR clinical question answering
evidence.effect: Self-critique improved accuracy for three of five models (p < 0.05); no parameter updates required
evidence.quote: Experiments across five open-source LLMs-BioMistral, Llama-3.1, DeepSeek, Qwen2.5, and Qwen3, show that the self-critique strategy improves accuracy for three of five models (p < 0.05) without requiring parameter updates.

controls.question: Should we use a two-stage cascade where a first screener decides which cases go to a second model or LLM adjudicator?
controls.control: Use a first-stage screener to gate cases to a second-stage model, LLM, or multi-agent adjudicator.

tradeoffs: Stage 3 relies on manual chart review for the final uncertain cases, and high-uncertainty cases still performed poorly in stage 2 (F1 0.58).

Modest simulated call overhead (ROUTER_R1 1.21 calls; ROUTER_R2_AUDIT 2.00 calls) versus a single LEAN call. Results come from deterministic offline simulations over stored outputs from a single model on synthetic vignettes.

Routers suggested slightly more tests than the lean baseline (about 2.14-2.21 vs 1.95). The simple router R1 still had 2/16 monotonicity violations. Only synthetic vignettes and a single model were tested.
The cascade's higher specificity came with much lower sensitivity (0.297). The high-recall screen produced 729 alerts per 1,000 messages that need clinician review.

evidence.title: Confidence-linked and uncertainty-based staged framework for phenotype validation using large language models
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.comparator_used: Stage 1 alone (zero-shot ensemble applied to all cases)
evidence.outcome: Overall F1-score against physician-labeled data
evidence.effect: F1 rose from 0.840 (stage 1) to 0.878 (stage 2) to 0.955 (stage 3).
evidence.tradeoff: Stage 3 relies on manual chart review for the final uncertain cases, and high-uncertainty cases still performed poorly in stage 2 (F1 0.58).
evidence.quote: The overall framework performance showed a progressive improvement in F1-scores from 0.840 (stage 1) to 0.878 (stage 2) to 0.955 (stage 3).

evidence.title: Persona Routing Associated With Fewer Safety and Monotonicity Violations in Simulated Emergency Large Language Model (LLM) Reasoning
evidence.comparator_used: Single-stage LEAN persona (P_HL) applied to all cases; SAFE persona (P_HS) applied to all cases as a secondary reference
evidence.outcome: Rule-defined contraindication/sequence safety violations, counterfactual monotonicity violations, and test-suggestion count
evidence.effect: LEAN baseline: safety violations 8/56 (14.3%), monotonicity violations 10/16 (62.5%), mean tests 1.95. Routing: safety violations eliminated, monotonicity violations 2/16 (ROUTER_R1) and 0/16 (ROUTER_R2_CF), mean tests 2.14-2.21. SAFE alone: 0/56 safety and 0/16 monotonicity violations but mean tests 3.38-4.32.
evidence.tradeoff: Modest simulated call overhead (ROUTER_R1 1.21 calls; ROUTER_R2_AUDIT 2.00 calls) versus a single LEAN call. Results come from deterministic offline simulations over stored outputs from a single model on synthetic vignettes.
evidence.quote: Routing eliminated safety violations and reduced monotonicity violations (ROUTER_R1 2/16; ROUTER_R2_CF 0/16) while keeping test counts near the lean baseline in the main router simulation (means: 2.14-2.21) with modest simulated call overhead (ROUTER_R1 1.21 calls; ROUTER_R2_AUDIT 2.00 calls).

evidence.title: Persona routing reduces safety and monotonicity violations in simulated emergency clinical reasoning with large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Static single-persona baselines applied to all cases (lean BASE_HL; safe BASE_HS and BASE_LS)
evidence.outcome: Safety violations, test counts and counterfactual monotonicity violations
evidence.effect: BASE_HL had safety violations in 8/56 scenarios (14.3%; mean severity 0.39) with mean 1.95 tests. SAFE baselines had zero violations but more tests (BASE_HS 3.38; BASE_LS 4.32). Routers had zero safety violations with mean tests of 2.14 (R1), 2.20 (R2_AUDIT) and 2.21 (R3_ARBITER). Monotonicity violations: LEAN 10/16 (62.5%), SAFE 0/16, ROUTER_R1 2/16, ROUTER_R2 (audit) 0/16.
evidence.tradeoff: Routers suggested slightly more tests than the lean baseline (about 2.14-2.21 vs 1.95). The simple router R1 still had 2/16 monotonicity violations. Only synthetic vignettes and a single model were tested.
evidence.quote: Routing eliminated safety violations while keeping test counts near the lean baseline (ROUTER_R1 mean 2.14; ROUTER_R2_AUDIT mean 2.20; ROUTER_R3_ARBITER mean 2.21).

evidence.title: AI safety evaluation in an underrepresented population: real-world performance of clinical decision support and frontier language models on Medicaid patient messaging triage
evidence.comparator_used: best balanced single tool applied to all messages
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity for autonomous triage of hazardous patient messages
evidence.effect: Highest-specificity cascade: sensitivity 0.297, specificity 0.874; best balanced single tool: sensitivity 0.594, specificity 0.592. A separate high-recall first-stage screen reached sensitivity 0.855 with 12.0 missed hazards and 729 alerts per 1,000 messages.
evidence.tradeoff: The cascade's higher specificity came with much lower sensitivity (0.297). The high-recall screen produced 729 alerts per 1,000 messages that need clinician review.
evidence.quote: No configuration met the autonomous benchmark; sensitivity and specificity reached 0.594 and 0.592 for the best balanced single tool, 0.685 and 0.575 for the best balanced ensemble, and 0.297 and 0.874 for the highest-specificity cascade.

evidence.title: A comprehensive inference-time augmentation framework in physiological signals: application to PPG-based AF detection
evidence.comparator_used: Standard ITA applied to all inputs (single-stage)
evidence.outcome: False positive rate on non-AF PPG datasets
evidence.effect: Selective ITA reduced average FPR by up to 4.4% (GPT-PPG) and 1.3% (ResNet)
evidence.quote: Selective ITA further reduced average FPR by up to 4.4% (GPT-PPG) and 1.3% (ResNet) on non-AF PPG datasets.

controls.question: Should we check generated outputs against hard rules or schemas and send failures back to the LLM for repair?
controls.control: Validate generated output against schemas, constraints, or database state and loop failures back for automated repair.
controls.comparator: Unvalidated single-pass generation
controls.aim: Prevent malformed or constraint-violating outputs from reaching downstream systems
controls.family_label: LLM-as-judge, self-consistency, second-model or second-vendor verification, ensembles, multi-agent debate
tradeoffs: Repair requires iterative loops; most errors resolved within one or two iterations (extra generation passes).

evidence.title: Closed-Loop Validation-Repair for Healthcare Interoperability: A Multi-Model Study of Schema Compliance in Clinical LLMs
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline single-pass generation without validation-repair (paired baseline condition)
evidence.outcome: Schema compliance of structured outputs (ICD-10, CPT, HL7 FHIR) across 960 model-scenario pairs
evidence.effect: Compliance rose from baseline 85.9-91.6% to 99.0% overall (98.4-99.4% across models); absolute improvements of 7.8 to 12.5 percentage points; exact McNemar p<0.001
evidence.tradeoff: Repair requires iterative loops; most errors resolved within one or two iterations (extra generation passes).
evidence.quote: Third, the validation-repair framework achieves 99.0 percent overall compliance, ranging from 98.4 to 99.4 percent across models, with most errors resolving within one or two iterations.

controls.question: Should we add an independent automated check on AI-generated contours, synthetic images, and radiotherapy plans before clinical use?
controls.control: Run an independent model or computation to flag AI-generated contours, synthetic images, or treatment plans needing review.
controls.comparator: Manual clinician review of AI outputs without automated QA
controls.aim: Catch erroneous contours, images, or plans before treatment
controls.family_label: LLM-as-judge, self-consistency, second-model or second-vendor verification, ensembles, multi-agent debate
tradeoffs: Recall of 0.75 means some poor contours are missed; the study does not report added workload or cost.

evidence.title: Automatic gross tumor volume segmentation with failure detection for safe implementation in locally advanced cervical cancer
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.comparator_used: No head-to-head comparison with manual review alone; classifier performance was measured against ground-truth DSC thresholds on the prospective test cohort
evidence.outcome: Detection of failed GTV auto-contours (DSC below threshold) from radiomic features of the segmented GTV
evidence.effect: Logistic Regression on test cohort (T = 0.67 on DSC): precision 0.88, recall 0.75, F1 0.81, accuracy 0.86
evidence.tradeoff: Recall of 0.75 means some poor contours are missed; the study does not report added workload or cost.
evidence.quote: Failure detection could generate precision ( P = 0.88  ), recall ( R = 0.75  ), F1-score ( F = 0.81  ), and accuracy ( A = 0.86  ) using Logistic Regression (LR) classifier on the test cohort with a threshold T = 0.67 on DSC values.

evidence.title: Automatic contour quality assurance using deep-learning based contours
evidence.comparator_used: Geometric-only comparison of primary and independent verification auto-contouring models (DSC, surface DSC, 95% Hausdorff distance, mean surface distance) without dose metrics
evidence.outcome: Ability of the verification model comparison to flag dosimetric errors in the primary auto-contours (D_error, mean and D_error, max), measured by ROC-AUC and AUPRC in the test set
evidence.effect: Adding dose metrics increased ROC-AUC and AUPRC for D_error,mean in H&N small structures. For D_error,max it increased performance for H&N small, H&N medium and GYN structures. No numeric values given in the abstract, and gains were not reported for all structure groups.
evidence.quote: In many instances, utilizing dose with geometric comparisons can improve the ability of a verification model to flag potential errors from a primary auto-contouring model.

controls.question: Should we test patient-facing materials with AI-simulated patient personas before release?
controls.control: Use AI patient personas simulating varied literacy and cognitive load to surface comprehension barriers in patient-facing documents.
controls.comparator: Readability formulas or expert review alone
controls.aim: Identify comprehension barriers in patient materials before release
controls.family_label: LLM-as-judge, self-consistency, second-model or second-vendor verification, ensembles, multi-agent debate
tradeoffs: The personas are simulated, so the findings must be validated with real patients.

evidence.title: Clinician-supervised large language AI model after-discharge instruction generation for common emergency department presentations
evidence.comparator_used: Flesch Reading Ease readability scores and physician review of the instructions
evidence.outcome: Identification of comprehension barriers in after-discharge instructions for marginalised patient groups
evidence.effect: Readability scores favoured Claude for simpler language after revisions, but the AI personas still found persistent medical jargon and vague instructions. No numeric effect reported in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: The personas are simulated, so the findings must be validated with real patients.
evidence.quote: Whilst Claude was preferred for simpler language after revisions, persona reviews revealed persistent medical jargon and vague instructions that could hinder understanding for marginalised groups.

controls.question: Should our AI send low-confidence cases to a human reviewer instead of outputting or acting on every prediction?
controls.control: Set a confidence or uncertainty cutoff; below it, withhold, suppress, or flag the AI output and route the case to human review.
controls.comparator: AI outputs every prediction, or uniform review of all outputs
controls.aim: Prevent errors on uncertain cases while focusing clinician review effort where it matters
variants: Abstain and route below-threshold cases to human review
Accept high-confidence outputs with lighter checks
Two cutoffs with rule-out, indeterminate, and rule-in zones; only the middle zone goes to review or a second test
Flag imaging segmentations with high uncertainty or low predicted quality for correction
Hide or de-emphasize outputs in score zones likely to mislead clinicians
Allow automated actions only on low-risk, high-confidence cases; tier autonomy by harm severity
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction
tradeoffs: 37% abstention rate. Fewer children get a determinate result at stricter thresholds. Indeterminate cases need further clinician evaluation.

Raising the cutoff improves accuracy but reduces workload savings (external cohort: 86.0% accuracy at 0.8 vs 95.1% accuracy with only 39.3% reduction at 0.9). Low-confidence cases still need IHC staining and manual review. Determinants of the confidence index are not fully characterized.

Triage had more missed fractures and more with clinical consequences than standalone AI. It increased FN in all experience subgroups except radiologists-in-training. It did reduce FP compared with standalone AI.

Only a fraction of reports are auto-labeled (34-37% of T-stage, 55% of N-stage); the remainder is deferred to human review. Accepted predictions were enriched for prototypical labels (e.g., N0 = 91%).
High-uncertainty cases performed poorly and still needed manual review: 285 of 1072 test cases went to chart review.
Requires human review of 30% of AI outputs, which adds reviewer workload.

evidence.title: From Concept to Clinic: Real World Evidence for Autonomous AI Deployment in Primary Care Telemedicine
evidence.comparator_used: AI diagnosis output for all cases (overall), with no confidence threshold applied
evidence.outcome: Top-1 diagnosis concordance with the treating clinician's diagnosis
evidence.effect: 91.3% overall vs 96.3% among cases meeting the pre-specified safety confidence threshold; 97.9% in common, lower-complexity conditions meeting the same threshold
evidence.quote: The AI’s top-1 diagnosis matched the clinician’s diagnosis in 91.3% of cases overall, increasing to 96.3% among cases meeting a pre-specified safety confidence threshold, and 97.9% in common, lower-complexity conditions that met the same confidence threshold.

evidence.title: An analysis of the real world performance of an artificial intelligence based autism diagnostic
evidence.comparator_used: Device outputting a positive or negative prediction for more cases, with abstention thresholds loosened toward a 100% determinate rate
evidence.outcome: Accuracy metrics (PPV, NPV, sensitivity, specificity) and determinate rate across decision thresholds
evidence.effect: Abstention thresholds that gave a 63.0% determinate rate preserved accuracy (PPV 92.44%, NPV 97.56%). Loosening them to 81.4% significantly dropped PPV (p=0.039) and increased false positives from 9 to 22. Loosening further to 94.7% significantly dropped PPV and sensitivity (p=0.042). Indeterminate cases still received a detailed report and clinician review.
evidence.tradeoff: 37% abstention rate. Fewer children get a determinate result at stricter thresholds. Indeterminate cases need further clinician evaluation.
evidence.quote: Restricting determinate outputs to the 63.0% of cases with sufficient certainty prevents the degradation of device performance that is seen when adjusting abstention thresholds to allow for larger determinate rates.

evidence.title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
evidence.comparator_used: fully automated model classifying every slide (and fully manual IHC plus pathologist review of all slides)
evidence.outcome: diagnostic accuracy and IHC workload in lineage prediction with confidence-threshold deferral to IHC and manual review
evidence.effect: Fully automated model had 16.1% lower accuracy and 0.040 lower AUC than IHC/manual review in the prospective cohort (p<0.001). Semi-automated with threshold deferral gave 95.9% accuracy, comparable to full IHC/manual (p=0.610), with a 68.9% reduction in IHC workload. Internal test: threshold >0.8 gave accuracy comparable to manual (p=0.856), with 78.0% auto-subtyped. External cohort: cutoff 0.8 gave 86.0% accuracy; cutoff 0.9 gave 95.1% accuracy (p=0.293 vs manual) with 39.3% workload reduction. Functional cohort: 99.0% accuracy, 74.4% workload reduction.
evidence.tradeoff: Raising the cutoff improves accuracy but reduces workload savings (external cohort: 86.0% accuracy at 0.8 vs 95.1% accuracy with only 39.3% reduction at 0.9). Low-confidence cases still need IHC staining and manual review. Determinants of the confidence index are not fully characterized.
evidence.quote: In the prospective cohort, the implementation of the semi-automated approach resulted in a 68.9% reduction in the workload of IHC staining.

evidence.title: AI for fracture diagnosis in clinical practice: Four approaches to systematic AI-implementation and their impact on AI-effectiveness
evidence.comparator_used: AI-standalone (AI outputs every prediction without radiologist consultation); also radiologist alone
evidence.outcome: False negatives and false positives for fracture detection, and their clinical consequences
evidence.effect: AI-triage (radiologist consulted when AI in doubt): 2.1% FN (32/1508; 18 consequences), 1.7% FP (26/1508). AI-standalone: 1.5% FN (23/1508; 11 consequences), 6.8% FP (103/1508). Radiologist alone: 2.7% FN, 1.2% FP.
evidence.tradeoff: Triage had more missed fractures and more with clinical consequences than standalone AI. It increased FN in all experience subgroups except radiologists-in-training. It did reduce FP compared with standalone AI.
evidence.quote: These results suggest AI should not be considered for problem-solving or triage at this time; AI standalone performs better than either and may be a source of assistance where radiologists are unavailable.

evidence.title: CALM-RAD: Calibrated GPT-4o Confidence-Based Triage Enables 96-100% Accuracy in Automated TNM Staging of Head and Neck Cancer Reports
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.comparator_used: Accepting all GPT-4o predictions without confidence-based triage (baseline accuracy on all test reports)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of auto-labeled T-stage and N-stage predictions after confidence-based triage
evidence.effect: T-stage: accepting 37% (simple prompt) and 34% (structured prompt) of predictions raised accuracy from 0.73 to 0.89 and from 0.81 to 1.00; N-stage: accepting 55% of cases achieved up to 1.00 accuracy (baseline 0.80 simple, 0.83 structured)
evidence.tradeoff: Only a fraction of reports are auto-labeled (34-37% of T-stage, 55% of N-stage); the remainder is deferred to human review. Accepted predictions were enriched for prototypical labels (e.g., N0 = 91%).
evidence.quote: Triage thresholds accepting 37% (simple) and 34% (structured) of T-stage predictions raised accuracies to 0.89 and 1.00, respectively; accepting 55% of N-stage cases achieved up to 1.00 accuracy.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence suppression as a strategy to mitigate artificial intelligence automation bias
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.comparator_used: AI diagnoses always shown to clinicians in the AI-assisted round, with no suppression
evidence.outcome: Clinicians' automation bias (errors caused by misleading AI diagnoses)
evidence.effect: Estimated 41.7% decrease in automation bias. Without suppression, automation bias accounted for 45.5% of clinicians' errors in the AI-assisted round.
evidence.quote: The proposed AI suppression strategy was estimated to decrease clinicians' automation bias by 41.7%.

evidence.title: Confidence-linked and uncertainty-based staged framework for phenotype validation using large language models
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.comparator_used: Uniform manual review of all cases (implied by the stated 75% reduction in review burden)
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy (weighted F1) by uncertainty level, and manual review burden
evidence.effect: Weighted F1 for low- vs high-uncertainty cases: 0.94 vs 0.57 in stage 1 and 0.82 vs 0.58 in stage 2. Overall F1 reached 0.955 after manual review of the remaining uncertain cases. Manual review burden fell by 75%.
evidence.tradeoff: High-uncertainty cases performed poorly and still needed manual review: 285 of 1072 test cases went to chart review.
evidence.quote: Low-uncertainty cases consistently outperformed high-uncertainty cases in both stages (weighted F1-scores: 0.94 vs 0.57 in stage 1 and 0.82 vs 0.58 in stage 2).

evidence.title: Next-generation multicenter studies: using artificial intelligence to automatically process unstructured health records of patients with lung cancer across multiple institutions
evidence.venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
evidence.comparator_used: AI-only extraction with no human review of low-confidence outputs (7.0% error rate)
evidence.outcome: Data extraction error rate
evidence.effect: Error rate fell from 7.0% with AI alone to 4.4% with targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs
evidence.tradeoff: Requires human review of 30% of AI outputs, which adds reviewer workload.
evidence.quote: A hybrid approach with targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs further decreased error rates to 4.4%.

evidence.title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.comparator_used: No certainty threshold (all LLM classifications accepted, with full coverage)
evidence.outcome: Extraction accuracy and coverage rate
evidence.effect: Accuracies improved to > 90% with certainty thresholds, while coverage fell to < 50%
evidence.tradeoff: Coverage rate dropped to < 50%, so more than half of the extractions were not classified automatically
evidence.quote: Setting certainty thresholds further improved accuracies to > 90% but reduced the coverage rate to < 50%.

evidence.title: Uncertainty-aware extraction of clinical findings from Finnish EHRs using open large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Simulated uncertainty-ranked selective expert review vs reviewing more/all patients to achieve complete error coverage.
evidence.outcome: Expert-review workload needed to cover extraction errors.
evidence.effect: Complete error coverage by reviewing <10% of patients for hemiplegia (8.3%) and headache (8.2%), and 19.6% for seizure.
evidence.tradeoff: Still required expert review of the flagged subset: 8.3%, 8.2%, and 19.6% of patients for the reported targets.
evidence.quote: Entropy-based triage achieved complete error coverage by reviewing <10% of patients for hemiplegia (8.3%) and headache (8.2%), and 19.6% for seizure.

evidence.title: Automated remote sleep monitoring needs uncertainty quantification
evidence.comparator_used: State-of-the-art ML model outputting every sleep-stage prediction without uncertainty-based flagging or expert review of uncertain epochs
evidence.outcome: Five-stage sleep-scoring accuracy on wearable EEG data
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 63.9% to 71.2% with the uncertainty-centred U-PASS pipeline that flags uncertain predictions for expert review
evidence.tradeoff: Manual review by sleep specialists without specific training for sleep staging on wearable EEG proved ineffective, so the review step depends on expert training.
evidence.quote: This increased the five-stage sleep-scoring accuracy of a state-of-the-art machine learning model from 63.9% to 71.2% on our dataset.

evidence.title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
evidence.comparator_used: AI model reviewing every chest X-ray alone, and physician reviewing every chest X-ray alone
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy for ARDS findings on chest X-ray
evidence.effect: AI-first with deferral to physician if uncertain: 0.869 (95% CI 0.835-0.903) vs AI alone 0.847 (0.806-0.887) and physician alone 0.808 (0.767-0.85)
evidence.tradeoff: Physicians must still review the uncertain cases; the AI decides up to 79% of cases, leaving the remainder for physician review.
evidence.quote: Among several collaboration strategies tested, we find that if the AI model first reviews the chest X-ray and defers to a physician if it is uncertain, this strategy achieves a higher diagnostic accuracy (0.869, 95% CI 0.835-0.903) compared to a strategy where a physician reviews a chest X-ray first and defers to an AI model if uncertain (0.824, 95% CI 0.781-0.862), or strategies where the physician reviews the chest X-ray alone (0.808, 95% CI 0.767-0.85) or the AI model reviews the chest X-ray alone (0.847, 95% CI 0.806-0.887).

evidence.title: Standard-of-Care vs. Machine Learning–Recommended Discharge Destinations for Geriatric Surgical Inpatients: Algorithm Development and Internal Validation
evidence.comparator_used: Accuracy on all predictions (no exclusion of uncertain predictions), simulating a human-in-the-loop strategy
evidence.outcome: Discharge destination prediction accuracy after excluding the 15% of predictions with highest uncertainty
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 82% overall to 85% for the remaining predictions (p = 0.006)
evidence.tradeoff: 15% of predictions were excluded and would need human review; the human-in-the-loop strategy was only mimicked, not actually tested.
evidence.quote: Mimicking a human-in-the-loop strategy, we excluded the 15% of predictions with the highest uncertainty, which increased accuracy for the remaining predictions to 85% (p = 0.006).

evidence.title: A confidence-based, artificial intelligence pathology model for diagnosis of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
evidence.venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
evidence.comparator_used: Same model without confidence thresholding (all predictions output, AUROC 0.840 in retrospective test set)
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic discrimination of ICCA vs metastasis (AUROC and false-positive rate) in the retrospective test set
evidence.effect: Confidence thresholding improved AUROC from 0.840 to 0.958 with an FPR of 0; prospective AUROCs 1.00 (French cohort) and 0.965 (Asian cohort)
evidence.tradeoff: Only 46% of samples retained for high-confidence prediction; the remainder is not predicted with confidence
evidence.quote: Implementation of confidence thresholding improved the AUROC to 0.958 with an FPR of 0, while retaining 46% of samples for high-confidence prediction.

evidence.title: A hybrid approach to scalable real-world data curation by machine learning and human experts
evidence.comparator_used: ML-only extraction and fully manual abstraction by clinical experts
evidence.outcome: Data error rate versus manual abstraction effort for curated oncology variables
evidence.effect: Only small amounts of manual abstraction were needed to reach expert-level error rates; in some cases hybrid error rates were lower than manual abstraction. No numeric values are given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Needs reference-standard labels to calibrate confidence thresholds and the tradeoff between abstraction effort and data quality.
evidence.quote: Only small amounts of manual abstraction are required for hybrid curation to achieve expert-level error rates.

evidence.title: Selective prediction as a triage gate for primary-care depression screening: quantifying and mitigating selection bias in CHARLS-2011
evidence.comparator_used: Model-embedded uncertainty (each model's own uncertainty) versus a decoupled XGBoost-residual selector; abstention at ~20% coverage compared with predicting on all cases
evidence.outcome: Selective prediction performance (test AUC at ~20% coverage) with abstention on uncertain cases
evidence.effect: With the decoupled XGBoost residual selector, all five models achieved selective prediction at approximately 20% coverage (test AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.85-0.95); model-embedded uncertainty succeeded only for XGBoost
evidence.tradeoff: Abstains on approximately 80% of cases, which are routed to human evaluation; only about 20% coverage is automated
evidence.quote: Model-embedded uncertainty succeeded only for XGBoost; with the decoupled XGBoost residual selector, all five models achieved selective prediction at approximately 20% coverage (test AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.85-0.95), abstaining on approximately 80% of cases for individual safety.

evidence.title: Adaptive AI for Cardiovascular Event Adjudication: Cardiovascular Event Adjudication Across Different Definitions in the ODYSSEY OUTCOMES and EUCLID Trials
evidence.comparator_used: ADAPT-CEC AI adjudication of all suspected events alone (and direct GPT 4o adjudication)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of end point classification versus human adjudication (F1 score, % correctly classified end points) and replication of the EUCLID primary treatment effect
evidence.effect: Hybrid correctly classified 95.6% of end points vs 86.4% for ADAPT-CEC and 76.3% for GPT 4o; non-end points 99.6% vs 99.4% and 99.8%. Hybrid F1: CV death 0.94, MI 0.80, stroke 0.82, bleeding 0.83. ADAPT-CEC F1 was lower for CV death, MI and stroke. EUCLID primary HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.94-1.15) hybrid vs 1.02 (0.93-1.13) human.
evidence.tradeoff: Humans must still adjudicate the 30% of suspected events with the lowest AI prediction certainty, so some adjudication time and cost remain; no cost or time figures reported.
evidence.quote: A hybrid approach with humans adjudicating those suspected events with the lowest 30% of ADAPT-CEC prediction certainty was superior to ADAPT-CEC alone or GPT 4o alone and replicated the EUCLID primary outcome treatment effect.

evidence.title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Case Study
evidence.comparator_used: Extraction output for all reports without a certainty threshold (full coverage)
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy and coverage rate
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose to >90% with certainty thresholds, while coverage fell to <50%
evidence.tradeoff: Coverage rate dropped to <50%, so over half of classifications fell below the threshold and would need other handling.
evidence.quote: Setting certainty thresholds further improved accuracies to >90% but reduced the coverage rate to <50%.

evidence.title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.comparator_used: LLM outputting all predictions without abstention (no confidence-based selective prediction)
evidence.outcome: LLM deprescribing recommendation performance with selective prediction (abstaining on low-confidence predictions)
evidence.effect: Only marginal improvement in performance; no numeric effect reported in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Confidence estimates were poorly calibrated, so confidence often failed to align with actual success, limiting the value of the abstention threshold.
evidence.quote: Selective prediction only marginally improved LLM performance due to poorly calibrated confidence estimates.

evidence.title: A Human-Centered AI Framework for Efficient Labelling of ECGs From Drug Safety Trials
evidence.comparator_used: Uniform expert review of all DL-based QT measurements
evidence.outcome: Review workload and QT accuracy when high-uncertainty measurements are routed to experts
evidence.effect: Only 10% of data reviewed per trial, selected mostly by high model uncertainty, while maintaining high QT accuracy
evidence.quote: We assess its effectiveness on 3 drug safety trials and show that it can significantly reduce effort required for ECG labelling-in our experiments only 10% of the data were reviewed per trial-while maintaining high levels of QT accuracy.

evidence.title: Benchmarking robustness of automated CT pancreas segmentation: achieving human-level reliability through human-in-the-loop optimization
evidence.comparator_used: Automated model predictions without flagging or revision of uncertain outputs
evidence.outcome: Fraction of predictions reaching human-level performance (Fractional Threshold, FT)
evidence.effect: Human revision of flagged outliers increased FT to 0.99, versus FT for DSC and NSD that remained lower than human performance in most cases without revision; 23-fold workload reduction
evidence.tradeoff: Average 1.54 minutes of human revision time per case; the model alone remained constrained by tail-case failures
evidence.quote: Human-in-the-loop revision of acquisition-flagged outliers increased FT to 0.99, with an average time of 1.54 minutes per case, corresponding to a 23-fold workload reduction.

evidence.title: Predicting future dementia from routine clinical MRI and linked healthcare data
evidence.comparator_used: Applying the SVM classifier to all scans without confidence-based stratification (overall performance, AUC 0.71)
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy for future dementia prediction in high-confidence (distance-from-hyperplane) subgroup vs all scans
evidence.effect: High-confidence subgroup (~35% of scans) had accuracy of around 80%; overall model AUC 0.71
evidence.tradeoff: Only about 35% of scans fall in the high-confidence subgroup, so selective use of high-certainty predictions leaves the remaining ~65% without a high-confidence prediction.
evidence.quote: Confidence-based stratification identified a high-confidence subgroup comprising approximately 35% of scans, within which prediction accuracy increased to around 80%.

evidence.title: InsightSleepNet: the interpretable and uncertainty-aware deep learning network for sleep staging using continuous Photoplethysmography
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.comparator_used: Same model outputting predictions for all epochs, before applying the energy score threshold
evidence.outcome: Sleep staging classification performance (accuracy, Cohen's kappa, weighted F1) on MESA, CFS and CAP datasets
evidence.quote: We observed a significant improvement in the model's performance with the implementation of the energy score threshold.

evidence.title: Predictive Performance Precision Analysis in Medicine: Identification of low-confidence predictions at patient and profile levels (MED3pa I)
evidence.comparator_used: Model outputs predictions for all patients (100% declaration rate), with no confidence-based restriction
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and AUC when retaining only the most confident predictions (Metrics by Declaration Rate curves)
evidence.effect: Limiting predictions to the 93% most confident cases improved sensitivity by 14.3% and AUC by 5.1% (internal validation)
evidence.tradeoff: Predictions are withheld for the remaining less-confident patients, so there is a trade-off between model performance and the proportion of patients for whom predictions are considered reliable.
evidence.quote: In internal validation, limiting predictions to the 93% most confident cases improved sensitivity by 14.3% and the AUC by 5.1%.

evidence.title: Application of simultaneous uncertainty quantification for image segmentation with probabilistic deep learning: Performance benchmarking of oropharyngeal cancer target delineation as a use-case
evidence.comparator_used: Full dataset with no referral (all model segmentations retained, no uncertainty-based rejection)
evidence.outcome: Segmentation accuracy (DSC) after referring high-uncertainty patients
evidence.effect: DSC improved from the full dataset by 4.7% (MC Dropout Ensemble) and 5.0% (Deep Ensemble) using uncertainty thresholds from 0.85 validation DSC, averaged over all uncertainty measures
evidence.tradeoff: 21.8% (MC Dropout Ensemble) and 22% (Deep Ensemble) of patients were referred, i.e. rejected from the set
evidence.quote: With referring patients based on uncertainty thresholds from 0.85 validation DSC for all uncertainty measures, on average the DSC improved from the full dataset by 4.7% and 5.0% while referring 21.8% and 22% patients for MC Dropout Ensemble and Deep Ensemble, respectively.

evidence.title: A Simulation-Based Validation Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Clinical Triage: Conformal Prediction and Ensemble Learning Applied to a Synthetic ICU Benchmark Cohort
evidence.comparator_used: Model predictions on all cases with no abstention (full-coverage AUC)
evidence.outcome: AUC on retained cases under selective prediction with abstention (synthetic ICU cohort)
evidence.effect: AUC rose from 0.917 to 0.980 at 50% abstention
evidence.tradeoff: Half of cases are abstained and would need human handling; results are from synthetic data only.
evidence.quote: Selective prediction raised AUC from 0.917 to 0.980 at 50% abstention.

evidence.title: Data leakage inflates reported accuracy of deep learning for kidney stone detection on CT: a leakage-free, calibrated and uncertainty-aware reassessment across three centers
evidence.comparator_used: classifying all cases without selective deferral
evidence.outcome: reliability of predictions
evidence.effect: Reported qualitatively as improved reliability; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Calibration and selective classification further improved reliability, and no sex disparity in sensitivity was found once results were pooled across patients, though one appeared spuriously at the image level.

evidence.title: Development and retrospective validation of SCOUT: scalable clinical oversight of large language models via uncertainty triangulation
evidence.comparator_used: Clinician review of every AI output.
evidence.outcome: Human review volume and projected final accuracy after selective deferral of unreliable LLM predictions.
evidence.effect: 45% to 83% reduction in cases requiring human review; projected final accuracy 99.1% to 100.0%
evidence.tradeoff: Final accuracy assumes expert correction of all flagged cases; prospective randomized validation is underway.
evidence.quote: SCOUT reduced the volume of cases requiring human review by 45% to 83%, with projected final accuracy of 99.1% to 100.0% assuming expert correction of all flagged cases.

evidence.title: Quantifying Epistemic Uncertainty in Predictions for Safer Health AI Performance Under Dataset Shifts
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.comparator_used: Performance on all samples (no uncertainty screening) versus samples below the 95th-percentile epistemic uncertainty threshold; flagged samples were set aside for review
evidence.outcome: Macro-F1 and robustness to temporal drift; capture of prediction errors by flagged samples
evidence.effect: Samples below the threshold had consistently higher macro-F1 and performance virtually invariant to temporal drift across all training-test time pairs; flagged samples captured most prediction errors (no numeric values in the abstract)
evidence.quote: Results across all training-test time pairs show that samples below this threshold exhibit consistently higher macro-F1 and render performance virtually invariant to temporal drift, while the flagged samples captured most prediction errors.

evidence.title: Prompt Engineering Strategies Improve the Diagnostic Accuracy of GPT-4 Turbo in Neuroradiology Cases
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline GPT-4 Turbo output for all cases without a confidence threshold
evidence.outcome: Top-diagnosis accuracy, five-candidate applicability and misdiagnosis rate
evidence.effect: Top diagnosis accuracy 55.1% at baseline vs 72.9% with a 90% confidence threshold; five-candidate applicability 70.6% vs 85.9%; misdiagnosis 29.4% vs 14.1%
evidence.tradeoff: Limited the analysis to half of cases, so the AI output was withheld for about half of cases.
evidence.quote: Applying a 90% confidence threshold increased the accuracy of the top diagnosis to 72.9% and the applicability of the five candidates to 85.9%, while reducing misdiagnoses to 14.1%, but limited the analysis to half of cases.

evidence.title: A selective deep learning framework for pressure injury staging with calibrated confidence and automated clinical documentation
evidence.comparator_used: Classifier outputting a prediction for every case (baseline overall accuracy 74.4%, no deferral)
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy on retained predictions and share of baseline errors captured by deferral
evidence.effect: At the 85% confidence threshold, accuracy on retained predictions was 90.8% versus 74.4% overall; deferral captured 83.3% of all baseline errors. On external validation, retained accuracy at the same threshold was 72.7%, against a macro F1 of 0.590 for all predictions.
evidence.tradeoff: Deferred cases need clinician review. The abstract does not report the proportion deferred. The benefit was much smaller on the external dataset.
evidence.quote: At an 85% confidence threshold, classification accuracy on retained predictions reached 90.8%, while deferral captured 83.3% of all baseline errors.

evidence.title: Semantic Consistency-Based Uncertainty Quantification for Factuality in Radiology Report Generation
evidence.comparator_used: Generating all reports without abstention (no rejection of high-uncertainty reports)
evidence.outcome: Factuality score of retained radiology reports (Radialog on MIMIC-CXR)
evidence.effect: Factuality scores improved by 10% when rejecting 20% of reports
evidence.tradeoff: 20% of reports are rejected/abstained from and would need human handling
evidence.quote: By abstaining from high-uncertainty reports, our approach improves factuality scores by 10%, achieved by rejecting 20% of reports using the Radialog model on the MIMIC-CXR dataset.

evidence.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Classification of Adamantinomatous Craniopharyngioma from Preoperative MRI
evidence.comparator_used: Classifier outputting every prediction without abstention (accuracy before applying the uncertainty-based abstention mechanism)
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy on retained cases
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved from 80.8% to 95.5% with a 34.2% abstention rate
evidence.tradeoff: 34.2% of cases were abstained on (not classified) and would need other handling
evidence.quote: Our model accuracy improved from 80.8% to 95.5%, with a 34.2% abstention rate.

evidence.title: Optimizing GPT-4 Turbo Diagnostic Accuracy in Neuroradiology through Prompt Engineering and Confidence Thresholds
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline GPT-4 Turbo answering every case without a confidence threshold (55.1% baseline accuracy)
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic precision and misdiagnosis rate in 751 neuroradiology cases
evidence.effect: Top diagnosis precision rose from 55.1% baseline to 72.9% with a 90% confidence threshold. The five-candidate list contained the correct diagnosis in 85.9% of cases, and the misdiagnosis rate fell to 14.1%. This effect was combined with the five-candidate output format and was not isolated.
evidence.tradeoff: The threshold reduced the number of cases that received a response.
evidence.quote: By reformatting responses to list five diagnostic candidates and applying a 90% confidence threshold, the highest precision of the diagnosis increased to 72.9%, with the candidate list providing the correct diagnosis at 85.9%, reducing the misdiagnosis rate to 14.1%.

evidence.title: Reliable Multilingual Orthopedic Decision Support from Clinical Narratives: Language-Aware Adaptation and Verification-Guided Deferral
evidence.comparator_used: Accept-all prediction (no deferral)
evidence.outcome: Selective accuracy and selective Macro-F1 on a held-out 5,000-record subset
evidence.effect: 84.4% selective accuracy and 0.76 selective Macro-F1 at 72.3% coverage, versus 71.5% accuracy and 0.65 Macro-F1 for accept-all.
evidence.tradeoff: Coverage was 72.3%, so about 27.7% of cases were deferred rather than predicted automatically.
evidence.quote: On a randomly selected held-out 5,000-record subset, it achieves 84.4% selective accuracy and 0.76 selective Macro-F1 at 72.3% coverage, compared with 71.5% accuracy and 0.65 Macro-F1 for accept-all prediction.

evidence.title: AICyte-alone capabilities as an independent screener for triaging cervical cytology using a 50% negative cutoff value
evidence.comparator_used: Original interpretive results (routine manual cytology review of all cases), used as the reference standard
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI-designated negative cases (NPV and sensitivity) and anticipated workload reduction when cases within the 50% negative cutoff skip further review
evidence.effect: 98.80% of AI cases designated as not needing further review were negative on original diagnosis. For ASC-H or higher, sensitivity was 90.77% and NPV 98.80%. For LSIL or higher, sensitivity was 98.92% and NPV 99.94%.
evidence.tradeoff: 49 LSIL+ cases were designated by AICyte as not needing further review. Of these, histology showed 8 CIN1 and 18 negative, and the rest had no histologic follow-up. Sensitivity for ASC-H+ was 90.77%, so some abnormal cases would be missed. Workload reduction was anticipated, not measured.
evidence.quote: In 98.80% of all artificial intelligence cases that were designated as not needing further review, the corresponding original diagnosis was also determined to be negative.

evidence.title: U-PASS: An uncertainty-guided deep learning pipeline for automated sleep staging
evidence.comparator_used: Model predictions for all epochs without deferral to an expert (the pipeline's starting point)
evidence.outcome: Sleep staging accuracy on a clinical dataset of elderly sleep apnea patients
evidence.effect: Full U-PASS pipeline reached 85% accuracy versus 75% at the starting point. Deferral of uncertain epochs to a sleep expert gave the largest improvement gain.
evidence.quote: The largest improvement gain is due to the deferral of uncertain epochs to a sleep expert.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Gait Classification Using Text-Encoded Kinematic Waveforms
evidence.comparator_used: All LLM predictions retained, with no confidence-based filtering
evidence.outcome: Multiclass MCC of GPT-5 gait classification
evidence.effect: Multiclass MCC increased to 0.83 on the high-confidence filtered subset, compared with 0.70 for GPT-5 with reference grounding on all predictions
evidence.tradeoff: The 0.83 applies only to the filtered subset. The abstract does not report how many cases were excluded. The confidence signal is the LLM's self-rating.
evidence.quote: Performance of the LLM was highly dependent on explicit reference information and self-rated confidence; when restricted to high-confidence predictions, multiclass MCC increased to 0.83 on the filtered subset.

evidence.title: Uncertainty-Aware Prediction Across Endoscopic Domains: Laryngeal Narrow-Band and Gastrointestinal Imaging
evidence.comparator_used: Full coverage, with the model outputting a prediction for every case (no abstention)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy among retained cases under resolution shift (GI endoscopy)
evidence.effect: Accuracy 0.683 at full coverage to 0.852 (95% CI 0.835-0.871) at 25% coverage; balanced accuracy 0.646 to 0.798
evidence.tradeoff: Only 25% of cases are automated at the best reported accuracy, and the rest are deferred to human review. Discrimination is not improved, and prospective validation is still required.
evidence.quote: Selective prediction improved reliability among retained cases: under resolution shift, accuracy rose from 0.683 at full coverage to 0.852 (95% CI 0.835-0.871) at 25% coverage (balanced accuracy 0.646 → 0.798).

evidence.title: Increased confidence of radiomics facilitating pretherapeutic differentiation of BRAF-altered pediatric low-grade glioma
evidence.comparator_used: Traditional single-threshold conversion of model outputs to class predictions for all patients
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of BRAF status prediction
evidence.effect: Single threshold accuracy 84.5%; double threshold accuracy 92.2% on the 80.7% of patients with the highest-confidence predictions
evidence.tradeoff: About 19.3% of patients were left with uncertain predictions that the model did not classify confidently.
evidence.quote: Traditional thresholding produced an accuracy of 84.5%, while the double threshold approach yielded 92.2% accuracy on the 80.7% of patients with the highest confidence predictions.

evidence.title: On-premise medical AI agents for reliable clinical decision-making
evidence.comparator_used: Autonomous handling of all cases without a consistency cutoff (overall accuracy of the agent)
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy in the retained (autonomously handled) subset
evidence.effect: At a consistency threshold of 0.90, 49.4% of cases retained at 98.9% diagnostic accuracy
evidence.tradeoff: Only about half of cases (49.4%) are handled autonomously; the remainder are deferred for human review
evidence.quote: At a consistency threshold of 0.90, 49.4% of cases were retained at 98.9% diagnostic accuracy.

evidence.title: Hallucination filtering in radiology vision-language models using discrete semantic entropy
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline answers to all questions with no uncertainty cutoff (low-temperature output for every question)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on answered questions after rejecting high-entropy (DSE > 0.6 or > 0.3) questions
evidence.effect: DSE > 0.3 cutoff: GPT-4o 51.7% to 76.3%; GPT-4.1 54.8% to 63.8%; gains seen across both datasets and largely significant after Bonferroni correction
evidence.tradeoff: Fewer questions answered (334/706 retained for GPT-4o, 499/706 for GPT-4.1). The abstract does not report any human review of the rejected questions.
evidence.quote: DSE filtering at a 0.3 threshold increased GPT-4o accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% and GPT-4.1 from 54.8% to 63.8%, while answering fewer questions.

evidence.title: Postprocessing-Enhanced Machine Learning for Reliable Real-Time Sleep Staging in Closed-Loop Neuromodulation
evidence.comparator_used: Smoothed predictions without control logic, and the single strategies (probability thresholding, naïve waiting, entropy constraint)
evidence.outcome: Stimulation-trigger precision per sleep stage
evidence.effect: Hybrid high-confidence and low-uncertainty control achieved 80% (Wake), 96% (N2), 98% (N3), and 86% (REM) precision
evidence.tradeoff: Conservative control logic adds waiting/evidence accumulation, so there is a trade-off between latency and reliability; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Control logic further enhances reliability: our hybrid method achieves 80% (Wake), 96% (N2), 98% (N3), and 86% (REM) precision.

evidence.title: Automated Intracranial Thrombus Segmentation from CT Images of Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Dual-Channel nnU-Net Approach with Uncertainty Quantification
evidence.comparator_used: Accepting all automated segmentations without uncertainty-based triage (all cases analysed as output)
evidence.outcome: Volume-category agreement with ground truth, and detection of poor segmentations (Dice <0.60)
evidence.effect: U_clot AUC 0.89 for poor segmentation; threshold 0.323 gave 90% sensitivity and 96% NPV; 60% of cases accepted automatically; volume-category agreement improved from 66% (κ=0.49) to 83% (κ=0.69)
evidence.tradeoff: Only 60% of cases were accepted automatically, so about 40% of cases are flagged for manual review or correction.
evidence.quote: As a univariate predictor of poor segmentation, U_clot achieved an AUC of 0.89; the optimal threshold (0.323) yielded 90% sensitivity and 96% negative predictive value, allowing 60% of cases to be accepted automatically while improving volume-category agreement from 66% (κ=0.49) to 83% (κ=0.69).

evidence.title: An integrated calibration-uncertainty framework for improving the reliability of deep learning models for seizure detection in EEG signals
evidence.venue: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline CNN-BiLSTM outputting every prediction with no deferral (also compared with models optimized for calibration alone or uncertainty alone)
evidence.outcome: Seizure classification accuracy on retained samples
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 91.7% (baseline) to 99.6% while retaining ~74% of samples; outperformed models optimized for either calibration or uncertainty alone
evidence.tradeoff: About 26% of samples were flagged as unreliable and deferred for further clinical evaluation, which adds review workload.
evidence.quote: The selective classification improved accuracy from 91.7% (baseline) to 99.6% while retaining ∼74% of samples, outperforming models optimized for either calibration or uncertainty alone.

evidence.title: Neonatal Pain Detection from Facial Expressions Using Deep Learning
evidence.comparator_used: Automated network detection alone, with every prediction output and no manual assessment branch (implied; the abstract gives no network-only figure for the full framework)
evidence.outcome: Pain-event detection accuracy and recall, with low-confidence cases routed to manual assessment
evidence.effect: Overall framework accuracy reached 82.35% with the manual assessment branch; the abstract says integration increases recall of true pain events but gives no network-only figure for comparison
evidence.tradeoff: Borderline or hard cases still need manual nurse evaluation, so some human workload remains.
evidence.quote: Experimental results show our neural network sur- passes state-of-the-art algorithms by at least 25% in accuracy on the MNPAD dataset, with overall framework accuracy reaching 82.35% with integration of manual assessment branch.

evidence.title: Large-scale deep learning for metastasis detection in pathology reports
evidence.comparator_used: model output on all reports without deferral (no deferral baseline)
evidence.outcome: Recall after deferring uncertain reports for human review
evidence.effect: retaining 72.9% of reports increased recall from 0.894 to 0.969
evidence.tradeoff: 27.1% of reports deferred for human review
evidence.quote: We found that retaining 72.9% of reports increased recall from 0.894 to 0.969.

evidence.title: From Attribution to Abstention: Training-Free Attention-Based Auditing for Clinical Summarization
evidence.comparator_used: Outputting all summaries without abstention (no withholding of low-groundedness output)
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness of released summary output
evidence.effect: Faithfulness improved from 61.7% to 72.6% when the least-grounded 20% of output was withheld
evidence.tradeoff: 20% of output is withheld and must be reviewed by clinicians
evidence.quote: For hallucination detection, groundedness scores achieve 0.77 AUROC with the medical-finetuned model: competitive with embedding-based confidence at zero additional cost, and enable an abstention mechanism that improves faithfulness from 61.7% to 72.6% by withholding the least: grounded 20% of output for clinician review.

evidence.title: Towards fair and trustworthy heart rate estimation from wrist-worn photoplethysmography: a multi-wavelength dataset and uncertainty-aware deep learning approach evaluated across skin tones, sexes, and motion conditions
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline heart rate estimation outputting every prediction without uncertainty-guided rejection
evidence.outcome: MAE and parity gaps across skin tones and sexes
evidence.effect: Uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and effectively eliminated the skin tone and sex gaps; skin tone parity gap fell from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM
evidence.quote: Baseline error was higher for participants with darker skin tones and for females; uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and effectively eliminated these gaps (reducing parity gaps from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM for skin tone).

controls.question: Should we use calibrated prediction sets to flag uncertain cases rather than point predictions or heuristic confidence cutoffs?
controls.control: Apply conformal prediction on a held-out calibration set to produce prediction sets or risk groups; flag or defer cases based on the uncertainty the sets represent.
controls.comparator: Raw point predictions or heuristic confidence cutoffs without coverage guarantees
controls.aim: Provide average error-rate control, valid under the method's assumptions, when flagging or deferring uncertain predictions
variants: Prediction sets or intervals with coverage guarantees conditional on exchangeability
Defer cases whose prediction set is large or empty
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction
tradeoffs: Needs about 100 labeled documents per domain for calibration. Review effort and residual risk must be traded off through tuning.
Increased abstentions (9.6%, 14%, 22% of instances at 90%, 95%, 97.5% confidence), meaning those cases receive no AI prediction

9-13% of extracted entities were rejected (deferred). Thresholds had to be calibrated separately per domain, extraction category and model, because miscalibration direction reverses across domains. Radiology reports needed very strict thresholds (up to 0.99).
29.4% of predictions required clinician review internally; on external validation 38.6% (n=4004) were flagged for review due to interdatabase heterogeneity

evidence.title: CARE: A Conformal Safety Layer for Medical Summarization
evidence.comparator_used: Alternative calibrated baselines (calibrating only one dimension, or marginal decompositions that are valid but conservative)
evidence.outcome: Number of sentences surfaced for review while meeting the target risk bound
evidence.effect: Surfaces up to 5x fewer sentences than alternative calibrated baselines. Satisfies the target risk bound at α = 0.15 with 95% confidence across 100 calibration/test resplits on five medical summarization tasks. Calibrating only one dimension can violate the target risk bound.
evidence.tradeoff: Needs about 100 labeled documents per domain for calibration. Review effort and residual risk must be traded off through tuning.
evidence.quote: By jointly calibrating over the full $(τ,γ)$ threshold space, CARE preserves formal guarantees while surfacing up to 5$\times$ fewer sentences than alternative calibrated baselines.

evidence.title: Enhancing Patient Selection in Sepsis Clinical Trials Design Through an AI Enrichment Strategy: Algorithm Development and Validation
evidence.comparator_used: Same model without conformal prediction (raw point predictions)
evidence.outcome: Overall prediction errors and identification of potentially persistent ill patients
evidence.effect: Mixed-confidence CP reduced overall prediction errors by 27.6% (n=62) in the internal validation cohort and 30.7% (n=412) in the external validation cohort; also identified more potentially persistent ill patients
evidence.quote: Compared to the model without CP, using the model with CP at a mixed confidence approach reduced overall prediction errors by 27.6% (n=62) and 30.7% (n=412) in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, as well as enabled the identification of more potentially persistent ill patients.

evidence.title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
evidence.comparator_used: Flagged decisions from the same conformal model (no raw point-prediction or heuristic-cutoff arm was tested)
evidence.outcome: Residual harm rate among algorithmically cleared vs flagged decisions
evidence.effect: AUROC 0.80 (95% CI 0.78 to 0.82); 89.5% (95% CI 88.9% to 90.1%) of decisions cleared with 1.22% (95% CI 1.14% to 1.30%) residual harm vs 6.67% (95% CI 6.02% to 7.32%) for flagged decisions
evidence.quote: The conformal model achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.80 (95% CI 0.78 to 0.82), clearing 89.5% (95% CI 88.9% to 90.1%) of decisions with 1.22% (95% CI 1.14% to 1.30%) residual harm versus 6.67% (95% CI 6.02% to 7.32%) for flagged decisions.

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of artificial intelligence for diagnostics of antibiotic-resistant bacteria
evidence.comparator_used: Predictions without conformal prediction (raw point predictions)
evidence.outcome: Prediction errors (correctness of susceptibility predictions) and abstention rate
evidence.effect: Without conformal prediction, 84% of predictions were correct with six antibiotics as input (major error 19%, very major error 12%); conformal prediction reduced errors, with abstention in 9.6%, 14%, and 22% of instances at 90%, 95%, and 97.5% confidence levels
evidence.tradeoff: Increased abstentions (9.6%, 14%, 22% of instances at 90%, 95%, 97.5% confidence), meaning those cases receive no AI prediction
evidence.quote: Conformal prediction reduced errors but increased abstentions; at confidence levels of 90%, 95%, and 97.5%, the model abstained in 9.6%, 14%, and 22% of instances.

evidence.title: ConfidentNeuro: Conformal Prediction-Based Uncertainty Quantification for Hallucination Risk Scoring in LLM-Assisted Alzheimer's Clinical Decision Support
evidence.comparator_used: Token-level log-probability confidence (calibration audit, ECE) and the 90% target coverage; no direct head-to-head with another uncertainty method reported in the abstract
evidence.outcome: Empirical coverage of conformal prediction sets for LLM answers to Alzheimer's clinical questions, versus the 90% target
evidence.effect: GPT-4o and Claude Haiku 97.1% coverage; Mixtral-8x7B 95.7%; all above the 90% target. GPT-4o token-level confidence was miscalibrated (ECE = 0.213).
evidence.quote: GPT-4o and Claude Haiku showed empirical coverage of 97.1%.

evidence.title: Act or Defer: Error-Controlled Decision Policies for Medical Foundation Models
evidence.comparator_used: Raw point predictions / standard approaches without selection-conditional coverage guarantees
evidence.outcome: False discovery rate control among selected patients and selection-conditional coverage for deferred patients
evidence.effect: Across tasks, StratCP controls the false discovery rate among selected patients and provides valid, selection-conditional coverage for deferred patients (no numeric values reported in the abstract).
evidence.quote: Across tasks, S  trat CP controls the false discovery rate among selected patients and provides valid, selection-conditional coverage for deferred patients.

evidence.title: A Simulation-Based Validation Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Clinical Triage: Conformal Prediction and Ensemble Learning Applied to a Synthetic ICU Benchmark Cohort
evidence.comparator_used: Theoretical nominal coverage guarantee at each miscoverage level (no raw-prediction comparator)
evidence.outcome: Empirical coverage of conformal prediction sets versus the theoretical guarantee
evidence.effect: Coverage matched the theoretical guarantee at all tested miscoverage levels
evidence.quote: Conformal coverage matched the theoretical guarantee at all tested miscoverage levels.

evidence.title: Conformal Prediction for Risk-Controlled Medical Entity Extraction Across Clinical Domains
evidence.comparator_used: Raw LLM confidence scores, which the study reports as miscalibrated (underconfident on FDA labels, overconfident on radiology reports); no head-to-head numeric comparison with heuristic cutoffs is reported
evidence.outcome: Empirical coverage of correct entities in LLM-based medical entity extraction (FDA drug labels and MIMIC-CXR radiology reports)
evidence.effect: Achieved target coverage (>=90%) in both domains. Conformal thresholds varied by domain: tau approx 0.06 on FDA labels and up to 0.99 on radiology reports. Rejection rates were 9-13%.
evidence.tradeoff: 9-13% of extracted entities were rejected (deferred). Thresholds had to be calibrated separately per domain, extraction category and model, because miscalibration direction reverses across domains. Radiology reports needed very strict thresholds (up to 0.99).
evidence.quote: Despite this heterogeneity, conformal prediction achieves target coverage ($\geq 90\%$) in both settings with manageable rejection rates (9--13\%).

evidence.title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Conformal Predictor to Predict Sepsis Mortality Risk: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.comparator_used: AI model point predictions without conformal prediction
evidence.outcome: Error rate of predictions (internal validation, 90% confidence level)
evidence.effect: 10.5% errors (n=438/4187) with conformal prediction vs 34.6% errors (n=1449) for the AI model without conformal prediction; 1229 (29.4%) predictions flagged for clinician review
evidence.tradeoff: 29.4% of predictions required clinician review internally; on external validation 38.6% (n=4004) were flagged for review due to interdatabase heterogeneity
evidence.quote: In contrast, the AI model without conformal prediction made 1449 (34.6%) errors.

evidence.title: FairICP: identifying biases and increasing transparency at the point of care in post-implementation clinical decision support using inductive conformal prediction
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline model predictions without FairICP, plus four benchmark frameworks (unfairness mitigation methods)
evidence.outcome: Prediction accuracy and accuracy gap between privileged and unprivileged subpopulations across cardiac MRI, chest X-ray and dermatology imaging
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved by 7.2% and the accuracy gap between privileged and unprivileged subpopulations was reduced by 2.2% on average across all three datasets, compared with baseline
evidence.quote: Compared to the baseline, FairICP improved prediction accuracy by 7.2% and reduced the accuracy gap between the privileged and unprivileged subpopulations by 2.2% on average across all three datasets.

evidence.title: Improving the reliability of polygenic risk score-based prediction for cardiovascular and renal complications across ancestries in type 2 diabetes using Mondrian Cross-Conformal Prediction
evidence.comparator_used: Logistic regression/probability-based stratification using multi-polygenic risk scores without Mondrian Cross-Conformal Prediction
evidence.outcome: Predictive performance and reliability/uncertainty-aware prediction across ancestries for nephropathy, stroke, and myocardial infarction in type 2 diabetes
evidence.effect: MCCP did not improve performance; it issued per-individual confidence and credibility, allowed a tolerated error level to be set in advance, delivered prediction sets respecting it in the majority of settings, and flagged individuals for whom no reliable prediction could be made. No numerical performance effect reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: On top of this baseline, MCCP did not improve performance but added capabilities absent from probability-based stratification: for each individual, it issued a prediction together with an explicit confidence and credibility level; it allowed a tolerated error level to be set in advance and delivered prediction sets respecting it in the majority of settings; and it flagged individuals for whom no reliable prediction could be made.

evidence.title: CONRep: Uncertainty-Aware Vision-Language Report Drafting Using Conformal Prediction
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.comparator_used: Uncertain (or uncertain/highly uncertain) subgroup of the same model's outputs, as separated by conformal prediction at α = 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2. The study did not compare against raw point predictions or heuristic cutoffs.
evidence.outcome: Agreement with ground truth in certain vs uncertain subgroups: AUROC for label-based classification, and cosine similarity plus LLM-judged agreement scores and match rates for sentence-based impressions
evidence.effect: Label-based: certain subset had significantly higher AUROCs across multiple findings (P < 0.05). Sentence-based: certain cases had significantly greater semantic similarity (P < 0.001). The independent LLM evaluator also gave significantly higher agreement scores and match rates to certain cases (P < 0.001). No effect sizes are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: In the label-based experiments, the certain subset achieved significantly higher AUROCs across multiple findings (P < 0.05).

controls.question: Should we recalibrate model probabilities on our own data before using them, especially at a new site?
controls.control: Recalibrate predicted probabilities post hoc on local or expert-validated held-out data.

The model should be recalibrated locally before use, so local data are needed. Prospective impact evaluation has not yet been done.
AUC decreased slightly (0.947 to 0.940) after recalibration
