Virtually no cost in classification performance

evidence.title: Large-scale esophageal cancer screening through noncontrast computed tomography and artificial intelligence
evidence.comparator_used: EAGLE before/without calibration in a real-world cohort
evidence.outcome: False positives while preserving sensitivity
evidence.effect: Calibration in a real-world cohort (three centers, n = 35,402) reduced false positives by 72.7% while preserving sensitivity
evidence.quote: Calibration in a real-world cohort (three centers, n = 35,402) reduced false positives by 72.7% while preserving sensitivity; prospective hospital validation (n = 17,446) achieved a 42.2% PPV, and real-world low-dose screening (n = 10,959) reached 99.94% specificity.

evidence.title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
evidence.comparator_used: the original, uncalibrated VPM baseline hazard (O/E ratio before recalibration vs after bootstrap-validated recalibration)
evidence.outcome: Ratio of observed to expected recurrence events (calibration)
evidence.effect: Original VPM O/E ratio 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2-2.0), indicating underestimation; after recalibration of the baseline hazard, bootstrap-validated O/E ratio 1.03 (95% CI 0.55-1.74)
evidence.tradeoff: Recalibration was post hoc and validated only internally; authors state the recalibrated VPM should preferably be externally validated.
evidence.quote: Internal bootstrap validation of this recalibration step indicated an O/E ratio of 1.03 (95% CI 0.55–1.74) of the updated VPM.

evidence.title: Assessing Calibration and Bias of a Deployed Machine Learning Malnutrition Prediction Model within a Large Healthcare System
evidence.comparator_used: The deployed MUST-Plus model's original uncalibrated probabilities, compared with recalibrated probabilities across race, gender and year
evidence.outcome: Model calibration (intercept and slope) across patient subgroups
evidence.effect: Overall baseline calibration intercept was -1.25 (95% CI: -1.28, -1.22) and slope was 1.55 (95% CI: 1.51, 1.59). Recalibration improved calibration across race, gender, and year. No post-recalibration numbers are given in the text.
evidence.quote: Recalibration is effective at reducing miscalibration across all patient subgroups.

evidence.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for accurate detection of wrong blood in tube errors in hospitalized patients
evidence.comparator_used: Model probabilities before recalibration (uncalibrated model output)
evidence.outcome: Positive predictive value and net benefit (false positives) in WBIT detection
evidence.effect: Recalibration improved positive predictive value and net benefit by reducing false positives; all values remained ≥90 %; specificities 98-99 %. No specific numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Slight decrease in sensitivity, although all values remained ≥90 %.
evidence.quote: Recalibration improved positive predictive value and net benefit by reducing false positives, with a slight decrease in sensitivity, although all values remained ≥90 %.

evidence.title: A Natural Language Processing-Based Approach for Early Detection of Heart Failure Onset using Electronic Health Records
evidence.comparator_used: No recalibration (also compared with recalibration in the large)
evidence.outcome: Model calibration in the overall cohort and demographic subgroups
evidence.effect: Logistic recalibration significantly improved model calibration; no numerical values reported in the abstract
evidence.quote: Logistic recalibration significantly improved model calibration in the overall cohort and demographic subgroups.

evidence.title: Haemodynamic intolerance at the de-resuscitation decision in critically ill adults: development, temporal and external validation of a prediction model across two intensive care databases
evidence.comparator_used: Uncalibrated model probabilities applied without refitting in temporal and external (eICU-CRD) validation
evidence.outcome: Calibration of predicted risk of haemodynamic intolerance under temporal and geographic shift
evidence.effect: Uncalibrated predictions over-predicted when prevalence fell (temporal split) and under-predicted when it rose (external cohort); a single logistic recalibration largely corrected the shift in both directions. Discrimination was unchanged (GB AUROC 0.733 temporal, 0.767 external). No numeric post-recalibration calibration metrics were given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: The model should be recalibrated locally before use, so local data are needed. Prospective impact evaluation has not yet been done.
evidence.quote: In contrast, calibration shifted predictably with event prevalence — over-prediction when prevalence fell across the temporal split and under-prediction when it rose in the external cohort — while the calibration slope remained close to, or slightly below, one; a single logistic recalibration largely corrected the shift in both directions.

evidence.title: Development and External Validation of a Treatment-Adjusted Machine Learning Model to Support Risk-Informed Group-Based Depression Care for People Living with HIV in Uganda
evidence.comparator_used: Uncalibrated XGBoost predicted probabilities in external validation (before vs after Platt recalibration)
evidence.outcome: Calibration (Brier score, calibration slope) and discrimination (AUC) of XGBoost in external validation
evidence.effect: Brier score improved from 0.174 to 0.113; calibration slope from 7.533 to 1.093; AUC 0.947 before vs 0.940 after recalibration (strong discrimination preserved)
evidence.tradeoff: AUC decreased slightly (0.947 to 0.940) after recalibration
evidence.quote: Following Platt-recalibration, XGBoost showed the best overall performance, preserving strong discrimination (AUC 0.940) while improving the Brier score from 0.174 to 0.113 and the calibration slope from 7.533 to 1.093.

evidence.title: Using temporal recalibration to improve the calibration of risk prediction models in competing risk settings when there are trends in survival over time
evidence.comparator_used: Standard analysis (model fitted on the full dataset, with no account taken of improvements in survival over time); period analysis was a second comparator
evidence.outcome: 10-year calibration of predicted risk of death from colon cancer and total risk of death in patients diagnosed in 2005
evidence.effect: The standard approach over-estimated 10-year risk of colon cancer death and total risk of death; calibration was improved with temporal recalibration or period analysis. No numeric estimates were reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The 10-year calibration plots demonstrated that using the standard approach over-estimated the risk of death due to colon cancer and the total risk of death and that calibration was improved using temporal recalibration or period analysis.

evidence.title: Preoperative risk prediction models for acute kidney injury after noncardiac surgery: an independent external validation cohort study
evidence.comparator_used: Original, uncalibrated published model probabilities in the external validation cohort, before intercept and slope updates
evidence.outcome: Calibration (calibration plot) and clinical utility (net benefit) for predicting AKI after noncardiac surgery
evidence.effect: All 9 models showed some miscalibration before updating; 5 of 9 were well-calibrated after intercept and slope updates. The 3 models with fair discrimination (AUROC 0.71-0.75) consistently gave a positive net benefit after recalibration. Results held in the sensitivity analysis.
evidence.quote: All models exhibited some miscalibration; five of the nine models were well-calibrated after intercept and slope updates.

evidence.title: Breast Ultrasound AI Under Dataset Shift: A Patient-Leakage-Aware Benchmark
evidence.comparator_used: Uncalibrated (raw) model probabilities
evidence.outcome: External calibration (expected calibration error and negative log-likelihood)
evidence.effect: Mean external ECE fell from 0.180 to 0.150; mean external NLL fell from 0.848 to 0.682
evidence.quote: Temperature scaling improved calibration-related metrics, reducing mean external expected calibration error from 0.180 to 0.150 and mean external negative log-likelihood from 0.848 to 0.682.

evidence.title: Prevalence Shift and ICU Mortality Miscalibration Across Institutions
evidence.comparator_used: Uncorrected model probabilities from the MIMIC-IV-trained models applied to eICU hospitals (Platt scaling with 30% labeled local data was also benchmarked)
evidence.outcome: Expected Calibration Error across 185 eICU hospitals
evidence.effect: Mean ECE fell from 0.071–0.085 to 0.027–0.037 with Bayesian prevalence correction, comparable to Platt scaling with 30% labeled data (ECE 0.022–0.024). AUROC was not significantly correlated with ECE.
evidence.tradeoff: Prevalence correction left ECE slightly above Platt scaling with 30% labeled data (0.027–0.037 vs 0.022–0.024), but it needs only the local mortality rate and no labeled target data. It corrects only the prevalence-driven share of miscalibration (about 55–65%).
evidence.quote: A closed-form Bayesian prevalence correction requiring only the local mortality rate, and no labeled target data, reduced mean ECE from 0.071–0.085 to 0.027– 0.037, comparable to Platt scaling applied with 30% labeled data (ECE = 0.022–0.024).

evidence.title: Data leakage inflates reported accuracy of deep learning for kidney stone detection on CT: a leakage-free, calibrated and uncertainty-aware reassessment across three centers
evidence.comparator_used: uncalibrated model probabilities (before temperature scaling)
evidence.outcome: reliability/calibration of predicted probabilities
evidence.effect: Reported qualitatively as improved reliability; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Calibration and selective classification further improved reliability, and no sex disparity in sensitivity was found once results were pooled across patients, though one appeared spuriously at the image level.

evidence.title: Fair admission risk prediction with proportional multicalibration
evidence.comparator_used: Unprocessed (not post-processed) risk prediction models and multicalibration post-processing, as implied by the abstract; the abstract does not name the comparators explicitly
evidence.outcome: Calibration fairness (multicalibration and differential calibration) across intersectional patient groups in ED admission prediction, and classification performance
evidence.effect: No numbers reported in the abstract; PMC post-processing controlled simultaneous measures of calibration fairness over intersectional groups
evidence.tradeoff: Virtually no cost in classification performance
evidence.quote: We observe that proportional multicalibration is a promising criteria for controlling simultaneous measures of calibration fairness of a model over intersectional groups with virtually no cost in terms of classification performance.

evidence.title: A selective deep learning framework for pressure injury staging with calibrated confidence and automated clinical documentation
evidence.comparator_used: Uncalibrated classifier probabilities before post-hoc temperature scaling
evidence.outcome: Expected calibration error on the test set
evidence.effect: Expected calibration error fell from 0.101 to 0.063
evidence.quote: Temperature scaling reduced test expected calibration error from 0.101 to 0.063.

evidence.title: Unsupervised Detection and Correction of Model Calibration Shift at Test-Time
evidence.venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
evidence.comparator_used: Sepsis prediction model with the calibration shift estimation/correction model versus the same sepsis prediction model without the calibration shift estimation model on two external validation cohorts.
evidence.outcome: Achieved positive predictive value (PPV) relative to a predefined 20% PPV target.
evidence.effect: When trained to achieve a PPV of 20%, PPV was 18.0% vs 12.9% and 23.1% vs 13.4% at the two external validation cohorts, respectively.
evidence.quote: For instance, when trained to achieve a PPV of 20%, the performance of the sepsis prediction model with and without the calibration shift estimation model was 18.0% vs 12.9% and 23.1% vs 13.4% at the two external validation cohorts, respectively.

evidence.title: Demographic Calibration Gaps in Breast Cancer Risk Prediction: Introducing the Demographic Calibration Gap Score
evidence.comparator_used: No calibration (uncalibrated base classifier probabilities), across five classifiers on the MIMIC-IV external cohort
evidence.outcome: Demographic Calibration Gap Score (DCGS) across racial and gender subgroups, relative to the 0.05 clinical significance threshold
evidence.effect: DCGS exceeded the 0.05 threshold in 28 of 40 model-calibration combinations on the race axis. Neither global Platt scaling nor isotonic regression reliably brought DCGS below the threshold.
evidence.quote: Neither global Platt nor isotonic calibration reliably reduced DCGS below that threshold.

evidence.title: Uncertainty-Aware Prediction Across Endoscopic Domains: Laryngeal Narrow-Band and Gastrointestinal Imaging
evidence.comparator_used: Uncalibrated model probabilities under resolution shift
evidence.outcome: Calibration (expected calibration error) under acquisition shift
evidence.effect: ECE 0.172 to 0.036 with temperature scaling and to 0.017 with isotonic regression
evidence.tradeoff: Recalibration does not recover discrimination, and residual confident-wrong predictions remain, so selective prediction is still needed.
evidence.quote: Target-domain recalibration substantially restores calibration under shift (ECE 0.172 → 0.036 with temperature scaling; → 0.017 with isotonic regression) but does not recover discrimination; selective prediction is complementary, mitigating residual confident-wrong predictions.

evidence.title: Decoupled Transferability of Calibration and Explainability in Cross-Cohort Breast Cancer Survival Prediction
evidence.comparator_used: Uncalibrated model probabilities on the SEER test set; the SEER-fit calibrators were also applied unchanged to the METABRIC cohort
evidence.outcome: Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on the SEER test set after post hoc recalibration
evidence.effect: Isotonic regression reduced SEER test ECE by 50–92% across all seven models. SEER-fit calibrators applied unchanged to METABRIC increased ECE by a factor of two to three for every model.
evidence.tradeoff: Calibrators fit on SEER did not transfer to METABRIC because of the base-rate shift (84.7% to 42.1% alive). Per-cohort recalibration on a labeled target sample is therefore needed. The study recommends this but did not test it.
evidence.quote: Isotonic regression reduced SEER test ECE by 50–92% across all seven models.

evidence.title: The Independence of Discrimination and Calibration in Clinical Risk Prediction: Lessons from a Multi-Timeframe Diabetes Prediction Framework
evidence.comparator_used: No uncalibrated-model arm reported; the calibrated framework was compared with QDiabetes-2018 run on the same synthetic cohort
evidence.outcome: Calibration (ECE and calibration-in-the-large O:E ratio) after isotonic recalibration on a held-out calibration set
evidence.effect: ECE = 0.006, but mean predicted risk was 8.4% vs observed 5.6% (O:E = 0.66, 95% CI 0.65-0.67), with overprediction in 9 of 10 risk deciles; QDiabetes-2018 had O:E = 0.89 and AUC 0.831 vs the framework's 0.844
evidence.tradeoff: Low bin-level ECE masked systematic 50% overprediction; recalibration on the deployment population is still likely to be needed.
evidence.quote: This miscalibration occurred despite isotonic regression on a held-out calibration set.

evidence.title: Signal Fidelity Index-aware calibration for addressing distributional shift in predictive modeling across heterogeneous real-world data
evidence.comparator_used: uncalibrated predictions and established baseline calibration methods, including isotonic regression and Platt scaling
evidence.outcome: predictive performance across six phenotypes, including F1-score, AUC, and Brier score decomposition
evidence.effect: Cohen's d = 0.603-5.002; F1-score gains ranging from +4.2% for fibromyalgia to +34.9% for dementia; AUC gains ranging from +4.7% to +40.1%; reliability reductions ranging from 11% to 29% and resolution increases ranging from +35% to +238%; isotonic regression AUC values degraded to 0.51-0.56 across all phenotypes
evidence.tradeoff: Requires supervised parameter development once per phenotype, followed by label-free deployment to target populations.
evidence.quote: SFI-aware calibration significantly improved predictive performance against both uncalibrated predictions and all baseline methods across nearly all six phenotypes (Cohen's d = 0.603-5.002, [Formula: see text]).

evidence.title: Trustworthy LLM-Embedding Clinical Prediction: Calibrating Confidence and Transparency for Foundation Model-Based Disease Risk Scores
evidence.comparator_used: Trust score without the confidence calibration component (uncalibrated classifier confidence) in the ablation
evidence.outcome: Expected calibration error (ECE) and clinician override rate
evidence.effect: ECE 0.007 with calibration vs. 0.024 without; override rate essentially unchanged (3.57% vs. 3.49%)
evidence.quote: Systematic ablation identified embedding-space similarity as the architecturally critical trust component: its removal increased override rates from 3.57% to 77–81% across all model sizes, while confidence calibration improved ECE (0.007 vs. 0.024) without meaningfully altering override behavior (3.57% vs. 3.49%).

evidence.title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
evidence.comparator_used: uncalibrated model probabilities under external validation
evidence.outcome: probability reliability (calibration) on the external dataset
evidence.effect: Post-hoc isotonic recalibration improved probability reliability after severe probability collapse in the Osteopenia class; no numeric values reported in the abstract
evidence.quote: Post-hoc recalibration improved probability reliability, while class-prior boosting substantially increased Osteopenia sensitivity and improved balanced accuracy and macro F1-score under external validation conditions.

evidence.title: Generalizable calibrated machine learning models for real-time atrial fibrillation risk prediction in ICU patients
evidence.comparator_used: Direct external validation of the model without recalibration (uncalibrated probabilities) on MIMIC-IV and GUH
evidence.outcome: External-validation discrimination (AUC) for ICU atrial fibrillation risk prediction
evidence.effect: Direct external validation AUCs reached 0.77 (internal validation AUC 0.81); recalibration gave performance matching or exceeding internal validation
evidence.quote: However, recalibration resulted in performances matching or exceeding that of the internal validation.

controls.question: Should we tune decision cutoffs for our population, use case, and each model version instead of using a fixed vendor default?
controls.control: Set AI score cutoffs on local validation data per model version, setting, subgroup, or intended purpose.
controls.comparator: Single fixed vendor or developer default threshold reused everywhere
controls.aim: Keep sensitivity and specificity appropriate across sites, subgroups, and model updates
variants: Retune per model size or quantization state
Purpose-specific cutoffs, e.g., screening versus confirmation
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction

evidence.title: Real-World Artificial Intelligence-Based Electrocardiographic Analysis to Diagnose Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
evidence.comparator_used: Alternative HCM probability thresholds (≥0.95, ≥0.90, ≥0.85) of the same AI-ECG algorithm, evaluated on local real-world data
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance for HCM (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, PPV) by probability threshold
evidence.effect: Threshold ≥0.85: sensitivity 95%, specificity and accuracy all >98%. Threshold ≥0.95: highest PPV (66%) but sensitivity only 50%.
evidence.tradeoff: A higher threshold raised PPV but cut sensitivity to 50%. The most sensitive threshold (≥0.85) had a lower PPV. Of 1,265 flagged patients, 54.6% had an alternate non-HCM diagnosis.
evidence.quote: HCM probability threshold of ≥0.85 provided the highest sensitivity (95%) for diagnosis of HCM with high specificity and accuracy (all >98%).

evidence.title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
evidence.comparator_used: a lower confidence cutoff of 0.8 versus a higher cutoff of 0.9 in the external cohort (different centers)
evidence.outcome: accuracy of semi-automated lineage prediction in the external cohort with a raised confidence cutoff
evidence.effect: External cohort: cutoff 0.8 yielded 86.0% accuracy; raising to 0.9 improved accuracy to 95.1%, statistically comparable to full IHC/manual evaluation (p=0.293), with workload reduction of 39.3%.
evidence.tradeoff: Higher cutoff reduces workload savings to 39.3%.
evidence.quote: Under this scenario, although the workload reduction was only 39.3%, the accuracy significantly improved to 95.1%.

evidence.title: Customizing AI-based screening with real-world data: Practical insights from diabetic retinopathy
evidence.comparator_used: Unmodified RetCAD with the manufacturer's default DR score cut-offs, compared with a threshold set on local data (Youden-index-adjusted, and the 'Greifswald modification' referral threshold of DR score >0.1)
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity for more than mild DR, and number of severe and moderate DR cases missed
evidence.effect: Diagnosable patients: sensitivity for more than mild DR rose from 70.41% (unmodified) to 86.89% (Youden-adjusted) and 93.63% (Greifswald). All patients: 60.06% to 74.14% to 79.87%. Severe DR missed: 13 (unmodified), 8 (Youden-adjusted), 2 (Greifswald). Moderate DR missed: 67 (unmodified) vs 13 (Greifswald).
evidence.tradeoff: Specificity fell: 93.86% to 82.67% (Youden) to 69.06% (Greifswald) in diagnosable patients, and 90.38% to 79.62% to 66.5% in all patients. The reduction in ophthalmologist exams shrank from 78.49% to 67.13% to 55.36%. The threshold was derived on a single-centre population and may not transfer to other populations.
evidence.quote: Under this scenario, 2 severe DR cases and 13 moderate DR cases would be missed compared to 13 severe DR and 67 moderate DR cases with unmodified RetCAD screening.

evidence.title: Stratified Care in Cognitive Behavioural Therapy: A Comparative Evaluation of Predictive Modelling Approaches for Individualized Treatment: La stratification des soins pour l'orientation vers une thérapie cognitivo-comportementale: une évaluation comparative des approches de modélisation prédictive pour un traitement individualisé
evidence.venue: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
evidence.comparator_used: Fixed 0.5 probability cut-off for assigning case complexity
evidence.outcome: Prediction accuracy of case complexity (standard vs complex) for stratifying patients to high- or low-intensity CBT
evidence.effect: Accuracy 0.749 with the ROC-derived cut-off vs 0.690 with the 0.5 cut-off
evidence.tradeoff: The models showed large sensitivity and specificity trade-offs that change the rates of assignment to high-intensity CBT, so the choice of cut-off matters when implementing the models.
evidence.quote: The ROC cut-off achieved the highest prediction accuracy of case complexity (0.749).

evidence.title: TOWARDS AN AI-DRIVEN REGISTRY FOR POSTOPERATIVE COMPLICA-TIONS: A PROOF-OF-CONCEPT STUDY EVALUATING THE OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES OF AI-MODELS
evidence.comparator_used: Two purpose-specific threshold sets compared with each other: one optimized for PPV (F-score 0.5) and one for sensitivity (F-score 2). No fixed vendor default was tested.
evidence.outcome: Detected postoperative complication counts and rates, and hospital-level comparisons
evidence.effect: The NLP models detected 8,512 PCs (9.14%) with the PPV-optimized thresholds and 15,892 PCs (17.1%) with the sensitivity-optimized thresholds. Trends over time were mostly stable or increasing under both settings. Threshold selection significantly influenced the regression findings.
evidence.tradeoff: Neither setting is better overall. The choice of threshold changes the observed complication rates and hospital rankings, so it has to match the surveillance purpose and be reported with PPV-sensitivity curves.
evidence.quote: Regression analyses demonstrated that threshold se-lection significantly influenced findings, impacting hospital comparisons.

evidence.title: Impact of Different Mammography Systems on Artificial Intelligence Performance in Breast Cancer Screening
evidence.comparator_used: Prespecified (vendor/developer) decision threshold reused at the new site, versus locally calibrated and software-version-specific thresholds
evidence.outcome: Recall rate of AI algorithm (and cancer detection with calibrated thresholds)
evidence.effect: Recall rate 48.3% (21 929 of 45 444) with prespecified threshold vs 13.0% (5896 of 45 444) after threshold calibration; observed service level 5.0% (2774 of 55 916). Recall rates increased approximately threefold after a mammography software upgrade, requiring per-software version thresholds. With software-specific thresholds AI would have recalled 277 of 303 (91.4%) screen-detected cancers and 47 of 138 (34.1%) interval cancers.
evidence.tradeoff: Even after calibration, AI recall rate (13.0%) remained well above the observed service recall level (5.0%); thresholds need re-derivation after each software upgrade.
evidence.quote: The prespecified threshold resulted in high recall rates (48.3%, 21 929 of 45 444), which reduced to 13.0% (5896 of 45 444) following threshold calibration, closer to the observed service level (5.0%, 2774 of 55 916).

evidence.title: Expert Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Trial Matching Solution Using Real-World Data From Patients With Cancer
evidence.comparator_used: Predefined trial-level eligibility threshold of 0.40 versus a lower threshold of 0.13 chosen to maximize sensitivity
evidence.outcome: Trial-level eligibility sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV
evidence.effect: At 0.40: sensitivity 78.3%, specificity 98.5%, PPV 92.6%, NPV 94.8%. At 0.13: sensitivity 98.7%, specificity 97.6%, PPV 91.2%, NPV 99.7%.
evidence.tradeoff: The lower threshold slightly reduced specificity (98.5% to 97.6%) and PPV (92.6% to 91.2%).
evidence.quote: A lower threshold (0.13) maximized sensitivity (98.7%), while maintaining high specificity at 97.6%, PPV at 91.2%, and NPV at 99.7%.

evidence.title: Implementation of a net benefit parameter in ROC curve decision thresholds for AI-powered mammography screening
evidence.comparator_used: Cutoff threshold determined by Youden's index on the ROC curve (compared using McNemar's test), not a fixed vendor default
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity, false-negative, false-positive and true-positive rates at the decision threshold for AI screening mammography across three AI models
evidence.effect: Replacing the Youden index with the net benefit method gave a threefold reduction in false-positive rates, a twofold reduction in false-negative rates and a twofold increase in true-positive rates. Sensitivity rose to 99% (maximum) versus 72% (maximum) with Youden's index.
evidence.tradeoff: Specificity fell to 48% (minimum) with the net benefit method versus 75% (minimum) with Youden's index.
evidence.quote: Thus, the sensitivity at the cutoff threshold determined by NB increased to 99% (maximum) compared to the sensitivity determined by Youden's index threshold (72% maximum).

evidence.title: Comparison of different Lunit INSIGHT CXR software versions when reading chest radiographs for tuberculosis
evidence.comparator_used: Single fixed cut-off threshold optimized for the older software version (v3.1.0.0) reused on the newer version (v3.9.0.1)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of Lunit INSIGHT CXR for TB detection at clinically relevant cut-offs, against Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra
evidence.effect: With the old version's threshold, the newer software was significantly less accurate than its predecessor. After re-calibrating the cut-off, there were no significant differences in sensitivity and specificity between versions. No numeric values for the threshold comparison were given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: When using an cut-off threshold optimized for the older software version, the newer software was significantly less accurate than its predecessors.

evidence.title: Optimizing Artificial Intelligence Thresholds for Mammographic Lesion Detection: A Retrospective Study on Diagnostic Performance and Radiologist-Artificial Intelligence Discordance
evidence.comparator_used: single fixed AI score threshold (≥35) applied across all lesion categories
evidence.outcome: diagnostic accuracy of AI mammographic lesion detection (ROC/Youden-derived thresholds) and radiologist-AI discordance
evidence.effect: Optimal threshold 19 for BI-RADS 4A (AUC = 0.685) and 63 for BI-RADS 4B/4C (AUC = 0.908). With the fixed cutoff of 35, discordant BI-RADS 4A lesions with scores ≥35 had a 43.8% malignancy rate, and BI-RADS 4B/4C lesions with scores <35 had a 19.5% malignancy rate.
evidence.tradeoff: BI-RADS 4A cases still show overlapping scores and limited discrimination (AUC 0.685), so radiologist oversight is still needed. The study was retrospective, with 194 mammograms.
evidence.quote: Using category-specific AI thresholds improves diagnostic accuracy and supports radiologist decision-making.

evidence.title: Deep learning for pediatric chest x-ray diagnosis: Repurposing a commercial tool developed for adults
evidence.comparator_used: Vendor-recommended adult thresholds applied to children
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance (sensitivity and specificity) of the AI tool for relevant chest radiograph findings in children
evidence.effect: With the adult threshold, older children (7-14 years) had AUC 0.96 (95% CI 0.94-0.98), sensitivity 87.5% and specificity 82.3%; performance 'further increased' with optimized pediatric thresholds (no numbers given in the abstract)
evidence.quote: In stratified analysis by age (2-7 vs. 7-14-years-old) a significantly higher performance (p < 0.001) was found for older children with an AUC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.94-0.98) with a sensitivity and specificity of 87.5% and 82.3% respectively, which further increased using optimized thresholds for children.

evidence.title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
evidence.comparator_used: Vendor default operating threshold of 0.15 versus a locally customised threshold of 0.10 on local primary care CXR data
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and negative predictive value for a safety-focused AI co-triage workflow
evidence.tradeoff: Specificity was 71.7% (95% CI 67.3% to 76.1%) at the lower threshold, which the authors judged acceptable for minimising false negatives. The abstract gives no specificity at the default threshold and does not report the change in operational improvement.
evidence.quote: Lowering the threshold to 0.10 increased sensitivity to 93.2% (95% CI 90.7% to 95.5%) and NPV to 91.3% (95% CI 88.2% to 94.3%), with specificity of 71.7% (95% CI 67.3% to 76.1%).

evidence.title: Doctor's Orders-Why Radiologists Should Consider Adjusting Commercial Machine Learning Applications in Chest Radiography to Fit Their Specific Needs
evidence.comparator_used: Single fixed operating threshold for all diseases (no explicit head-to-head with the vendor default; study explored adjusted thresholds per disease and screening scenario)
evidence.outcome: Rule-out capacity and workload reduction with adjusted thresholds in screening
evidence.effect: About 40% of cases correctly ruled out when screening for a single disease at sensitivity above 95% (exploratory analysis); optimized threshold gave overall sensitivity 85% and specificity 75.4%, AUC 0.84; for combined reading of all abnormalities only marginal workload reduction was achieved
evidence.tradeoff: Insufficient specificity limited workload reduction for combined multi-disease reading; performance varied by sex, age and comorbidity (possible bias in elderly and women); human supervision still required
evidence.quote: About 40% of cases could be ruled out correctly when screening for only one specific disease with a sensitivity above 95% in the exploratory analysis.

evidence.title: The Role of AI-Based Software BrainScan in the Interpretation of Non-Contrast Head CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke: An External Validation Study
evidence.comparator_used: Default (vendor) AI score threshold, which gave ischemia sensitivity 59.2% and specificity 99.8%
evidence.outcome: Ischemia detection sensitivity on non-contrast head CT
evidence.effect: Sensitivity rose from 59.2% (95% CI 52.1-66.1) at the default threshold to 86.1% at the Youden-optimal threshold of 0.055; AUC 0.930 (0.906-0.954)
evidence.tradeoff: Negligible specificity loss reported. The threshold was derived on the same cohort, and the authors call for multicentre validation and site-specific recalibration.
evidence.quote: The Youden-optimal threshold (0.055) recovered sensitivity to 86.1% with negligible specificity loss, reflecting a markedly bimodal score distribution.

evidence.title: Validation of several TB-CAD chest-X-ray applications in individuals with presumptive TB visiting peripheral health institutes in Delhi State
evidence.comparator_used: Vendor-recommended threshold score for qXR compared with the locally derived optimal threshold
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity for TB detection at different qXR threshold scores
evidence.effect: Sensitivity increased with minimal loss in specificity using the vendor recommended threshold; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Minimal loss in specificity
evidence.quote: Sensitivity increased with minimal loss in specificity when using the vendor recommended threshold.

evidence.title: Multi-label arrhythmia classification from Holter scatter plots using deep learning and clinically oriented thresholds
evidence.comparator_used: Single fixed decision threshold of 0.5 applied to all rhythm labels
evidence.outcome: Mean specificity and macro-F1 across 15 rhythm labels
evidence.effect: Mean specificity rose from 0.844 (0.822–0.865) to 0.885 (0.860–0.909); macro-F1 fell from 0.738 (0.666–0.774) at fixed 0.5 threshold to 0.693 (0.628–0.726)
evidence.tradeoff: Overall macro-F1 was lower with clinically oriented thresholds, so higher specificity came at the cost of overall F1 balance.
evidence.quote: Clinically oriented thresholds increased mean specificity from 0.844 (0.822–0.865) to 0.885 (0.860–0.909), but reduced macro-F1 to 0.693 (0.628–0.726).

evidence.title: Alert Policy and Rare-Event Metrics for Seven-Day-Ahead Agitation Forecasting in Passive Dementia Monitoring
evidence.comparator_used: Default 0.5 threshold versus F1-optimized thresholds set on the validation set for each model (LSTM 0.6463; GRU 0.7060; BiLSTM+Attention 0.5931)
evidence.outcome: Precision (PPV), recall and alert burden for seven-day-ahead agitation alerts
evidence.effect: Default thresholds gave 20–23% precision with 94–100% recall; optimized thresholds gave 73–82% precision with 56.25% recall (BiLSTM: accuracy 91.15%, F1 0.667). At test scale, optimized BiLSTM gave roughly one alert per 6–7 flagged days versus one per 2–3 under default, cutting expected false alarms by more than half.
evidence.tradeoff: Sensitivity fell from 94–100% at the default threshold to 56.25% at the optimized thresholds, so more agitation episodes are missed.

evidence.title: An analysis of the real world performance of an artificial intelligence based autism diagnostic
evidence.comparator_used: Same device with abstention thresholds loosened to give larger determinate rates, up to 100% (no abstention, always a best-guess output)
evidence.outcome: PPV, NPV, sensitivity and specificity of determinate outputs versus determinate rate
evidence.effect: At the selected thresholds, the determinate rate was 63.0% with PPV 92.44%, NPV 97.56%, sensitivity 99.1% and specificity 81.63%. Raising the determinate rate to 81.4% cut indeterminates from 95 to 49, raised false positives from 9 to 22 and false negatives from 1 to 4, and PPV dropped significantly (p=0.039). At 94.7%, PPV and sensitivity dropped significantly (p=0.042). Lowering the determinate rate to 20.9% gave 100% on all four metrics. Raising it to 72.0% significantly improved the determinate rate without a significant accuracy loss.
evidence.tradeoff: 37% of cases got no determinate output. Stricter thresholds leave fewer children with a result (52.97% would be a significantly lower determinate rate, p=0.047). Of the indeterminate cases, 29.8% had a positive reference-standard autism diagnosis and 88.3% had a noted risk of another neurodevelopmental condition.
evidence.quote: Restricting determinate outputs to the 63.0% of cases with sufficient certainty prevents the degradation of device performance that is seen when adjusting abstention thresholds to allow for larger determinate rates.

evidence.title: Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty

evidence.outcome: Model uncertainty and safer abstention behaviour
evidence.effect: Explicit abstention options consistently increased model uncertainty and safer abstention, far more than input perturbations; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Notably, providing explicit abstention options consistently increases model uncertainty and safer abstention, far more than input perturbations, while scaling model size or advanced prompting brings little improvement.

evidence.title: Intent Drift in LLM-Assisted BCI Communication: An In-Silico Benchmark Under Simulated Decoder Corruption
evidence.comparator_used: Other correction strategies in a six-strategy, seven-model subanalysis (permissive, alternatives, or expansion strategies versus conservative editing or abstention)
evidence.outcome: Intent drift (wrong message) in LLM-corrected simulated BCI text
evidence.effect: Conservative editing or abstention lowered drift, while alternatives or expansion raised it. No strategy eliminated drift, and even the best still produced a wrong message in 18 of 100 corrections. Per-strategy numbers are not given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: A separate subanalysis of six correction strategies (original seven-model panel) found no strategy removed drift: conservative editing or abstention lowered it, while alternatives or expansion raised it.

evidence.title: Quantifying and Mitigating Premature Closure in Frontier LLMs
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline prompting with no safety orientation, where models were not told they could abstain, clarify or escalate
evidence.outcome: Premature closure (false-action rate or inappropriate answers) on MedQA and AfriMed-QA with the correct option removed, and on HealthBench and physician-authored adversarial queries
evidence.effect: Safety-oriented prompting reduced premature closure across models, but residual failure persisted. Baseline false-action rates were 55-81% (MedQA) and 53-82% (AfriMed-QA). Baseline inappropriate answers averaged 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 adversarial queries. Post-prompting numbers are not given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Residual premature closure persisted despite the prompting. No cost, latency or over-refusal data are reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Safety-oriented prompting reduced premature closure across models, but residual failure persisted, highlighting the need to evaluate whether medical LLMs know when not to answer.

evidence.title: Ask Before You Diagnose: Safe-Psych, a Sequential Evaluation Benchmark for LLMs in Psychiatry
evidence.comparator_used: Standard prompting without safety-aware instructions, where models are not explicitly guided toward abstaining or clarifying
evidence.outcome: Premature commitment (under-abstention) versus excessive abstention
evidence.effect: Under-abstention exceeded 60% for most models; safety-aware prompting reduced premature commitment only by shifting errors toward excessive abstention (no figures given in the abstract)
evidence.tradeoff: New failure mode: excessive abstention replaces premature diagnosis
evidence.quote: Our findings show that capability does not ensure calibration: even strong models struggle under incomplete clinical information, with under-abstention exceeding 60% for most models and safety-aware prompting reducing premature commitment only by shifting errors toward excessive abstention.

evidence.title: Navigating uncertainty matters: Evaluating large language models for drug-drug interaction identification
evidence.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot baseline prompt without uncertainty-acknowledgment or refusal encouragement, compared with 3 prompt formats including a patient safety-focused mitigation prompt
evidence.outcome: Refusal Index (alignment between refusal behavior and likelihood of error)
evidence.effect: RI ranged 0.104-0.574 across models (weak to moderate alignment). Mitigation prompts had inconsistent effects on RI and did not reliably recalibrate uncertainty behavior. Qwen3-32B and GPT-4o-mini increased refusal rates under mitigation prompting.
evidence.tradeoff: Refusals increased under mitigation prompting but not in cases where responses were more likely to be incorrect, so extra refusals were not well targeted at errors.
evidence.quote: Prompt-based mitigation strategies produced inconsistent effects on RI and did not reliably recalibrate uncertainty behavior.

evidence.title: Condence, Calibration, and Abstention in Small Open-Weight Language Models on Psychiatric Knowledge Questions: A Cross-Domain Replication
evidence.comparator_used: Same models forced to always answer (no abstention option), paired same-item analysis on 150 psychiatric MedMCQA items
evidence.outcome: Paired accuracy when an abstention option was offered vs. forced answering
evidence.effect: Only the 1.2B model showed a paired effect distinguishable from noise, and it was negative (−6.7 points, 95% CI [−12.7,−0.7]); the 7.6B model's paired effect reversed from a naive +0.8 to −5.3 points (95% CI [−9.3,−1.3]). Naive answered-item accuracy had suggested a modest benefit for three of four models.
evidence.tradeoff: Self-chosen abstentions were poorly targeted: 8 of the 7.6B model's 12 abstentions forfeited an item it would otherwise have answered correctly. Naive unpaired accuracy on answered items overstated the benefit.
evidence.quote: We read the surviving evidence as: miscalibration and weak error-detection are general properties of this model family; accuracy ranking is domain-dependent and should not be assumed to transfer; and a prompted abstention option is not a free safety improvement for any of the four models once evaluated with paired, coverage-aware statistics rather than naive answered-item accuracy.

evidence.title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering

evidence.effect: AUROC 0·41–0·66 for flagging errors with perplexity-based confidence; the token-level toolkit localised instability to mid-chain stages (40–70% of the normalised trajectory).

evidence.title: Uncertainty-aware extraction of clinical findings from Finnish EHRs using open large language models
evidence.comparator_used: No reliability scoring (correctly classified cases used as the reference)
evidence.outcome: Ability of consistency-based Shannon entropy across repeated calls to separate misclassified from correctly classified cases
evidence.effect: Entropy in misclassified cases was 2.4-3.4 times higher than in correctly classified cases
evidence.tradeoff: Requires 15 repeated calls per model per patient (five temperatures x three repeats).
evidence.quote: Entropy in misclassified cases was 2.4–3.4 times higher than in correctly classified cases.

evidence.title: Retrieving Evidence from EHRs with LLMs: Possibilities and Challenges
evidence.comparator_used: No reliability scoring (model confidence compared against faithfulness of summaries)
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness of LLM-generated evidence summaries (limiting hallucinations)
evidence.effect: Model confidence in outputs strongly correlates with faithful summaries (no numeric value given in the abstract)
evidence.quote: In this setting, however, we show that model confidence in outputs strongly correlates with faithful summaries, offering a practical means to limit confabulations.

evidence.title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
evidence.comparator_used: Unconstrained baseline (no semantic-entropy UQ gate)
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic precision
evidence.effect: 49.3% diagnostic precision for the full architecture, which includes the semantic entropy gate (K=5 samples), an absolute improvement of 11.3 percentage points over the unconstrained baseline. The abstract does not isolate the UQ gate's own contribution.
evidence.quote: The full architecture achieves 49.3% diagnostic precision, representing an absolute improvement of 11.3 percentage points over an unconstrained baseline.

evidence.title: Real-time hallucination detection and intervention in medical LLMs via calibrated hidden-state probes
evidence.comparator_used: multi-sample (consistency-based) baselines and post-hoc checking
evidence.outcome: Detection latency and lead time before error onset
evidence.effect: Probe latency ~10ms per answer versus ~10s for multi-sample baselines; trigger fires roughly 10-35 tokens before error onset versus zero lead time for a post-hoc check
evidence.quote: Probe latency is ∼10ms per answer versus ∼10s for multi-sample baselines.

evidence.title: Token Probabilities to Mitigate Large Language Models Overconfidence in Answering Medical Questions: Quantitative Study
evidence.comparator_used: LLM's verbalized self-rated confidence (expressed confidence rated 0 to 100)
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of response accuracy (AUROC) across 9 LLMs on USMLE MedQA questions
evidence.effect: Response token probability AUROCs ranged from 0.71 (95% CI 0.69-0.73) for Phi-3-Mini to 0.87 (95% CI 0.85-0.89) for GPT-4o, versus expressed confidence AUROCs of 0.52 (95% CI 0.50-0.53) for Phi-3-Mini to 0.68 (95% CI 0.65-0.71) for GPT-4o; all P<.001
evidence.tradeoff: All models still showed imperfect calibration with a general trend toward overconfidence.
evidence.quote: In contrast, the response token probability consistently outperformed expressed confidence for predicting response accuracy (AUROCs ranging from 0.71, 95% CI 0.69-0.73 for Phi-3-Mini to 0.87, 95% CI 0.85-0.89 for GPT-4o; all P<.001).

evidence.title: Semantic Consistency-Based Uncertainty Quantification for Factuality in Radiology Report Generation
evidence.comparator_used: No reliability scoring (unfiltered generated reports)
evidence.outcome: Hallucination detection and factual accuracy of generated radiology reports; flagging lowest-precision sentence
evidence.effect: Sentence-level uncertainty flags the lowest-precision sentence in each report with an 82.9% success rate; report-level filtering improves factuality by 10% at 20% rejection
evidence.quote: Furthermore, sentence-level uncertainty flags the lowestprecision sentence in each report with an 82.9% success rate.

evidence.title: Confidence Measurement Metrics in Multimodal Large Language Models for Ultrasound-Based Radiology Cases: Comparative Evaluation Study of Self-Reported, Consistency-Based, and Hybrid Methods
evidence.comparator_used: Self-reported (verbalized) confidence metrics (first and mean self-reported confidence), plus consistency-based metrics alone (relative entropy, majority-vote percentage)
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of correct vs incorrect answers (ROC AUC), Spearman correlation of confidence with accuracy, and calibration (ECE, Brier score)
evidence.effect: Top Weighted Score (hybrid of response frequency and self-reported confidence) was the only metric with significant correlations across all 4 models: Gemini-3-Pro ρ=0.52, GPT-5 ρ=0.43, Claude-4.5-Sonnet ρ=0.30, GPT-4o ρ=0.22. AUC 0.826 (95% CI 0.731-0.920) for Gemini-3-Pro and 0.767 (95% CI 0.668-0.866) for GPT-5. Lowest ECE in GPT-5 (0.098) and Claude-4.5-Sonnet (0.192); Gemini-3-Pro was comparable between relative entropy (0.119) and Top Weighted Score (0.122). It was the only significant metric in GPT-4o.
evidence.tradeoff: Consistency-based and hybrid metrics need 20 repeated outputs per case. Reasoning models required substantially longer processing times and higher token consumption than the general model. The authors call for resource-efficient sampling strategies, and association strength varied across models.
evidence.quote: Receiver operating characteristic analysis revealed that Top Weighted Score demonstrated the highest discriminative ability, with area under the curve values of 0.826 (95% CI 0.731-0.920) for Gemini-3-Pro and 0.767 (95% CI 0.668-0.866) for GPT-5.

evidence.title: On-premise medical AI agents for reliable clinical decision-making
evidence.comparator_used: Internal-likelihood and language-based reliability measures
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of diagnostic correctness (AUC)
evidence.effect: Diagnostic behavioral consistency AUC = 0.860, and AUC = 0.875 under stress testing
evidence.quote: Diagnostic behavioral consistency provided the strongest discrimination of correctness (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.860) and remained informative under stress testing (AUC = 0.875).

evidence.title: Hallucination filtering in radiology vision-language models using discrete semantic entropy
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline low-temperature (0.1) answers to all questions, with no reliability scoring
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic/VQA answer accuracy on retained questions after filtering by discrete semantic entropy
evidence.effect: DSE > 0.3 filter: GPT-4o accuracy 51.7% to 76.3% (334/706 retained); GPT-4.1 54.8% to 63.8% (499/706 retained); both p < 0.001
evidence.tradeoff: Many questions go unanswered (372/706 excluded for GPT-4o, 207/706 for GPT-4.1). Each question needs 15 sampled responses at temperature 1.0 plus bidirectional entailment clustering.
evidence.quote: After filtering out high-entropy questions (DSE > 0.3), accuracy on the remaining questions was 76.3% (retained questions: 334/706) for GPT-4o and 63.8% (retained questions: 499/706) for GPT-4.1 (both p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Learning the Phenotype of Medical Hallucinations
evidence.comparator_used: Unrefined GPT-4o answers without hallucination-probability-guided refinement
evidence.outcome: USMLE pass rate of GPT-4o
evidence.effect: Pass rate improved by five percentage points to 92.1%; compute significantly reduced; detection AUCs 0.95-0.98 across models and tasks
evidence.quote: As a practical application, we demonstrate that the hallucination probability signal from CHECK can guide an iterative refinement process, improving GPT-4o’s USMLE pass rate by five percentage points to a new state-of-the-art of 92.1\% while significantly reducing compute.

evidence.title: Measuring large language model uncertainty in women's health using semantic entropy and perplexity: a comparative study
evidence.venue: The Lancet. Obstetrics, gynaecology, & women's health
evidence.comparator_used: Perplexity (token-probability-based uncertainty score)
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of incorrect LLM responses (AUROC) to MRCOG obstetrics and gynaecology questions
evidence.effect: Full dataset (n=1670): AUROC 0·76 [95% CI 0·75-0·78] for semantic entropy vs 0·62 [0·60-0·65] for perplexity. Expert-validated subset (105 questions): 0·97 [0·91-1·00] vs 0·57 [0·405-0·68]. Discrete semantic entropy, which needs no model internals, performed similarly.
evidence.tradeoff: Semantic clustering, required for semantic entropy, succeeded in only 30% of questions, though it still gave informative uncertainty signals when incomplete. Each item was entered into the LLM ten times to compute the score.
evidence.quote: Semantic entropy showed superior discrimination of incorrect responses compared with perplexity (AUROC 0·76 [95% CI 0·75-0·78 vs 0·62 [0·60-0·65]).

evidence.title: From Attribution to Abstention: Training-Free Attention-Based Auditing for Clinical Summarization
evidence.comparator_used: Embedding-based confidence
evidence.outcome: Hallucination detection (AUROC)
evidence.effect: Attention-based groundedness scores reached 0.77 AUROC with the medical-finetuned model, described as competitive with embedding-based confidence at zero additional cost
evidence.quote: For hallucination detection, groundedness scores achieve 0.77 AUROC with the medical-finetuned model: competitive with embedding-based confidence at zero additional cost, and enable an abstention mechanism that improves faithfulness from 61.7% to 72.6% by withholding the least: grounded 20% of output for clinician review.

controls.question: Should disagreement between models or explanation methods trigger review, rather than relying on one model's confidence?
controls.control: Flag outputs for review when independent models or explanation methods disagree, or when outputs diverge from medical knowledge checks.
controls.comparator: A single model's confidence score alone
controls.aim: Detect unreliable outputs that single-model confidence misses
variants: Combine disagreement with confidence and similarity into one composite review score
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction
tradeoffs: Superficial explanations could do more harm than good by misleading physicians into relying on uncertain predictions.

evidence.title: Can physician judgment enhance model trustworthiness? A case study on predicting pathological lymph nodes in rectal cancer
evidence.comparator_used: standalone uncertainty estimation using only the variance of prediction probability
evidence.outcome: Model reliability / prediction uncertainty estimation for lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer
evidence.effect: No significant advantage of the human-in-the-loop estimate (variance plus quantified agreement between attention maps and physician understanding) over variance alone; no numbers given in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Superficial explanations could do more harm than good by misleading physicians into relying on uncertain predictions.
evidence.quote: Our findings revealed no significant advantage of the human-in-the-loop approach over the standalone one.

evidence.title: Comparative benchmarking of failure detection methods in medical image segmentation: Unveiling the role of confidence aggregation
evidence.comparator_used: Other failure detection methods based on a single model's confidence
evidence.outcome: Segmentation failure detection performance under test-time distribution shift
evidence.effect: Disagreement between ensemble predictions (pairwise Dice) performed best; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Our findings highlight the importance of pixel confidence aggregation and we observe superior performance of the pairwise Dice score (Roy et al., 2019) between ensemble predictions, positioning it as a simple and robust baseline for failure detection in medical image segmentation.

controls.question: Should the AI ask for clarification or explicitly flag gaps when input is incomplete or ambiguous, instead of answering as if it were complete?
controls.control: When inputs are ambiguous, missing, or stale, have the AI ask clarifying questions, or mark fields unknown and qualify its recommendation.
controls.comparator: AI gives an unqualified answer from incomplete input without seeking information
controls.aim: Prevent fabricated or overconfident outputs built on gaps in the input
variants: Active: trigger clarifying questions on ambiguity-driven uncertainty
Passive: downgrade recommendation strength when data are incomplete
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction
tradeoffs: Premature diagnoses made without clarification were less accurate than on-time diagnoses

evidence.title: Engineering framework for curiosity-driven and humble AI in clinical decision support
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLM responses without the BODHI framework (no structured uncertainty decomposition or virtue-based stance rules)
evidence.outcome: Rate of appropriate clarifying questions (context seeking) and overall clinical response quality on 200 HealthBench Hard vignettes
evidence.effect: Clarifying questions: 97.3% vs 7.8% (GPT-4.1-mini) and 73.5% vs 0.0% (GPT-4o-mini). Context seeking rate Cohen's d=16.38 and 19.54. Overall quality +16.6 pp (GPT-4.1-mini, p<0.0001, d=11.56) and +2.2 pp (GPT-4o-mini, p<0.0001, d=1.56).
evidence.quote: Crucially, 97.3% of GPT-4.1-mini responses and 73.5% of GPT-4o-mini responses included appropriate clarifying questions, compared with 7.8% and 0.0% at baseline, demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in eliciting information gathering behaviour.

evidence.title: Ask Before You Diagnose: Safe-Psych, a Sequential Evaluation Benchmark for LLMs in Psychiatry
evidence.comparator_used: Default prompting without explicit instruction to seek clarification
evidence.outcome: Rate of clarification-seeking under sequential, incomplete evidence
evidence.effect: Models rarely sought clarification unless explicitly prompted; no numbers given in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Premature diagnoses made without clarification were less accurate than on-time diagnoses
evidence.quote: In sequential evaluation, models frequently diagnose before sufficient evidence is available and rarely seek clarification unless explicitly prompted; these premature diagnoses are less accurate than on-time diagnoses.

evidence.title: Developing and Testing an Engineering Framework for Curiosity-Driven and Humble AI in Clinical Decision Support
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLM responses without the BODHI framework (no structured uncertainty decomposition or virtue-based stance rules)
evidence.outcome: Rate of appropriate clarifying questions / context-seeking in responses to HealthBench Hard vignettes
evidence.effect: 97.3% of GPT-4.1-mini responses and 73.5% of GPT-4o-mini responses included appropriate clarifying questions vs 7.8% and 0.0% at baseline; context-seeking rate Cohen's d = 16.38 and 19.54
evidence.quote: Crucially, 97.3% of GPT-4.1-mini responses and 73.5% of GPT-4o-mini responses included appropriate clarifying questions, compared to 7.8% and 0.0% at baseline, demonstrating the framework’s effectiveness in eliciting information-gathering behavior.

controls.question: Should we predefine conditions under which the AI goes silent or falls back to a safe mode?
controls.control: Predefine stop criteria (data completeness, operating conditions, failure triggers) that suppress AI output or switch to a safe fallback or human control.
controls.comparator: AI runs in all conditions without predefined stop or failure behavior
controls.aim: Prevent harmful outputs when operating conditions are unsafe or the AI fails
variants: Fallback to baseline or non-personalized policy
Automatic shutdown triggers with human takeover
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction
tradeoffs: Most visits had forecasts suppressed under strict requirements, mainly because of incomplete assessments, so fewer forecasts are available to clinicians.

evidence.title: A clinic-updated digital twin for Parkinson’s disease progression: Governed Bayesian forecasting with uncertainty-gated reporting
evidence.comparator_used: Strict three-domain gate requirements versus a validated partial-observation extension (no ungated comparator reported)
evidence.outcome: Proportion of visits at which governed forecasts were released, and the reasons for suppression
evidence.effect: Released at 32.7% of visits under strict three-domain requirements, rising to 48.1% under the partial-observation extension. Suppression was driven by incomplete clinical assessment (51.5%) rather than model uncertainty (0.2%). It was equitable across sexes (Cramér's V=0.049).
evidence.tradeoff: Most visits had forecasts suppressed under strict requirements, mainly because of incomplete assessments, so fewer forecasts are available to clinicians.
evidence.quote: The confidence gate released governed forecasts at 32.7% of visits under strict three-domain requirements, increasing to 48.1% under a validated partial-observation extension.

controls.question: Should the system abstain or warn when retrieved evidence is absent or below a defined similarity threshold?
controls.control: Require retrieved or verbatim evidence above a similarity threshold before answering; otherwise abstain or warn users.
controls.comparator: Answering from the model regardless of retrieved evidence
controls.aim: Reduce unsupported answers by abstaining or warning when an evidence-relevance check fails
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction
tradeoffs: Coverage dropped because of more abstentions and, for Gemini, more invalid outputs. Only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported, so the approach introduces new failure modes.
More abstentions and, for Gemini, more invalid outputs. Quotes introduce new failure modes: only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.
Correct judgments without valid verbatim evidence were downgraded to incomplete entries, which reduces apparent agreement

evidence.title: MedFabric: Gold Evidence Hides the Difficulty of Word-Level Medical Fabrication Detection
evidence.comparator_used: Answering from retrieved evidence regardless of its confidence (no retrieval-confidence gate)
evidence.outcome: Macro F1 for word-level medical fabrication detection
evidence.effect: Macro F1 rose from 61% to 74% with the retrieval-confidence gate
evidence.quote: The failure is actionable: a retrieval-confidence gate that abstains on low-confidence evidence raises macro F1 from 61% to 74%, and we release MedFabric, all code, and every baseline.

evidence.title: Show Your Work: Verbatim Evidence Requirements and Automated Assessment of Large Language Models for Biomedical Text Processing of Trial Eligibility Criteria
evidence.comparator_used: Label-only output without a required verbatim supporting quote (abstention allowed in both conditions)
evidence.outcome: Macro-F1 and coverage (non-invalid, non-abstained outputs) for trial eligibility-scope classification
evidence.effect: Coverage fell: GPT-5.2 86.2% to 84.3%, Gemini 3 flash preview 98.3% to 92.8%, Claude Opus 4.5 96.0% to 94.5%. Macro-F1 stayed high, with slight gains for GPT-5.2 and Gemini and a decrease for Claude. Labels were stable across repetitions (Fleiss' kappa 0.829 to 0.969).
evidence.tradeoff: Coverage dropped because of more abstentions and, for Gemini, more invalid outputs. Only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported, so the approach introduces new failure modes.
evidence.quote: Macro-F1 remained high but changed by model (slight gains for GPT-5.2 and Gemini, decrease for Claude).

evidence.title: Show Your Work: Verbatim Evidence Requirements and Automated Assessment for Large Language Models in Biomedical Text Processing
evidence.comparator_used: label-only prompt without a required verbatim supporting quote
evidence.outcome: coverage and conditional macro-F1 for trial eligibility-scope classification
evidence.effect: Coverage fell: GPT-5.2 86.2% to 84.3%, Gemini 98.3% to 92.8%, Claude 96.0% to 94.5%. Conditional macro-F1 changed by model: slight gains for GPT-5.2 and Gemini, a decrease for Claude. Labels were stable across repetitions (Fleiss' kappa 0.829 to 0.969).
evidence.tradeoff: More abstentions and, for Gemini, more invalid outputs. Quotes introduce new failure modes: only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.
evidence.quote: Evidence requirements modestly reduced coverage (GPT-5.2 86.2% to 84.3%, Gemini 98.3% to 92.8%, Claude 96.0% to 94.5%) by increasing abstentions and, for Gemini, invalid outputs.

evidence.title: A decision-basis contract for auditable LLM-assisted medical billing verification: deterministic rules, verbatim evidence, and fail-closed abstention
evidence.comparator_used: Raw model judgments without the verbatim evidence gate
evidence.outcome: Validity of evidence behind correct raw judgments and conversion to incomplete decision-basis entries
evidence.effect: Some correct raw judgments lacked valid evidence and were converted to incomplete entries; no counts given in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Correct judgments without valid verbatim evidence were downgraded to incomplete entries, which reduces apparent agreement
evidence.quote: The evidence gate also exposed cases in which correct raw judgments lacked valid evidence and were converted to incomplete decision-basis entries.

controls.question: Should we screen inputs for quality and refuse to analyze unusable scans or signals?
controls.control: Screen input quality first and refuse or flag ungradable images or signal segments before the model analyzes them.
controls.comparator: Analyzing all inputs regardless of quality
controls.aim: Avoid unreliable outputs from poor-quality images or signals
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction

evidence.title: Task-Specific Quality Gating for Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans: Learned Representations Over Scalar Metrics in Choroid Segmentation
evidence.comparator_used: hand-crafted scalar NR-IQA metrics (BRISQUE, NIQE, PIQE, SNR, PSNR) as quality gates; device-reported quality scores are cited as unreliable but not tested
evidence.outcome: Ability of the quality gate to predict whether a B-scan will yield a reliable choroid segmentation (ROC-AUC, correlation)
evidence.effect: Scalar NR-IQA metrics: |r| < 0.20. ImageNet-pretrained representations: ROC-AUC up to 0.77. RETFound (OCT-specific foundation model): ROC-AUC ≈ 0.81.
evidence.quote: General-purpose ImageNet-based pretrained representations (EfficientNet-b0, ResNet-50, ViT-B/16) improve upon NR-IQA, achieving ROC-AUC up to 0.77, indicating that learned representations are better suited to task-specific quality gating than hand-crafted scalar statistics.

controls.question: Should a learned policy decide which cases the AI defers to clinicians, instead of a simple confidence cutoff?
controls.control: Train or derive a deferral policy that decides case-by-case whether AI or clinician decides, based on their complementary strengths.
controls.comparator: Fixed confidence threshold or LLM-decided deferral
controls.aim: Improve combined human-AI accuracy by deferring cases where clinicians outperform the AI
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction

controls.question: Should uncertain cases be escalated from a cheap model to a stronger model or retrieval step instead of running the expensive path for everything?
controls.control: Route only uncertain cases from a small model to a larger LLM or retrieval-augmented generation based on uncertainty signals.
controls.comparator: Single model for all cases, or expensive model for all cases
controls.aim: Balance accuracy and cost by spending heavier computation only on uncertain cases
controls.family_label: confidence thresholds, abstention, calibrated deferral to a human, conformal prediction

controls.control: Assign the model an explicit role or persona, such as senior physician or a defined patient-facing chatbot character.
controls.comparator: Prompt with no assigned role or persona
controls.aim: Improve answer quality and appropriateness of model behavior for the clinical context
variants: Clinical role such as senior physician
Patient chatbot persona: doctor vs peer
controls.family_label: role, few-shot, chain-of-thought, structured, or optimized prompts and system instructions
tradeoffs: Structured prompt was more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias; no model reliably produced clinically usable summaries. Role was not tested in isolation from tone, task and format.

evidence.title: Prompting Pro Tips! Best Practices for Generating Clinical Narrative Summaries
evidence.comparator_used: Vague prompt without structured elements (structured prompt bundled role, task, tone and format)
evidence.outcome: Clinically adequate summary rate, with hallucinations and bias, across 8 LLMs and 8 scenarios
evidence.effect: Clinically adequate summary 39% structured vs 9% vague; conformance to instructions comparable (64% for both); structured more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias
evidence.tradeoff: Structured prompt was more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias; no model reliably produced clinically usable summaries. Role was not tested in isolation from tone, task and format.
evidence.quote: The structured approach was more likely to produce a clinically adequate summary (39% compared to 9%) but also more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.

evidence.title: Enhancing responses from large language models with role-playing prompts: a comparative study on answering frequently asked questions about total knee arthroplasty
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot prompting (question-only) with no assigned role
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, comprehensiveness (5-point Likert) and acceptability of LLM answers to TKA FAQs, rated by four orthopaedic surgeons
evidence.effect: Role-playing as an experienced orthopaedic surgeon significantly improved all metrics for ChatGPT-3.5 (P < 0.05) and acceptability for ChatGPT-4 (P = 0.033); no significant prompting effects for Gemini or Claude. ChatGPT-4 with role-playing scored accuracy 3.73, comprehensiveness 4.05, acceptability 77.5%; ChatGPT-3.5 with role-playing 3.70, 3.85, 72.5%.
evidence.quote: Within-model comparisons showed role-playing significantly improved all metrics for ChatGPT-3.5 (P < 0.05) and acceptability for ChatGPT-4 (P = 0.033).

evidence.title: Personas Shift Clinical Action Thresholds in Large Language Models
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline prompting with no assigned physician persona
evidence.outcome: Rate of affirmative ("Yes") answers on binary clinical action decisions (safety, autonomy, treatment, resource use, follow-up) under fixed clinical evidence
evidence.effect: Baseline 42.8% Yes; persona prompts shifted affirmative rates from 36.9% to 46.4%, a 9.5-percentage-point swing; largest in autonomy and treatment; 85.7% directional agreement across corpora, r = 0.82 for effect sizes
evidence.tradeoff: Personas shift clinical action thresholds with the clinical facts unchanged, so the prompt acts as a policy-setting layer; susceptibility varied by model (4.9–16.1 points). No accuracy outcome was reported.
evidence.quote: Persona prompts shifted affirmative rates from 36.9% to 46.4%, a 9.5–percentage-point swing under fixed clinical evidence.

evidence.title: Shaping AI in Pelvic Floor Physiotherapy: The Impact of Role-Play Prompting on ChatGPT Response Quality
evidence.comparator_used: Neutral prompt with no assigned role or persona
evidence.outcome: Physiotherapist-rated response quality (relevance, accuracy, comprehensiveness, clarity; 5-point rubric) for 21 pelvic floor physiotherapy questions
evidence.effect: Significant improvement across all domains (p < 0.001); mean differences: comprehensiveness 1.45, relevance 1.12, accuracy 0.88, clarity 1.48; Cohen's d 1.66-2.11; inter-rater ICC 0.61-0.81
evidence.tradeoff: Accuracy remains imperfect, so all generated responses still require careful professional oversight.
evidence.quote: Persona-based prompting significantly improved response quality across all domains (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: What Users Cannot See: Evaluating LLM Emotional Support Beyond User Preference
evidence.comparator_used: Default prompt with no assigned persona
evidence.outcome: Soothe (affective comfort), Reframe (cognitive perspective-shift) and Endorse (agreement with user's framing) in LLM emotional-support responses
evidence.effect: Friend and therapist personas both increased Soothe relative to default. Friend prompting increased Endorse and reduced Reframe; therapist prompting did the reverse. Lay raters rated the personas similarly helpful and desirable. No numeric effect sizes in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Friend persona increased Endorse and reduced Reframe, which could reinforce users' existing appraisals and plausibly contribute to escalation risk. Lay raters did not notice this.
evidence.quote: Across 9,000 GPT-5.6 responses to 3,000 venting and advice-seeking Reddit posts, friend- and therapist-style personas both increased Soothe relative to default but moved Reframe and Endorse in opposite directions: friend prompting increased Endorse and reduced Reframe, a pattern that could reinforce users' existing appraisals and plausibly contribute to escalation risk, whereas therapist prompting did the reverse.

evidence.title: A randomized factorial experiment to optimize the design of a culturally tailored breast cancer screening outreach chatbot intervention
evidence.comparator_used: Control chatbot condition (no assigned persona/communication style manipulation), compared with doctor vs breast cancer survivor Black woman personas crossed with direct vs polite style
evidence.outcome: Trust and intention to use the chatbot for scheduling breast cancer screening
evidence.effect: Doctor-polite condition was most preferred for both trust and intention to use compared with the control; no numeric estimates reported in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Qualitative feedback: some participants perceived the Black woman persona as stereotyping, patronizing, or targeting; caution needed to avoid perpetuating stereotypes
evidence.quote: Among the experimental conditions, the doctor-polite condition was the most preferred in terms of both trust and intention to use, compared with the control.

evidence.title: Decomposing Persona Prompts for Simulated Clinical Reasoning: A Two-by-Two Factorial In Silico Experiment of Time Pressure and Safety Prioritization
evidence.comparator_used: Alternative persona components: lean-efficiency optimization target (versus safety-first), and high versus low time-pressure framing. There was no no-persona arm.
evidence.outcome: Safety-net specificity in discharge plans and contraindication or sequencing violations in trap cases
evidence.effect: Safety-first improved safety-net specificity (mean 4.5 versus 2.6 on a five-point scale). Violations occurred only in the high/lean condition (8 of 56 runs, 14.3%). In trap cases, violations were 8 of 8 under high/lean and 0 of 24 in the other three conditions. Safety-first also increased proposed testing (beta = 1.32, p < 0.001) and diagnostic breadth (beta = 0.247, p < 0.001). High time pressure reduced proposed tests (beta = -1.05, p < 0.001) and diagnostic breadth (beta = -0.246, p < 0.001).
evidence.tradeoff: Safety-first prompting increased the number of proposed tests (beta = 1.32). High time-pressure framing narrowed diagnostic search and reduced testing, and the high/lean persona produced all the violations.
evidence.quote: Time-pressure framing narrowed diagnostic search and reduced proposed testing, whereas safety-first prompting improved safety-netting and prevented severe trap-case violations outside the high/lean condition.

evidence.title: The use of structured prompt to improve the readability, accuracy, and quality of ChatGPT responses on labor epidural analgesia: a brief report
evidence.comparator_used: Direct questions to ChatGPT-5.2 without a structured prompt (Role was one element of the bundled CRAFT prompt)
evidence.outcome: Readability and accuracy of chatbot responses on labor epidural analgesia (effect of the whole CRAFT bundle, not role alone)
evidence.effect: Direct-question responses ranged from 9th grade to college level; CRAFT responses ranged from 6th to 9th grade. Accuracy 99.8% ± 0.2% vs 99.0% ± 0.4%, P = 0.029. No significant differences in understandability or actionability.
evidence.quote: Accuracy was significantly higher in CRAFT-based prompt group than direct-question group (99.8% ± 0.2% vs. 99.0% ± 0.4%, P = 0.029).

evidence.title: Role-Prompting in Frontier Large Language Models Influences Clinical Reasoning in Complex Medical Cases
evidence.comparator_used: Other stakeholder role prompts (physician, patient) on the same cases; no unprompted, no-role baseline was tested
evidence.outcome: Alignment of LLM decisions with physician panel majority in cases with clear consensus
evidence.effect: Insurer role reduced alignment with physician majority by 50% for GPT-5.4 (p = 0.004), 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro (p = 0.008) and 10.5% (NS) for Opus 4.6
evidence.tradeoff: Insurer role shifted primary ethical values from beneficence (27%) to financial stewardship (20%) across all LLMs, with systematic denial of physician-endorsed, patient-preferred treatments
evidence.quote: Among 20 cases with clear physician consensus, LLMs prompted as an insurer reduced alignment with physician majority by 50% for GPT-5.4 (p = 0.004), 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro (p = 0.008) and 10.5% (NS) for Opus 4.6.

evidence.title: Persona system prompts reshape simulated clinical reasoning: a 2×2 factorial in-silico experiment decomposing time pressure and safety priority
evidence.comparator_used: LEAN (efficiency-oriented) persona system prompt, and low vs high time-pressure personas, rather than a no-persona baseline
evidence.outcome: Contraindication/sequence violations, diagnostic breadth, and order/precaution markers in simulated ED vignettes
evidence.effect: SAFE optimization increased tests_count (β=1.32, P<0.001), broadened diagnostic breadth (entropy β=0.247, P<0.001), and increased order/precaution markers (β=0.554, P<0.001). Violations occurred only in High×LEAN (8/56, 14.3% overall). SAFE framing partially mitigated time-pressure narrowing (High×SAFE entropy interaction β=0.097, P<0.001).
evidence.tradeoff: SAFE framing increased the number of suggested tests (β=1.32). High time-pressure framing reduced tests_count (β=-1.05) and narrowed diagnostic breadth (entropy β=-0.246). All violations in High×LEAN were high severity (mean 2.75/3).
evidence.quote: Contraindication/sequence violations occurred only in the High×LEAN condition (8/56, 14.3% overall); all violations occurred in trap cases and were high severity (mean 2.75/3).
