evidence.title: CardioAgent: A Traceable Agentic and Retrieval-Augmented Architecture for Cardiovascular Clinical Decision Support
evidence.comparator_used: Generic zero-shot LLM prompt without cardiology specialization
evidence.outcome: Weighted accuracy on nine synthetic cardiovascular cases
evidence.effect: Weighted accuracy rose from 55.6% (generic LLM) to 66.7% after domain prompting
evidence.quote: In a controlled set of nine synthetic cardiovascular cases, weighted accuracy increased from 55.6% for the generic LLM to 66.7% after domain prompting and to 100% with the complete agent.

evidence.title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Large Language Models for Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: Clinical Accuracy and Efficiency
evidence.comparator_used: Same RAG-LLMs run without the preprompt
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on infective endocarditis prophylaxis questions
evidence.effect: Improved across all LLMs; e.g., Claude 3.7 Sonnet rose from 42.1% without preprompt to 47.1% with preprompt
evidence.quote: Preprompting improved performance across all LLMs.

evidence.title: Gender-Based Prompt Variation and Diagnostic Accuracy of Large Language Models in Chagas Disease and Visceral Leishmaniasis: A Comparative Experimental Study
evidence.comparator_used: Female vs male infectious disease specialist persona in the prompt (no persona-free arm)
evidence.outcome: Top-five diagnostic accuracy for visceral leishmaniasis and Chagas disease across four LLMs
evidence.effect: VL: female prompt numerically higher in all four models (gains of 8.3–16.7 percentage points), ChatGPT-4o reaching 91.7%. CD: ChatGPT-4o 100% under both conditions; LLaMA 3 70B and Mixtral 8x7B improved by 16.7 percentage points with the female prompt; Meditron-70B stayed at 16.7%. No between-prompt differences were statistically significant (all p>0.05).
evidence.quote: The gender assigned to the physician persona produced subtle, nonsignificant variations in LLM diagnostic accuracy, with a consistent numerical trend favoring the female prompt in open-weight models.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language models for diagnostic reasoning from unstructured clinical narratives in epilepsy
evidence.comparator_used: prompts without clinical role impersonation (implied by the ablation on clinical in-context impersonation)
evidence.outcome: Model performance on seizure onset zone prediction
evidence.effect: 13.7% performance variation attributed to clinical in-context impersonation; direction not stated in the abstract
evidence.quote: Performance is further strongly modulated by clinical in-context impersonation, narrative length and language context (13.7%, 32.7% and 14.2% performance variation, respectively).

evidence.title: How Reliably Do Large Language Models Reproduce Vital Pulp Therapy Guidelines? A Mixed-Effects Evaluation of Guideline-Concordance and Error Directionality
evidence.comparator_used: Non-prompted queries with no professional role assigned, across four LLMs (GPT-5, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini 2.5 Flash)
evidence.outcome: Guideline-concordance accuracy and error direction (false-positive and false-negative rates) on 26 vital pulp therapy yes/no questions
evidence.effect: No overall prompt effect with numbers is given in the text. The model × prompt interaction showed a trend toward significance but did not reach the conventional threshold. Gemini had the highest observed accuracy non-prompted and DeepSeek the highest prompted. DeepSeek outperformed GPT-5 and GPT-4o under prompted conditions. Effects varied by model: DeepSeek had reduced false positives and no false negatives when prompted, while Gemini's false negatives increased.
evidence.tradeoff: Role prompting raised Gemini's false-negative responses, a new error pattern.
evidence.quote: Error-direction analysis revealed model-specific patterns: Gemini showed consistently low false-positive rates but increased false-negative responses under prompted conditions; DeepSeek showed reduced false-positive and no false-negative responses under prompted conditions.

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT pass the polish national medical specialization examination in orthopedics and traumatology?
evidence.venue: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
evidence.comparator_used: Professor vs Specialist vs Resident role prompts (no no-role baseline)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on PES orthopedics and traumatology exams across role prompts
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 81% (range 68.33%-85.83%); highest score 85.83% recorded multiple times across different prompt types; agreement between prompting strategies moderate to substantial (Cohen's κ 0.518-0.632; Fleiss' κ = 0.571)
evidence.quote: The highest score (85.83%) was recorded multiple times across different prompt types, indicating that the model could approach or exceed the minimum passing threshold depending on prompt structure.

evidence.title: The Persona Paradox: Medical Personas as Behavioral Priors in Clinical Language Models
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt with no assigned persona (non-medical/no-persona baseline)
evidence.outcome: Task accuracy and calibration on clinical triage and patient-safety tasks
evidence.effect: Medical personas improve performance in critical care tasks, with gains of up to ~+20% in accuracy and calibration, but degrade performance in primary-care settings by comparable margins.
evidence.tradeoff: Degraded accuracy and calibration in primary-care settings; effects are context-dependent and non-monotonic; interaction style effects on risk propensity are highly model-dependent.
evidence.quote: We find systematic, context-dependent, and non-monotonic effects: Medical personas improve performance in critical care tasks, yielding gains of up to $\sim+20\%$ in accuracy and calibration, but degrade performance in primary-care settings by comparable margins.

evidence.title: Application of LLMs in CAD-RADS Classification and Patient Management
evidence.comparator_used: Alternative persona: prompt framed as a radiologist vs as a cardiologist (no no-role baseline tested)
evidence.outcome: Agreement with human reference standard for CAD-RADS scoring (weighted Cohen's kappa) and management recommendations
evidence.effect: Claude-3.7 κ = 0.997 regardless of identity; Gemini radiologist κ = 0.962 vs cardiologist κ = 0.990; ChatGPT radiologist κ = 0.896 vs cardiologist κ = 0.715; DeepSeek radiologist κ = 0.637 vs cardiologist κ = 0.768. Scoring and management recommendations varied with prompt identity.
evidence.tradeoff: Results were inconsistent across models, and the best persona differed by model. Management recommendations were much less accurate than scoring regardless of persona.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, both CAD-RADS scoring and management recommendations varied depending on the professional identity specified in the prompt.

evidence.title: The Performance of Large Language Models in Extracting Intestinal Symptoms From Electronic Health Records: Retrospective Observational Study
evidence.comparator_used: No-role prompting compared with zero-shot prompting (role-assigned) across 12 local LLMs
evidence.outcome: Macro-averaged F1-score and balanced accuracy for intestinal symptom extraction
evidence.effect: No single strategy was consistently best. Qwen3-8b reached F1 0.89 under no-role prompting, and Qwen3-1.7b reached 0.85 under zero-shot. Some pairwise differences were significant (P<.05), but absolute F1 gains were small.
evidence.quote: The effect of prompting strategy varied across models, with no single strategy consistently outperforming the others.

evidence.title: Dissecting Role Cognition in Medical LLMs via Neuronal Ablation
evidence.comparator_used: Prompts with no assigned clinical role (baseline implied; the abstract does not describe it explicitly)
evidence.outcome: Medical reasoning ability on three medical QA datasets, with neuron ablation and representation analysis used to probe reasoning pathways
evidence.effect: No numeric results in the abstract; role prompts did not significantly enhance medical reasoning, mainly changed surface-level linguistic features, and showed no distinct reasoning pathways across roles
evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that role prompts do not significantly enhance the medical reasoning abilities of LLMs.

controls.question: Should the prompt tailor tone, content, length and reading level to the specific reader?
controls.control: Specify the intended recipient and set tone, content, length, language and reading level for that audience.
controls.comparator: Prompt with no audience, tone or reading-level specification
controls.aim: Improve readability, empathy and relevance of outputs for the intended user
variants: Tailoring to clinician role, patient demographics, location or needs
controls.family_label: role, few-shot, chain-of-thought, structured, or optimized prompts and system instructions
tradeoffs: All responses remained above accepted recommendations for presenting medical information to patients.
Structured prompt was more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias. Tone was not tested in isolation from role, task and format.
Prompt B, with specified length and grade-level limits, reduced accuracy and comprehensiveness.
Accuracy was not assessed; the authors state readability gains must be paired with ongoing verification of clinical accuracy to mitigate misinformation risk.
No gain in semantic fidelity to physician answers
Readability remained too high for patients with only primary education despite the audience persona instruction

evidence.title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt V2 (slot-filling with knowledge base, no output format, simplified language or empathetic style constraints) compared with V3, which added constrained output length and structure, simplified language and an empathetic style
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated personalization and clarity, and safety and fairness (plus the other 4 dimensions) in simulated dialogues
evidence.effect: V3 vs V2: personalization and clarity adjusted P=.02; safety and fairness adjusted P<.001; the remaining dimensions not significant (adjusted P>.05)
evidence.quote: Compared with prompt V2, prompt V3 demonstrated statistically significant improvements only in personalization and clarity (adjusted P =.02) and safety and fairness (adjusted P <.001), whereas differences in the remaining dimensions did not reach statistical significance (adjusted P >.05).

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT responses on obstructive sleep apnea for patient education
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
evidence.comparator_used: No prompting (no audience, tone or reading-level specification)
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of ChatGPT answers
evidence.effect: Patient-friendly prompt 12.45 ± 2.32 vs no prompt 14.15 ± 1.59; physician-level prompt 14.27 ± 2.09 was not lower than no prompt; P < .0001 overall.
evidence.tradeoff: All responses remained above accepted recommendations for presenting medical information to patients.
evidence.quote: Responses from patient-friendly prompting had a lower mean grade level (12.45 ± 2.32) than no prompting (14.15 ± 1.59), physician-level prompting (14.27 ± 2.09), and statistics/references prompting (15.00 ± 2.26) (P < .0001).

evidence.title: Effect of Emotional Prompt on the Quality of ChatGPT Based Discharge Instructions After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Using ERAS Derived Benchmarks
evidence.comparator_used: Primary prompt (PP) without motivational cues, versus emotional prompt (EP) with motivational cues added to the PP structure
evidence.outcome: Relational/motivational tone (Composite Relationality Index) and content completeness against a 43-item ERAS-derived benchmark
evidence.effect: Almost all PP outputs had CRI of zero, while EP outputs frequently used modal verbs, affirmatives and empathetic expressions, with CRI up to 5.28. No statistically significant differences in completeness for any of the 43 features, and no factual inaccuracies, guideline inconsistencies or harmful statements were found.
evidence.quote: Emotional prompting substantially enhances the relational and motivational tone without improving content completeness.

evidence.title: Prompting Pro Tips! Best Practices for Generating Clinical Narrative Summaries
evidence.comparator_used: Vague prompt without structured elements (structured prompt bundled role, task, tone and format)
evidence.outcome: Clinically adequate summary rate, with hallucinations and bias, across 8 LLMs and 8 scenarios
evidence.effect: Clinically adequate summary 39% structured vs 9% vague; conformance to instructions comparable (64% for both); structured more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias
evidence.tradeoff: Structured prompt was more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias. Tone was not tested in isolation from role, task and format.
evidence.quote: The structured approach was more likely to produce a clinically adequate summary (39% compared to 9%) but also more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.

evidence.title: ChatGPT: Is This Patient Education Tool for Urological Malignancies Readable for the General Population?
evidence.comparator_used: ChatGPT default structured question with no audience or reading-level specification
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT output (Flesch-Kincaid reading ease)
evidence.effect: Readability increased further when the question targeted a 16-year-old audience; no numeric values given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Ease of use of the information generated from ChatGPT was increased further when the question was modified to target an audience of 16 years of age, the average level of education attained by an Australian.

evidence.title: Guidelines vs. generative AI in CKD patient education: the role of prompt engineering and expert blinded evaluation
evidence.comparator_used: Initial AI responses without the structured prompt
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated CKD patient education responses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT FKGL 11.34 to 7.87 and FRE 36.17 to 64.23; Gemini FKGL 9.62 to 7.13 and FRE 46.36 to 61.45
evidence.quote: However, when a structured prompt was applied, AI responses demonstrated significant improvements in readability, reducing the required literacy level to approximately the 7th-grade (ChatGPT FKGL: 7.87, FRE: 64.23; Gemini FKGL: 7.13, FRE: 61.45).

evidence.title: Enhancing Patient Communication With Chat-GPT in Radiology: Evaluating the Efficacy and Readability of Answers to Common Imaging-Related Questions
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.comparator_used: Same ChatGPT questions asked without the short prompt asking for an accurate, easy-to-understand answer for the average person
evidence.outcome: Response relevance and consistency improved, accuracy did not change significantly (radiologist-rated)
evidence.quote: Fewer unprompted responses were considered fully relevant at 67% (176 of 264), although this increased significantly to 80% when prompts were given (210 of 264; P = .001).

evidence.title: Prompt engineering with ChatGPT3.5 and GPT4 to improve patient education on retinal diseases
evidence.venue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie
evidence.comparator_used: Stand-alone question with no audience, tone or reading-level specification (also compared with prompt A, which had no length or grade-level limits)
evidence.outcome: Readability (average grade reading level) versus accuracy and comprehensiveness of responses when length and reading level were specified
evidence.effect: Average grade reading level 13.45 (stand-alone), 11.5 (prompt A), 10.3 (prompt B) (p < 0.001). Median accuracy and comprehensiveness 5.0, 5.0, 4.0 for stand-alone, prompt A, prompt B; prompt B lower (p < 0.001).
evidence.tradeoff: Prompt B, with specified length and grade-level limits, reduced accuracy and comprehensiveness.
evidence.quote: The use of prompt B was associated with a lower accuracy and comprehensiveness than responses to stand-alone question or prompt A questions (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence improves urologic oncology patient education and counseling
evidence.comparator_used: Default ChatGPT prompt with no audience or reading-level specification
evidence.outcome: Readability and quality of patient-directed urologic oncology content
evidence.effect: Grade level fell from 12.16 (default ChatGPT) to 7.50 (ChatGPT-a with education-level-adjusted prompting), with quality remaining high.
evidence.quote: When adjusted for user education level (ChatGPT-a and Epic Easy to Read), readability improved (7.50 and 3.53), but only ChatGPT-a retained high quality.

evidence.title: The use of structured prompt to improve the readability, accuracy, and quality of ChatGPT responses on labor epidural analgesia: a brief report
evidence.comparator_used: Direct questions to ChatGPT-5.2 without a structured prompt (bundled CRAFT prompt including Context, Role, Action, Format, Tone)
evidence.outcome: Readability and accuracy of chatbot responses on labor epidural analgesia
evidence.effect: Direct-question responses ranged from 9th grade to college level; CRAFT responses ranged from 6th to 9th grade. Accuracy 99.8% ± 0.2% vs 99.0% ± 0.4%, P = 0.029. No significant differences in understandability or actionability.
evidence.quote: Responses generated using CRAFT-based prompt had significantly better readability than those with direct questions only.

evidence.title: Comparative Readability of Large Language Models Responses to Male Infertility Questions: Impact of Contextual Prompting
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt with no audience, tone or reading-level specification (no additional context)
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM responses to male infertility FAQs (Flesch Reading Ease and SMOG)
evidence.effect: Readability improved across all five models after contextual prompting; e.g., Grok mean FRE 69.71±6.09 and SMOG 9.96±1.04 after prompting, versus non-prompted DeepSeek FRE 46.28±6.86 and SMOG 11.71±0.76 and Claude FRE 23.83±12.29 and SMOG 16.37±2.47
evidence.tradeoff: Accuracy was not assessed; the authors state readability gains must be paired with ongoing verification of clinical accuracy to mitigate misinformation risk.
evidence.quote: These findings suggest that simple contextual prompting can substantially enhance readability of LLM-generated male infertility education; however, readability gains must be paired with ongoing verification of clinical accuracy to mitigate misinformation risk.

evidence.title: Prompt Framing Modulates Safety in Shoulder and Elbow Red-Flag Vignettes: A Large Language Model Study
evidence.comparator_used: patient-oriented prompt compared with general physician-oriented and specialist-oriented prompts (no unframed baseline)
evidence.outcome: Safety-critical under-triage in red-flag vignettes
evidence.effect: Under-triage was 10/24 (41.7%) with patient-oriented prompts, 6/24 (25.0%) with general physician-oriented prompts and 3/24 (12.5%) with specialist-oriented prompts.
evidence.quote: Safety-critical under-triage occurred in 19 of 72 red-flag responses (26.4%) and was most frequent with patient-oriented prompts (10/24, 41.7%), followed by general physician-oriented prompts (6/24, 25.0%) and specialist-oriented prompts (3/24, 12.5%).

evidence.title: Can "AI" Be a Doctor? A Study of Empathy, Readability, and Alignment in Clinical LLMs
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline LLM prompt without empathy-oriented instruction
evidence.outcome: Affective polarity (extreme negativity), readability (FKGL grade level) and semantic fidelity to physician answers
evidence.effect: Reduced extreme negativity and lowered FKGL by up to 6.87 points for GPT-5; no significant increase in semantic fidelity
evidence.tradeoff: No gain in semantic fidelity to physician answers
evidence.quote: Empathy-oriented prompting reduces extreme negativity and lowers grade-level complexity (up to -6.87 FKGL points for GPT-5) but does not significantly increase semantic fidelity.

evidence.title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
evidence.comparator_used: General-purpose ChatGPT5.2 baseline without instruction configuration
evidence.outcome: Patient-facing communication quality (total 20-point rubric score covering readability, disclaimers, practicality, empathy, structure)
evidence.effect: Mean total rubric score 17.95 ± 1.62 for CSA-GPT vs 9.55 ± 1.94 for ChatGPT5.2 (p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 3.22). Practicality, empathetic tone and structural clarity were all higher for CSA-GPT (all p < 0.001). Major factual errors: 1.25% vs 3.75% (p = 0.25).
evidence.quote: In this exploratory proof-of-concept study, instruction configuration improved the patient-facing communication quality of LLM responses in cosmetic dentistry across readability, practicality, empathetic tone, structural clarity, and safety boundary-setting, without increasing major factual errors.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses on Atrial Fibrillation for Patient Education
evidence.comparator_used: Form 1 (no prompt); Form 3 physician-level prompt also compared
evidence.outcome: Estimated reading grade level of answers when audience (patient vs physician) was specified
evidence.effect: Patient-friendly prompt 12.80 ± 3.38 vs no prompt 14.23 ± 2.34 vs physician-level prompt 16.73 ± 2.65 (p < 0.05); correctness did not differ by form (p = 0.350).
evidence.quote: Form 2 answers had a lower mean grade level (12.80 ± 3.38) than Forms 1 (14.23 ± 2.34), 3 (16.73 ± 2.65), and 4 (14.85 ± 2.76) (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Effectiveness of ChatGPT in simplifying information for Polish patients on cervical cancer screening using advanced prompting
evidence.venue: Annals of agricultural and environmental medicine : AAEM
evidence.comparator_used: Zero-shot prompting without audience or reading-level specification (STANDARD)
evidence.outcome: Readability/difficulty level of ChatGPT-generated cervical cancer screening information in Polish (Jasnopis.pl)
evidence.effect: Mean difficulty 5.32 (at least 15 years of formal education) for STANDARD vs 4.15 (12 years of formal education) for EASY; 21 of 24 linguistic indicators showed statistically significant improvement (p < 0.05)
evidence.tradeoff: Readability remained too high for patients with only primary education despite the audience persona instruction
evidence.quote: While ChatGPT significantly simplified MICC_GPT, the readability levels remained too high for patients with only primary education.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses on Thyroid Nodules for Patient Education
evidence.venue: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association
evidence.comparator_used: Four prompt types were compared: no prompting, patient-friendly prompting, 8th-grade level prompting, and prompting for references.
evidence.outcome: Answer correctness and readability for thyroid-nodule patient education responses
evidence.effect: Proportions at least partially correct (p = 0.795) and correct (p = 0.402) did not differ by prompt; 8th-grade prompting had the lowest mean Flesch-Kincaid grade level, 13.43 ± 2.86, lower than no prompting 14.97 ± 2.01 (p = 0.01) and prompting for references 16.43 ± 2.05 (p < 0.0001).
evidence.tradeoff: Despite targeted prompting, responses remained above recommended patient-education reading levels.
evidence.quote: Responses from 8th-grade level prompting were the lowest mean grade level (13.43 ± 2.86) and were significantly lower than no prompting (14.97 ± 2.01, p = 0.01) and prompting for references (16.43 ± 2.05, p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Enhancing Patient Comprehension of Glomerular Disease Treatments Using ChatGPT
evidence.comparator_used: General explanation prompt with no reading-level specification
evidence.outcome: Readability and understandability vs accuracy of patient-facing explanations
evidence.effect: Readability 12.85 ± 0.93 to 8.44 ± 0.72; PEMAT-P 60.7% to 76.8%; accuracy fell from 4.56 ± 0.66 to 3.99 ± 0.39 (p < 0.0001)
evidence.tradeoff: Reduced accuracy/comprehensiveness in the tailored explanations
evidence.quote: The accuracy of GPT-4's tailored explanations was significantly lower compared to the general explanations (3.99 ± 0.39 versus 4.56 ± 0.66, p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Unlocking Health Literacy: The Ultimate Guide to Hypertension Education From ChatGPT Versus Google Gemini
evidence.comparator_used: No prompting (Form 1) compared with patient-friendly (Form 2) and physician-level (Form 3) audience prompting
evidence.outcome: Response word count and Flesch-Kincaid grade level (accuracy was also scored across all forms)
evidence.effect: Physician-level prompts gave a higher word count across both platforms (p < 0.001). ChatGPT had a higher FK grade level with physician-level prompting (p = 0.033). Most responses were at collegiate reading level, above NIH recommendations. The abstract gives no separate accuracy or readability result for patient-friendly versus no prompting.
evidence.tradeoff: Physician-level audience prompts produced longer responses. Most responses stayed at collegiate reading level, above NIH recommendations.
evidence.quote: Physician-level prompts resulted in a higher word count across both platforms (p < 0.001).

controls.question: Should we specify required fields, a template or allowed answers in the prompt?
controls.control: Specify required fields, output schema, clinical template or allowed answer set in the prompt.
controls.comparator: Brief prompt with free-text, open-ended output
controls.aim: Improve completeness, parseability, consistency and safety of generated outputs
variants: Clinical note and handoff templates such as I-PASS or ISBAR
Completeness rules and evidence citation requirements
Candidate answer lists or fixed number of outputs
Explicit permission to abstain or say 'I don't know'
controls.family_label: role, few-shot, chain-of-thought, structured, or optimized prompts and system instructions
tradeoffs: Constraints produced systematic over-prediction of rare conditions (more false alarms). Removing them cut false alarms but sensitivity fell to 8.8%, so life-threatening diagnoses would be missed.
Gemini 2.5 Pro Exp failed to generate responses in 50% of scenarios under structured prompt conditions; qualitative review found critical deficiencies across all models.
Structured prompt was more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias. Format was not tested in isolation from role, task and tone.
Minimum prompts gave shorter, less descriptive output, though still acceptable and possibly useful in busy settings. Structured prompts need more clinician input.
ISBAR did not reduce safety-critical omissions (16.0% with ISBAR vs 11.5% unstructured), so failure modes were not eliminated.
DermDecoder gave generic education disconnected from the pathological findings. The basic prompt preserved details but lacked clinical context. Human-in-the-loop oversight is still needed.

evidence.title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt with diagnostic category constraints removed (open-ended diagnosis, not limited to the seven predefined conditions plus Other Diagnosis)
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity for emergent chest-pain diagnoses, and false alarms per 500 encounters
evidence.effect: Baseline prompt with category constraints: sensitivity 79.3%, specificity 45.2%. Removing category constraints: specificity 94.7%, 140 fewer false alarms per 500, sensitivity 8.8%.
evidence.tradeoff: Constraints produced systematic over-prediction of rare conditions (more false alarms). Removing them cut false alarms but sensitivity fell to 8.8%, so life-threatening diagnoses would be missed.
evidence.quote: With baseline prompting, GPT-4o systematically over-predicted rare conditions (sensitivity 79.3%; specificity 45.2%); adding prevalence cues or removing diagnostic category constraints respectively increased specificity (83.0% and 94.7%) while reducing false alarms by 107 and 140 per 500, but at the cost of poor sensitivity (30.4% and 8.8%).

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
evidence.comparator_used: Open-ended inquiry prompt (free-text output) vs structured template prompt, same models and 30 IPC scenarios
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated composite quality, mainly evidence quality (1-10 scales rated by 16 experts)
evidence.effect: Structured prompting yielded significant improvements, primarily by enhancing evidence quality (p < 0.001)
evidence.tradeoff: Gemini 2.5 Pro Exp failed to generate responses in 50% of scenarios under structured prompt conditions; qualitative review found critical deficiencies across all models.
evidence.quote: Structured prompting yielded significant improvements, primarily by enhancing evidence quality (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: A deterministic large language model (LLM) framework for safe, protocol-adherent clinical decision support: application in hemodialysis anemia management (AnemiaCare HDs)
evidence.comparator_used: Phase 1 loosely structured prompt with open-ended output
evidence.outcome: Protocol adherence and consistency of structured, rationale-based outputs
evidence.effect: Phase 2 (fixed six clinical inputs, deterministic prompt logic) 300/300 (100%) adherent vs Phase 1 96/300 (32%); p < 0.001
evidence.quote: In Phase 1, loosely structured prompting produced variable outputs, with only 96 of 300 simulated cases (32%) fully protocol-adherent and frequent unsafe recommendations.

evidence.title: Prompting Pro Tips! Best Practices for Generating Clinical Narrative Summaries
evidence.comparator_used: Vague prompt without structured elements (structured prompt bundled role, task, tone and format)
evidence.outcome: Clinically adequate summary rate, with hallucinations and bias, across 8 LLMs and 8 scenarios
evidence.effect: Clinically adequate summary 39% structured vs 9% vague; conformance to instructions comparable (64% for both); structured more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias
evidence.tradeoff: Structured prompt was more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias. Format was not tested in isolation from role, task and tone.
evidence.quote: The structured approach was more likely to produce a clinically adequate summary (39% compared to 9%) but also more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical utility of multimodal large language models in rare maculopathy
evidence.comparator_used: Open-ended prompts with no restriction on answer choices
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity of MLLMs for PPS maculopathy vs mimics
evidence.effect: Improved accuracy and sensitivity with restricted answer choices; no numeric values reported in the abstract
evidence.quote: MLLMs showed improved accuracy and sensitivity when answer choices were restricted, with ChatGPT consistently performing best when all imaging modalities were prompted together.

evidence.title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
evidence.comparator_used: More specific and detailed prompts compared with less specific/unprompted prompts.
evidence.outcome: Adherence to status epilepticus guideline elements in ChatGPT recommendations.
evidence.effect: vital sign assessment from 33 to 91%; correct dosages of second-line drugs from 50 to 100%; correct dosages of third-line drugs from 0 to 100%; screening for complications from 0 to 100%
evidence.quote: More specific and detailed prompts increased guideline adherence most markedly regarding vital sign assessment (from 33 to 91%), correct dosages of second-line (from 50 to 100%), third-line drugs (from 0 to 100%), and screening for complications (from 0 to 100%).

evidence.title: Can artificial intelligence (AI)-based software programs generate accurate clinical dictation?
evidence.comparator_used: Minimum specific prompts (least clinician input) for the same two clinical scenarios
evidence.outcome: Clinical accuracy, completeness and descriptive detail of AI-generated dental dictations
evidence.effect: All 5 programs produced clinically accurate dictations with the structured prompt. No substantial differences in procedural accuracy were identified, and discrepancies were mainly stylistic or in level of descriptive detail. Minimum prompts gave shorter, less descriptive dictations that were still clinically acceptable in all programs. No numeric effect sizes were reported.
evidence.tradeoff: Minimum prompts gave shorter, less descriptive output, though still acceptable and possibly useful in busy settings. Structured prompts need more clinician input.
evidence.quote: With minimum specific prompts, the dictations were shorter and less descriptive but still captured the essential procedural steps for both clinical scenarios and were considered clinically acceptable in all included AI software programs.

evidence.title: Comparison of Large Language Model-Based Systems and Prompt Engineering for Internal Medicine Clinical Pharmacy Cases
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
evidence.comparator_used: No prompt engineering template (plain prompt)
evidence.outcome: Composite of response accuracy and completeness
evidence.effect: GPT no Template 0.54 vs with Template 0.60; OpenEvidence no Template 0.64 vs with Template 0.52; no significant interactions
evidence.quote: Neither the use of health care provider domain-specific LLM with RAG nor a prompt engineering template was found to improve LLM-based system accuracy and completeness.

evidence.title: Evaluating Safety-Critical Communication Behavior of Large Language Models Using Workflow-Embedded Multi-Agent Clinical Simulation
evidence.comparator_used: Unstructured nurse handover (control) vs ISBAR-structured nurse handover in a paired simulation
evidence.outcome: Hallucination frequency, escalation dialogue length, and safety-critical omissions
evidence.effect: Hallucinations 10.0% vs 26.5%; median 7 vs 9 turns; safety-critical omissions 16.0% vs 11.5% (ISBAR vs unstructured)
evidence.tradeoff: ISBAR did not reduce safety-critical omissions (16.0% with ISBAR vs 11.5% unstructured), so failure modes were not eliminated.
evidence.quote: Across 200 paired (n=400) escalation simulations, ISBAR-structured handover reduced hallucination frequency (10.0% vs 26.5%) and shortened esca lation dialogues (median 7 vs 9 turns) but did not reduce safety-critical omissions (16.0% vs 11.5%).

evidence.title: AI Simplification of Dermatopathology Reports for Patients: Basic Versus Prompt-Engineered Approaches
evidence.comparator_used: Basic ChatGPT-4.0 with a simple prompt versus custom 'DermDecoder' GPT with a structured 489-word prompt
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated factualness, completeness and potential harm of simplified dermatopathology reports
evidence.effect: Mean ratings ranged 1.27-1.63 (factualness/completeness) and 1.31-1.83 (harmfulness). DermDecoder was significantly worse for completeness in psoriasis (t = -2.79, p = 0.007) and for harmfulness in molluscum contagiosum (p = 0.049) and melanoma in situ (p = 0.048).
evidence.tradeoff: DermDecoder gave generic education disconnected from the pathological findings. The basic prompt preserved details but lacked clinical context. Human-in-the-loop oversight is still needed.
evidence.quote: Prompt engineering offered no advantage over basic AI usage in balancing professional accuracy with patient accessibility, necessitating human-in-the-loop oversight for AI-generated explanations.

evidence.title: Prognostic Prediction of Avulsed Permanent Teeth Using Conversational AI Models Versus Expert Dentists: Influence of Prompt Structure and Temporal Stability
evidence.venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
evidence.comparator_used: Narrative-format prompt with identical clinical content, compared with the other standardized formats
evidence.outcome: Alignment of LLM avulsion prognosis scores and categories with expert dentist assessments
evidence.effect: Prompt format significantly influenced outputs; the clinical-practical format showed the closest alignment with experts and the narrative format the weakest (no numeric values given in the abstract)
evidence.quote: Prompt format significantly influenced outputs, with the clinical-practical format showing the closest alignment and the narrative format the weakest.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-generated patient information leaflets: a comparison of contents according to British Association of Dermatologists standards
evidence.comparator_used: Initial generic request for a PIL, with no targeted specification of content
evidence.outcome: Inclusion of patient-relevant content (e.g. curability, heritability) omitted from the initial AI-generated PILs
evidence.effect: Initial AI PILs omitted content such as curability and heritability; the repeat series with targeted request phrasing included this content (no numeric data reported)
evidence.quote: Targeted request phrasing saw AI generate PILs including this content.

evidence.title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline prompt (first stage of the two-stage prompt engineering strategy)
evidence.outcome: Output variance and translational accuracy of LLM-generated patient-centric reports
evidence.effect: Optimized structured prompts significantly reduced output variance and improved translational accuracy, most prominently in DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-4.0 (no numeric values given in the abstract)
evidence.quote: To address these limitations, optimized structured prompts significantly reduced model output variance and improved translational accuracy, with particularly prominent effects observed in DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-4.0.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Prompt Design and Internal Reasoning in Chatbot-Based Medical History Taking: Simulation Study
evidence.comparator_used: Minimal prompt configurations and rule-based choice-mode baseline
evidence.outcome: Checklist-based information coverage in simulated chatbot medical history taking
evidence.effect: Detailed and thinking mode: 72.3% mean coverage (SD 14.3%); configurations using either thinking or detailed prompts alone: approximately 60%; minimal nonthinking and rule-based configurations: approximately 51%-54%; overall configuration difference P<.001. Factorial analysis found prompt detail significantly associated with improved information coverage, with a significant interaction with internal reasoning.
evidence.quote: In the factorial analysis of the 4 LLM configurations, both prompt detail and internal reasoning were significantly associated with improved information coverage, with a significant interaction between prompt detail and internal reasoning interaction.

evidence.title: Prompting is All You Need: How to Make LLMs More Helpful for Clinical Decision Support
evidence.comparator_used: Simple question prompt ("Should this patient be offered thrombolytics?") with open-ended output
evidence.outcome: Guideline adherence, unsafe recommendations, risk recognition, guideline grading accuracy, conversational explanation (across six LLMs, three stroke vignettes)
evidence.effect: GPT-4o and o3: guideline adherence 83.3% to 100%, unsafe recommendations 16.7% to 0%, guideline grading accuracy 0% to 100%. GPT-5.2 Thinking: 100% adherence, 0% unsafe, 100% grading with structured prompts. R1-1776: 100% adherence, 0% unsafe, 100% grading, 100% conversation, with grading and conversation up from 0%. Llama-4-Scout and Llama-3.3-70B: risk recognition 83.3% to 100%, grading 0% to 66.7%, but adherence stayed 66.7% and unsafe recommendations 33.3%.
evidence.tradeoff: Gains varied by model family; the Llama models were only modestly improved and kept unsafe recommendations (33.3%). Vigilant human oversight is still essential.
evidence.quote: For some closed-source models (GPT-4o, o3), prompts structured in the CARDS style improved guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, eliminated unsafe recommendations (16.7% to 0%), and increased specific guideline grading accuracy from 0% to 100%.

evidence.title: Prompt-Driven ChatGPT Carbon Calculator for Dental Practices: Estimation and Tailored Improvement Strategies
evidence.comparator_used: Variant 1: unstructured, open-ended request to ChatGPT, compared with structured data entry with predefined emission factors (Variants 2 and 3); estimates benchmarked against the Excel tool
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and specificity of carbon footprint estimates and recommendations
evidence.effect: No numeric effect reported. Unstructured prompts gave general recommendations of limited contextual relevance. Structured prompts improved accuracy and specificity. Estimates were largely comparable to the Excel benchmark, with minor discrepancies in waste-related emissions.
evidence.tradeoff: Risk of hallucinated outputs and regional generalisations. Effective use requires prompt literacy and open access to validated emission factor databases. Minor discrepancies in waste-related emissions.
evidence.quote: Structured prompts improved both accuracy and specificity.

evidence.title: [EMERGING THERAPIES FOR LI-FRAUMENI SYNDROME AND RHABDOMYOSARCOMA: CAN CHAT GPT ASSESS THE THERAPIES IT SUGGESTS USING THE BRADFORD-HILL CRITERIA?]
evidence.comparator_used: General question based solely on the case presentation, with open-ended output
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and clinical usefulness of ChatGPT treatment suggestions (qualitative)
evidence.effect: No numbers reported. Targeted, structured prompts gave more accurate and clinically useful responses than the general question, which was insufficiently informative.
evidence.tradeoff: Even targeted-prompt responses should be approached with caution.
evidence.quote: Targeted prompts (instructions for structuring the response, formulated as questions) lead to the generation of more accurate and clinically useful model responses but these, too, should be approached with caution.

evidence.title: Evaluating open-source LLMs for dental EMR generation
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline 'Basic Prompt' (CRISPE structured framework as a bundle vs basic prompt; components not tested separately)
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated 7-Dimensional Index (7DI) score for AI-generated dental EMRs
evidence.effect: Mean 7DI 28.86 ± 2.12 with CRISPE vs 26.91 ± 2.36 with basic prompt; p<.001, across all six models
evidence.quote: The CRISPE strategy significantly outperformed the basic prompt across all models (Mean 7DI: 28.86 ± 2.12 vs. 26.91 ± 2.36; p<.001).

evidence.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Extract and Translate Medical Information in Doctors' Notes for Health Records and Diagnostic Billing Codes
evidence.comparator_used: No explicit comparator stated; effect of schema enforcement measured
evidence.outcome: Output formatting compliance
evidence.effect: Near 100% formatting compliance
evidence.tradeoff: Format compliance did not ensure accurate specific diagnostic codes for smaller local models (7B-20B parameters)
evidence.quote: Results show that strict JSON schema enforcement achieved near 100% formatting compliance, but accurate generation of specific diagnostic codes remains challenging for smaller local models (7B-20B parameters).

controls.question: Should we put the relevant guideline, criteria or established clinical framework directly into the prompt?
controls.control: Embed the relevant guideline, diagnostic criteria, scoring rubric, definitions or named clinical or therapeutic framework in the prompt.
controls.comparator: Generic prompt relying on the model's built-in knowledge
controls.aim: Improve guideline adherence, accuracy and fidelity of conversational behavior to evidence-based frameworks
variants: Expert rule files or structured patient features
CBT, motivational interviewing or crisis intervention frameworks in chatbot prompts
Socratic tutoring or debrief rubrics for education
controls.family_label: role, few-shot, chain-of-thought, structured, or optimized prompts and system instructions
tradeoffs: Performance remained unfit for benchmarking; potential harm scores were still considerable in both groups; concurrent interventions and dosing still had the highest error rates; the model expressed high confidence for 100% of responses regardless of guidance.
Structured prompts reduced primary-site accuracy (0.96 to 0.91).
In the augmented model, at least one model choice was among the poor or contraindicated treatments for 120 vignettes (12.0%).
The approach depends on a delusion classifier that is itself unreliable on the most vulnerable models. Prompting models to assess user distress backfired under delusional framing.
Hallucinations occurred in all LLMs, and some responses were unreliable and biased even with improved inputs. Performance still depended on extensively curated input.
Tested only on synthetic data; authors call it necessary but insufficient pending prospective validation on real patient data. The abstract does not describe the exact context content.

evidence.title: Generating colloquial radiology reports with large language models
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.comparator_used: Naive prompting strategy without extracted medical term definitions
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of colloquial translations, as rated by radiologists
evidence.effect: Across all grade levels, approach was 20% more accurate than baseline; at 8th-grade level, accuracy was 88% (Findings) and 93% (Impression)
evidence.quote: Across all grade levels, our approach was 20% more accurate than the baseline method.

evidence.title: Don’t stop the heart: a performance analysis of large language models and potassium dosing
evidence.comparator_used: Same GPT-5-chat prompt without the clinician-curated potassium dosing principles (relying on built-in knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Rate of appropriate potassium replacement recommendations versus clinician answers (errors, accuracy, potential harm severity)
evidence.effect: Total errors dropped from 165 to 104; average accuracy improved from 45% to 65%; notable reduction in harm severity scores with the dosing guidance document
evidence.tradeoff: Performance remained unfit for benchmarking; potential harm scores were still considerable in both groups; concurrent interventions and dosing still had the highest error rates; the model expressed high confidence for 100% of responses regardless of guidance.
evidence.quote: When given the potassium dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with GPT-5-Chat.

evidence.title: Streamlined TI-RADS Reporting From Bilingual Speech Recognition to LLM-Assisted Conclusion Generation Using a Two-Stage Workflow
evidence.comparator_used: Minimal prompting (basic-scoring instruction) versus detailed prompting with comprehensive TI-RADS guidelines, using GPT-4o
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of TI-RADS scoring (ACR TI-RADS points and K-TIRADS categories)
evidence.effect: ACR TI-RADS point accuracy rose from 50.3% to 78.5% (P < 0.001); Korean TI-RADS category accuracy rose from 58.4% to 79.9% (P < 0.001)
evidence.quote: ACR TI-RADS point accuracy increased from 50.3% with minimal prompting to 78.5% with detailed prompting (P < 0.001).

evidence.title: A deterministic large language model (LLM) framework for safe, protocol-adherent clinical decision support: application in hemodialysis anemia management (AnemiaCare HDs)
evidence.comparator_used: Phase 1 loosely structured prompt without encoded ESA kinetics, iron dosing rules, and timing safeguards
evidence.outcome: Protocol adherence of ESA and IV iron recommendations, as judged by two nephrologists (300 simulated cases per phase)
evidence.effect: Phase 2 deterministic prompt 300/300 (100%) adherent vs Phase 1 96/300 (32%); p < 0.001; eliminated protocol deviations, unsafe iron dosing and timing violations
evidence.quote: In Phase 2, deterministic encoding achieved full protocol adherence (300/300, 100%), eliminating unsafe or premature recommendations (p < 0.001 vs. Phase 1) and consistently generating structured, rationale-based outputs.

evidence.title: CALM-RAD: Calibrated GPT-4o Confidence-Based Triage Enables 96-100% Accuracy in Automated TNM Staging of Head and Neck Cancer Reports
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.comparator_used: Simple prompt
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of T, N, and primary site labels
evidence.effect: Simple prompt accuracies were 0.73 for T, 0.80 for N, and 0.96 for site; structured prompts raised T to 0.81 and N to 0.83, but reduced site to 0.91.
evidence.tradeoff: Structured prompts reduced primary-site accuracy (0.96 to 0.91).
evidence.quote: Simple prompt accuracies were 0.73 for T, 0.80 for N, and 0.96 for site; structured prompts raised T to 0.81 and N to 0.83, but reduced site to 0.91.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Augmented Clinical Trial Screening
evidence.comparator_used: Prompts without expert guidance (SO and CoT without EG, plus Self-Discover and LLM-generated guidance)
evidence.outcome: Criterion-level and patient-level eligibility screening accuracy, Youden Index and AUC
evidence.effect: GPT-3.5: Structured Output + EG performed best (median accuracy across approaches 0.761). GPT-4 strict eligibility: CoT + EG accuracy 0.65. GPT-4 highest Youden Index (0.729) came from Self-Discover and highest proportional AUC (0.82) from CoT + LLM-G.
evidence.quote: GPT-3.5 showed a median accuracy of 0.761 (range: 0.554–0.910), with the Structured Out-put + EG approach performing best.

evidence.title: Clinical decision support for bipolar depression using large language models
evidence.venue: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
evidence.comparator_used: Un-augmented GPT-4-turbo without guidelines in the prompt
evidence.outcome: Proportion of vignettes where the model's choice matched the expert-designated optimal next-step pharmacotherapy
evidence.effect: Augmented model 508/1000 (50.8%, 95% CI 47.7-53.9%; kappa 0.31) vs un-augmented 234 (23.0%, 95% CI 20.8-26.0%); McNemar's p < 0.001. Un-augmented model performance was similar to community clinicians (23.1%).
evidence.tradeoff: In the augmented model, at least one model choice was among the poor or contraindicated treatments for 120 vignettes (12.0%).
evidence.quote: By comparison, an un-augmented model identified the optimal treatment for 234 (23.0%, 95% CI 20.8-26.0%; McNemar's p < 0.001 versus augmented model) of the vignettes.

evidence.title: Inclusivity and Innovation: A Pilot Study on Free AI Models for Clinical Supervision in Gestalt Therapy (GT)
evidence.comparator_used: Prompts used in the two previous studies, which lacked the precise instructions on good supervision
evidence.outcome: Quality of supervision feedback from the AI model
evidence.effect: Reported as a significant improvement attributed to the new prompt's instructions on the fundamental characteristics of good supervision; no numbers given in the abstract
evidence.quote: The results show the surprising competitiveness of the free model and a significant improvement in the supervision feedback obtained, compared to that of previous studies, attributable to the characteristics of the new prompt, which includes precise instructions on the fundamental characteristics of good supervision.

evidence.title: The performance boundaries of knowledge prompts: A study on injection strategies and scale effects for ICD coding tasks in large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Four other prompting strategies tested with GPT-4o (the abstract does not describe them; a baseline without injected knowledge is presumably among the five)
evidence.outcome: ICD coding accuracy for primary diagnosis, secondary diagnosis and surgical procedure coding
evidence.effect: Contextual prompting tailored to medical specialties was best with GPT-4o, with accuracies of 84%, 85% and 82% for the three coding tasks. Accuracies for the other strategies are not given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Contextual prompting tailored to medical specialties achieved the best performance with GPT-4o, with accuracies of 84%, 85%, and 82% for the three coding tasks.

evidence.title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress
evidence.comparator_used: Standard prompting, including a distress-assessment prompt that asks the model to assess user distress, under delusional framing
evidence.outcome: Safety intervention rates under delusional framing compared with matched distress-only controls
evidence.effect: Delusion-aware prompting with explicit response guidance closed the gap, where the baseline gap was safety interventions suppressed by up to 4.5x. The distress-assessment prompt backfired under delusional framing. No other numbers are given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: The approach depends on a delusion classifier that is itself unreliable on the most vulnerable models. Prompting models to assess user distress backfired under delusional framing.
evidence.quote: Worse, the intuitive fix of prompting models to assess user distress backfires under delusional framing; only delusion-aware prompting with explicit response guidance closes the gap, and even this depends on a delusion classifier that is itself unreliable on the most vulnerable models.

evidence.title: Comparative Assessment of Performance of Domain-Specific and Primed Versus Non-Primed Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Clinical Decision-Making in Injuries to the Primary Dentition: An Exploratory Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
evidence.comparator_used: Same general-purpose chatbots (ChatGPT 5.2, Perplexity Pro) non-primed, without the summarized guideline document
evidence.outcome: Accuracy versus IADT guideline recommendations for follow-up interval and radiographic recommendations in primary dentition trauma scenarios
evidence.effect: Priming significantly improved general-purpose chatbot performance, with marked gains in follow-up interval accuracy and radiographic recommendations. All chatbots had complete diagnostic accuracy. Exact figures are not given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Priming significantly improved the performance of general-purpose chatbots, with ChatGPT and Perplexity demonstrating marked gains in follow-up interval accuracy and radiographic recommendations.

evidence.title: Cultural bias in large language models' ability to follow neuroradiology guidelines
evidence.comparator_used: Explicit prompt naming the guideline to follow, without the guideline text (generic prompt relying on the model's built-in knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Adherence to the target non-U.S. guideline recommendations in conflicting-guideline neuroradiology vignettes
evidence.effect: Restored accuracies above 90% across all models, after adherence to non-U.S. recommendations had declined sharply with explicit naming alone
evidence.quote: Providing the complete guideline text was the most effective mitigation strategy, restoring accuracies above 90% across all models.

evidence.title: Improvement of Clinical Practice Guideline Appraisal by Human Experts and AI Agents by Using Structured Guidance: Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Validation Study
evidence.comparator_used: AI agents appraising guidelines without the structured guideline appraisal workbook (no additional guidance)
evidence.outcome: Agreement (ICC) between AI agent and human consensus in AGREE II guideline appraisal
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 ICC increased from 0.613 to 0.709; o1-mini from 0.629 to 0.687. Without guidance, agent-human agreement was moderate (ICC=0.608-0.629). External validation: DeepSeek-R1 ICC=0.711.
evidence.quote: The workbook improved agreement for both models, with DeepSeek-R1's increasing from 0.613 to 0.709 and o1-mini's from 0.629 to 0.687.

evidence.title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-concordant Treatment Decision-making on Real-world Data
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt without added guideline knowledge, using original medical reports as input
evidence.outcome: Agreement with Heart Team (Cohen's kappa), reliability (ICC) and bias toward TAVR (FBI) for guideline-concordant treatment decisions
evidence.effect: Original reports: kappa −0.47–0.22, ICC 0.0–1.0, FBI 0.95–1.51. Case summaries plus added guideline knowledge: kappa −0.02–0.63, ICC 0.01–1.0, FBI 0.46–1.23. The guideline effect is confounded with the use of summaries.
evidence.tradeoff: Hallucinations occurred in all LLMs, and some responses were unreliable and biased even with improved inputs. Performance still depended on extensively curated input.
evidence.quote: The LLMs’ performance improved substantially when case summaries were used as input and additional guideline knowledge was added to the prompt (kappa: −0.02–0.63, ICC: 0.01–1.0, FBI: 0.46–1.23).

evidence.title: Harnessing Large Language Models for Reliable Automatic Charlson Comorbidity Index Scoring: A Validation Study
evidence.comparator_used: Same LLMs prompted without guideline-based prompting (generic prompt relying on built-in knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Consistency/agreement of LLM-computed Charlson Comorbidity Index with expert consensus
evidence.effect: Structured prompting 'further improved consistency'; no numeric effect for the with-vs-without comparison reported in the abstract (overall best agreement across models: R² up to 0.93, Cohen's κ up to 0.75)
evidence.quote: Open-source and proprietary systems achieved comparable accuracy, and structured prompting further improved consistency.

evidence.title: Bridging the outcome documentation gap in epilepsy surgery: Validating large language model agents for automated Engel and International League Against Epilepsy scoring from clinical notes
evidence.comparator_used: Concise definition-based prompt (Engel/ILAE definitions only) versus context-aware prompt adding temporal, causal and adherence logic, using GPT-4-turbo
evidence.outcome: Exact agreement with human-adjudicated consensus for Engel subclass and ILAE category scoring, plus ordinal distance
evidence.effect: Engel exact agreement 56.5% (95% CI 49.0-63.7) to 94.7% (95% CI 90.2-97.2); ILAE exact agreement 60.6% (95% CI 53.1-67.6) to 93.5% (95% CI 88.8-96.3); lower ordinal distance on both scales (paired sign tests p < .001)
evidence.quote: The context-aware prompt improved exact agreement to 94.7% for Engel (95% CI = 90.2-97.2) and 93.5% for ILAE (95% CI = 88.8-96.3), with lower ordinal distance for both scales (paired sign tests p < .001).

evidence.title: Accuracy and Consistency of Frontier LLMs on Orthodontic Diagnostic Tasks: A Repeated-Trial Comparison
evidence.comparator_used: Standard prompts under default settings (main 200-item evaluation) versus context-rich prompting on a 40-item supplementary set
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy on orthodontic tasks (errors)
evidence.effect: Context-rich prompting eliminated all errors across all three models (480 observations on 40 items), versus 94.0-99.0% accuracy in the main evaluation
evidence.tradeoff: Tested only on synthetic data; authors call it necessary but insufficient pending prospective validation on real patient data. The abstract does not describe the exact context content.
evidence.quote: Context-rich prompting eliminated all errors across all three models.

evidence.title: AI as a signal assessor – Can a Large Language Model perform causality assessment on a case series?
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt without Bradford Hill viewpoint descriptions (earlier prompt versions during iterative development)
evidence.outcome: Specificity and grounding of LLM causality assessment output
evidence.effect: Qualitative only: providing Bradford Hill viewpoint descriptions improved specificity and grounding; no numeric effect reported for this element alone
evidence.quote: Prompt design substantially influenced output quality; providing Bradford Hill viewpoint descriptions, including case series data, and adding explicit anti-hallucination instructions improved specificity and grounding.

evidence.title: Use of a large language model with instruction-tuning for reliable clinical frailty scoring
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
evidence.comparator_used: Basic prompt without the CFS definition (instruction-tuned prompt bundled the CFS definition with a directive for accurate responses and temperature control, so the effect is not isolated)
evidence.outcome: Consistency and inter-rater reliability of CFS scoring by GPT-3.5-turbo across seven scenarios
evidence.effect: Score distributions differed significantly between basic and instruction-tuned prompts in 5 of 7 scenarios; instruction-tuned prompt Fleiss' Kappa 0.887 with consistent responses in all scenarios; median scores within 1 point of human raters
evidence.tradeoff: Scoring was difficult in scenarios with less explicit ADL information, and the LLM may overestimate frailty when less ADL information is given.
evidence.quote: The instruction-tuned prompt showed high inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' Kappa of 0.887) and produced consistent responses in all scenarios.

evidence.title: A Longitudinal Analysis of the Usefulness, Readability, Consistency, and Capacity of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses Regarding the Reality of Chronic Pain in Children
evidence.comparator_used: Same prompt without scoring criteria (January 2025 responses without explicit criteria as context)
evidence.outcome: Usefulness score (10 predefined criteria) and readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of chatbot responses
evidence.effect: All four chatbots reached maximum usefulness scores (10/10) and a readability level below 7th grade when given explicit scoring criteria
evidence.quote: When provided with explicit scoring criteria, all systems achieved maximum usefulness scores (10/10) and attained a readability level below the 7th grade.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Caries Risk Assessment: Evaluating the Current Status of Caries Management by Risk Assessment and Cariogram with Large Language Models
evidence.comparator_used: Unguided prompting (generic prompt relying on the model's built-in knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Mean absolute error vs expert reference CRA classification, plus quality and accuracy of AI outputs (CAMBRA and Cariogram, ChatGPT-5.1 and Gemini-3.0 Pro)
evidence.effect: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy compared with the unguided condition (p < 0.001); no effect sizes given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy compared with the unguided condition (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Optimizing GPT-5 for Operation-Procedure-Code-Extraction from Operative Reports in Meningioma Surgery: Feasibility and Comparison of Context-Enhancements
evidence.comparator_used: GPT-5 with no additional context (GPT-5s)
evidence.outcome: OPS-code extraction accuracy, hallucinations and total mistakes
evidence.effect: Specified meningioma coding rules (GPT-5r): accuracy 79% vs 44% for GPT-5s; hallucinations 8 vs 105; mistakes 21 vs 132 (p < 0.001)
evidence.quote: We show, that specific context enhancement significantly improves GPT-5s ability to perform OPS-code extraction from operational reports, while significantly lowering mistake- and hallucination rates.

evidence.title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt without added guideline knowledge, applied to original medical reports
evidence.outcome: Agreement with heart team treatment decision (Cohen κ), reliability (ICC), and bias toward TAVR (FBI)
evidence.effect: Original reports: κ -0.47 to 0.22; ICC 0.0-1.0; FBI 0.95-1.51. Case summaries plus guideline knowledge in the prompt: κ -0.02 to 0.63; ICC 0.01-1.0; FBI 0.46-1.23. The guideline effect is confounded with the switch to summaries.
evidence.tradeoff: Hallucinations occurred in all LLMs tested. Reliability remained variable (ICC 0.01-1.0), and some models still agreed poorly with the heart team (κ as low as -0.02).
evidence.quote: The LLMs' performance improved substantially when case summaries were used as input and additional guideline knowledge was added to the prompt (Cohen κ coefficient: -0.02 to 0.63; ICC: 0.01-1.0; FBI: 0.46-1.23).

evidence.title: ChatGPT-CARE: a Superior Decision Support Tool Enhancing ChatGPT with Clinical Practice Guidelines
evidence.comparator_used: Original ChatGPT without integrated clinical practice guidelines (generic prompt relying on built-in knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and clarity of COVID-19 outpatient treatment decision responses, as rated by two pulmonary/critical care physicians
evidence.effect: Increased accuracy and clarity versus original ChatGPT; no numeric values reported in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Hallucination was only moderate in ChatGPT-CARE. The tool also combined guideline in-context learning with chain-of-thought prompting, so the guideline effect is not isolated.
evidence.quote: The results indicate that ChatGPT-CARE offers increased accuracy and clarity, with moderate hallucination, compared to the original ChatGPT.

evidence.title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Case Study
evidence.comparator_used: Default prompts
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy across five open-source LLMs
evidence.effect: Default prompts: 59.23–72.86% accuracy; adapted prompts that better explain classification tasks: 64.71–85.32%
evidence.quote: Adapting prompts to better explain classification tasks improved performance for all models, with accuracies of 64.71–85.32%.

evidence.title: Prompt-Driven ChatGPT Carbon Calculator for Dental Practices: Estimation and Tailored Improvement Strategies
evidence.comparator_used: Variants 1 and 2 (unstructured prompt, or structured prompt with emission factors only) versus Variant 3, which instructed ChatGPT to rely exclusively on outputs from a previously validated sustainability tool
evidence.outcome: Quality and evidence base of sustainability recommendations, and agreement of footprint estimates with the Excel benchmark
evidence.effect: No numeric effect reported. Variant 3 gave detailed, evidence-based recommendations consistent with established literature. Estimates were largely comparable to the Excel benchmark across variants, with minor discrepancies in waste-related emissions.
evidence.tradeoff: Risk of hallucinations and regional generalisations remains. Needs access to validated emission factor databases and prompt literacy.
evidence.quote: Variant 2 generated tailored outputs using emission factors, while Variant 3 provided detailed, evidence-based recommendations consistent with established literature.

evidence.title: Securing Safety and Quality in AI-generated Patient Education: A Nurse-led Methodological Framework Integrating Kolcaba's Comfort Theory
evidence.comparator_used: Earlier-stage prompts without Kolcaba's Comfort Theory (initial and clinically refined prompts)
evidence.outcome: Holistic alignment of content across comfort domains
evidence.effect: Qualitative: theoretical integration ensured alignment across comfort domains; no separate numeric effect reported
evidence.quote: Theoretical integration ensured holistic alignment across comfort domains.

evidence.title: Automating the triage of rheumatology outpatient referrals: a comparative evaluation of 23 large language models under simple and advanced prompting
evidence.comparator_used: Simple prompt without explicit triage expectations (generic prompt relying on built-in knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Between-model variance in triage accuracy across 23 LLMs, size-accuracy and accuracy-cost associations
evidence.effect: Between-model variance in accuracy fell 5.3-fold (0.014 to 0.003; Levene P=.01). Size-accuracy association went from rho=0.42 (P=.047) to rho=-0.05 (P=.83), and the accuracy-cost relationship was removed.
evidence.tradeoff: Under-triage errors persisted with some LLMs. The advanced prompt bundled explicit triage expectations with worked examples, so the effect of the expectations alone is not isolated.
evidence.quote: Advanced prompting minimised between-model variance in accuracy 5.3-fold (0.014 to 0.003; Levene P=.01), abolished the size-accuracy association (rho=-0.05; P=.83) and removed the accuracy-cost relationship.

evidence.title: Automated risk scoring for venous thromboembolism using large language models with expert knowledge-augmented prompting: a multicenter validation study
evidence.comparator_used: Basic and complex prompts (without Delphi-derived expert knowledge) across six open-source LLMs
evidence.outcome: Item-level PABAK and F1 for Padua and Caprini VTE risk scoring from unstructured EHRs
evidence.effect: Expert knowledge-augmented prompts showed the highest performance in both datasets; in the test dataset mean item-level PABAK and F1 were 0.97 and 0.96 for Padua, and 0.97 and 0.93 for Caprini
evidence.tradeoff: Processing time of 6.07 s per case for Padua and 12.82 s per case for Caprini; Caprini risk stratification was weaker (PABAK 0.73; F1 0.64) than Padua (PABAK 0.92; F1 0.96)
evidence.quote: Expert knowledge-augmented prompts showed the highest performance in both datasets.

evidence.title: The Effect of Structured Context on Chest Radiograph Interpretation by a Multimodal Large Language Model: A Pilot Comparative Study
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline generic prompt "Diagnose this X-ray image." relying on the model's built-in knowledge
evidence.outcome: Overall chest radiograph diagnostic accuracy (percent-correct with partial credit) on 50 images
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy rose from 28% to 62% with the author-developed radiologic framework (study identification, quality assessment, systematic review, separating findings from impressions, uncertainty, structured reporting). It was delivered together with the labeled-example teaching module, so the framework effect cannot be isolated.
evidence.tradeoff: Atelectasis accuracy fell from 40% to 20%. Lung cancer (20%) and feeding tube placement (40%) stayed poor, and rib fractures were missed in both conditions. Overall reliability stayed inadequate for independent clinical use.
evidence.quote: Overall accuracy improved from 28% at baseline to 62% after the structured-context intervention.

evidence.title: Exploring clinical feasibility of zero-shot learning in a large language model for immunofixation electrophoresis image interpretation
evidence.venue: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
evidence.comparator_used: Simple prompt without structured diagnostic guidance
evidence.outcome: Recall and F1-score for zero-shot IFE image classification across ten classes
evidence.effect: Detailed prompting consistently improved recall and F1-scores; no per-class simple vs detailed deltas given in the abstract. Gemini with detailed prompts reached F1 of MK 89.80, AK 84.75, GK 71.54.
evidence.quote: Detailed prompting consistently improved recall and F1-scores, underscoring the importance of prompt design.

evidence.title: Clinical reasoning from real-world oncology reports using large language models
evidence.comparator_used: Same Gemma models prompted without structured guideline-based (RECIST/AJCC) reasoning prompts
evidence.outcome: F1-score on RECIST tumor response and AJCC TNM staging reasoning tasks
evidence.effect: Gemma 12B with structured reasoning prompts reached F1 of 81.5 (95% CI: 79.8-83.3) for tumor response, 74.3 (70.8-77.8) for T-stage, 87.1 (85.1-89.0) for N-stage and 90.8 (89.1-92.2) for M-stage, described as substantial improvements; Gemma 4B showed inconsistent performance. Baseline F1 values are not given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: The 4B model was sometimes degraded under reasoning prompts.
evidence.quote: In contrast, the 4B model showed inconsistent performance and was sometimes degraded under reasoning prompts.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for detecting anaphylaxis in electronic medical records
evidence.comparator_used: Primary prompt (general practitioner role) without WAO criteria
evidence.outcome: Anaphylaxis detection performance (precision, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy)
evidence.effect: Adding WAO criteria slightly improved performance of older models (GPT 3.5 + 4 configuration); for GPT 4 Turbo the additional information did not enhance precision (primary prompt GPT 4 Turbo: 90.6% precision, 100% sensitivity, 99.5% specificity, 99.5% accuracy, kappa 0.95).
evidence.quote: The inclusion of WAO criteria slightly improved the performance of older models (GPT 3.5 + 4 configuration).

evidence.title: Institution-Specific LLM Prompting Recovers PHI That De-identification Systems and Their Gold Standards Both Miss
evidence.comparator_used: Prompt 1, a HIPAA-aligned baseline prompt without the institutional PHI categories
evidence.outcome: Recovery of institutional PHI categories missed by the baseline prompt, plus precision
evidence.effect: Naming the missed categories recovered 79% (48/61) of them; adding instructions against over-redaction restored precision
evidence.quote: Naming the missed categories recovered 79\% (48/61) of them, and discouraging over-redaction restored precision.

evidence.title: Safety-Oriented Benchmarking of Large Language Models in Risk-Based Management of Abnormal Cervical Screening Results: Scenario-Based Benchmark Study
evidence.comparator_used: Baseline Clinical Prompt (generic prompt relying on the model's built-in knowledge)
evidence.outcome: Unsafe major error-free performance and exact guideline concordance in ASCCP risk-based management of abnormal cervical screening results (3 LLMs, 60 synthetic scenarios, 1080 observations)
evidence.effect: Guideline-directed prompt package associated with higher odds of unsafe major error-free performance (OR 3.76, 95% CI 2.45-5.77; P<.001) and exact concordance (OR 8.27, 95% CI 4.14-16.52; P<.001). Under the package, unsafe major error-free rate was 100% for GPT-5.3, 98.9% for Gemini 3 Flash, and 75% for DeepSeek V3.2.
evidence.tradeoff: Even with the package, the best-performing model remained vulnerable in complex, history-dependent scenarios; error rates rose from 3.1% in low-complexity to 29% in high-complexity scenarios. Most frequent errors were undermanagement, genotype misinterpretation, and history neglect.
evidence.quote: In the main-effects model, the guideline-directed prompt package was associated with higher odds of both unsafe major error-free performance (odds ratio [OR] 3.76, 95% CI 2.45-5.77; P<.001) and exact concordance (OR 8.27, 95% CI 4.14-16.52; P<.001).

evidence.title: Beyond the Flag: Clinical Framing Closes the Moderation Gap in Suicide Risk Measurement
evidence.comparator_used: Vendor moderation APIs (the abstract does not report a generic-prompt baseline)
evidence.outcome: Macro F1 for ordinal suicide-severity classification of r/SuicideWatch posts
evidence.effect: Clinically grounded zero-shot prompting reached 0.562 macro F1, versus 0.395 for vendor moderation APIs
evidence.quote: Clinically grounded zero-shot prompting recovers much of that gap (0.562 macro F1), and expert-authored framing (not fine-tuning, added reasoning, or naive multi-agent aggregation) is the effective lever.

evidence.title: Impact of guideline-based prompting on the large language model performance in dental trauma management clinical decision-making
evidence.comparator_used: Same models (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.5 Flash, DeepSeek v3.2) answering without the guideline, relying on built-in knowledge
evidence.outcome: Open-ended question score, guideline concordance, and multiple-choice accuracy on dental trauma questions
evidence.effect: OEQ median scores with guideline: DeepSeek 32, ChatGPT 30, Gemini 30; without guideline: 26, 20, 23 respectively. MCQ accuracy 100% for all models with guideline vs 81.2% to 100% without.
evidence.quote: Guideline-based prompting substantially improved performance and guideline concordance on open-ended questions.

evidence.title: BiomechAgent: AI-Assisted Biomechanical Analysis Through Code-Generating Agents
evidence.comparator_used: Generic prompts without biomechanically-informed instructions
evidence.outcome: Agent performance on the biomechanics benchmark
evidence.effect: Significantly improved performance over generic prompts (no numbers given in the abstract)
evidence.quote: Biomechanically-informed, domain-specific instructions significantly improved performance over generic prompts, and integrating validated specialized tools for gait event detection substantially boosted accuracy on challenging spatiotemporal analysis where the base agent struggled.

evidence.title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
evidence.comparator_used: Model configurations without therapeutic prompting (standard prompt)
evidence.outcome: Safety and conversation performance scores in high-risk mental health vignettes
evidence.effect: Configuration-specific gains concentrated among weaker models; no numbers given in the abstract
evidence.quote: Therapeutic prompting produced configuration-specific gains concentrated among weaker models, while elevated reasoning produced no average improvement.

evidence.title: Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Endometrial Cancer Decision Making: A Case-Based In Silico Benchmarking Study
evidence.comparator_used: Standardized prompt without guideline information (post hoc subgroup of 12 cases)
evidence.outcome: Concordance with the expert guideline-based reference standard (0-2 score)
evidence.effect: Guideline-informed prompting significantly improved concordance for Gemini and Claude; no numeric effect sizes reported in the abstract, and no significant improvement was reported for ChatGPT.
evidence.quote: In the post hoc subgroup analysis, guideline-informed prompting significantly improved concordance for Gemini and Claude.

evidence.title: Multilingual LLM Prompting Strategies for Medical English-Vietnamese Machine Translation
evidence.comparator_used: zero-shot prompting without dictionary/terminology cues
evidence.outcome: Domain-specific medical En-Vi translation quality
evidence.effect: Terminology-aware (Meddict dictionary-augmented) cues consistently improved domain-specific translation; no numbers given in the abstract
evidence.quote: In contrast, terminology-aware cues and embedding-based example retrieval consistently improve domain-specific translation.
