evidence.title: Large language models versus expert clinicians in optimizing Chinese patient education materials for temporomandibular disorders: a mixed-methods study integrating readability, accuracy, actionability, and cultural adaptability
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified Chinese TMD patient education materials (Group A)
evidence.outcome: Readability (sentence length) and actionability (PEMAT)
evidence.effect: Mean sentence length 21.1 vs 33.9 characters (p < 0.001); actionability 95.6% vs 16.7% (p < 0.001)
evidence.tradeoff: LLM-only rewrites were less accurate than clinician rewrites (clinician accuracy 4.48 vs 3.23). Limited depth on TCM concepts. Actionability attenuated under a concise prompt.
evidence.quote: LLM-rewritten texts demonstrated significantly shorter sentences (21.1 vs. 33.9 characters, p < 0.001) and substantially higher actionability (95.6% vs. 16.7%, p < 0.001) compared with original texts.

evidence.title: Improving Patient Communication by Simplifying AI-Generated Dental Radiology Reports With ChatGPT: Comparative Study
evidence.comparator_used: Original AI-generated radiology report (text 1), not simplified
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, LIX) and patient-rated clarity, tone, structure, engagement and ability to understand findings without help
evidence.effect: FRE 51.1 (original) vs 55.0 (simplified, text 2) vs 56.4 (further simplified, text 3), P<.001; LIX lower for simplified texts; clarity and tone P<.001 for texts 2 and 3; understanding findings without help mean 1.5 (SD 0.7) for text 3 vs 3.1 (SD 1.4) for text 1
evidence.quote: Both simplified texts showed significantly higher readability scores (text 1: FRE score=51.1; text 2: FRE score=55.0; and text 3: FRE score=56.4; P<.001) and lower LIX scores, indicating enhanced clarity.

evidence.title: Utilizing artificial intelligence to increase the readability of patient education materials in pediatric neurosurgery
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified pediatric neurosurgery patient education materials from 7 children's hospitals (before vs after ChatGPT 4o modification)
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level readability
evidence.effect: Mean reading level fell from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28); p < 0.05; 38 materials; target 6th-grade level reached across all conditions
evidence.tradeoff: Limitations in maintaining word count and in precise grade-level control; accuracy and completeness of content were not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT effectively reduced the mean reading level from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28; p < 0.05), achieving the target 6th-grade level across all conditions.

evidence.title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials Using Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online patient education materials from AHA, ACS and ASA websites
evidence.outcome: Readability (grade level and other indices) of patient education materials, with accuracy and PEMAT-U understandability as balancing measures
evidence.effect: Mean grade level fell from 10.1 (original) to 7.6 with ChatGPT, 6.6 with Gemini and 5.6 with Claude (all P<.001). Original website means were 10.7 (AHA), 10.0 (ACS) and 9.6 (ASA). Word counts fell from a mean range of 410.9-953.9 to 201.9-248.1. Baseline PEMAT-U understandability was preserved.
evidence.tradeoff: 3.3% of Gemini and Claude simplified PEMs were inaccurate (none for ChatGPT). Model performance varied, and the authors say human review of LLM output is needed. Word counts were substantially reduced.
evidence.quote: After optimization by the LLMs, readability scores significantly improved across all 3 websites when compared with the original text.

evidence.title: Using Large Language Models to Generate Educational Materials on Childhood Glaucoma
evidence.comparator_used: Original online childhood glaucoma resources (20 from a Google search) before LLM rewriting
evidence.outcome: Readability of existing online materials after rewriting to a 6th-grade level (SMOG, FKGL)
evidence.effect: All LLMs consistently reduced mean SMOG and FKGL scores; ChatGPT-4 reached the 6th-grade level (SMOG 4.8 ± 0.8, FKGL 3.7 ± 1.9)
evidence.tradeoff: Only ChatGPT-4 achieved the specified 6th-grade level; ChatGPT-3.5 and Bard did not.
evidence.quote: Although Prompt C responses showed consistent reduction of mean SMOG and FKGL scores, only ChatGPT-4 achieved the specified 6th-grade reading level (4.8 ± 0.8 and 3.7 ± 1.9, respectively).

evidence.title: Improving the readability of trauma patient education materials: a ChatGPT solution demonstrated using materials by the Orthopaedic Trauma Association
evidence.venue: OTA international : the open access journal of orthopaedic trauma
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified OTA/AO patient education articles
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL and FRE) of patient education articles
evidence.effect: FKGL reduced from 8.2 ± 1.1 to 5.7 ± 0.5 (P < 0.001); FRE increased from 65.5 ± 6.6 to 76.4 ± 5.7 (P < 0.001); 29 (70.7%) revised articles accurate without modification
evidence.tradeoff: Content omissions: 3 (7.3%) articles needed minor modifications and 9 (22%) needed substantial edits, so nearly a third required revision.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT significantly reduced the FKGL (8.2 ± 1.1‒5.7 ± 0.5, P < 0.001) and increased the FRE (65.5 ± 6.6‒76.4 ± 5.7, P < 0.001) of the OTA/AO patient education articles.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Performance of Artificial Intelligence for Improving Readability of Online English- and Spanish-Language Orthopaedic Patient Educational Material: Challenges in Bridging the Digital Divide
evidence.venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online orthopaedic patient educational materials (English and Spanish)
evidence.outcome: Cumulative average reading grade level (readability), plus word count, complex words and long sentences
evidence.effect: English: 9.6 ± 2.6 to 7.7 ± 1.9 (95% CI of difference, 1.68 to 2.15; p < 0.05), a reduction of 2.0 ± 1.8 grade levels. Spanish: 9.5 ± 1.5 to 8.3 ± 1.3 (95% CI, 1.17 to 1.45; p < 0.05), a reduction of 1.5 ± 1.2 grade levels. Word count, complex words and long sentences were also significantly reduced in both languages.
evidence.tradeoff: Rewritten text still did not reach the sixth-grade target (7.7 English, 8.3 Spanish), and the reduction was smaller for Spanish. Accuracy and similarity to the original content were reported as high.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT significantly lowered the reading grade level (improved comprehension) to 7.7 ± 1.9 (95% CI of difference, 1.68 to 2.15; p < 0.05) for English-language content and 8.3 ± 1.3 (95% CI, 1.17 to 1.45; p < 0.05) for Spanish-language content.

evidence.title: Readability of Hospital Online Patient Education Materials Across Otolaryngology Specialties
evidence.comparator_used: Existing hospital and national organization online patient education materials (OPEMs)
evidence.outcome: Readability (average grade level across seven indices)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-generated materials averaged a 6.8-grade level, versus an 8th-12th grade level for hospital OPEMs, and were more readable than all hospital and organization OPEMs
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-generated materials averaged a 6.8-grade level, demonstrating improved readability, especially with specialized prompting, compared to all hospital and organization OPEMs.

evidence.title: A Blinded Analysis of Quality and Fidelity in Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials Simplified by ChatGPT and Humans
evidence.venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified Epic/Elsevier orthopaedic PEMs (baseline mean grade 8.6 English, 5.8 Spanish); human easy-to-read versions used for fidelity comparison
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Mean reading grade fell from 8.6 to 6.1 in English and from 5.8 to 3.5 in Spanish with ChatGPT-4o simplification (806 PEMs).
evidence.tradeoff: Fidelity errors in 86 PEMs: ChatGPT-4o had higher Spanish hallucinations than human simplifications, though fewer English omissions and fewer inconsistencies in both languages. Authors recommend clinician-supervised use.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o-simplified PEMs showed mean reading grade levels of 6.1 in English and 3.5 in Spanish.

evidence.title: Leveraging artificial intelligence to decipher gynecologic cytopathology reports: Insights from an exploratory study for possible use in patient portals
evidence.comparator_used: No direct comparison with the original unsimplified reports; pathologists rated the ChatGPT simplifications on their own
evidence.outcome: Pathologist-rated factual accuracy, completeness and potential harm of ChatGPT-simplified gynecologic cytopathology reports
evidence.effect: 180 evaluations by 6 pathologists; the vast majority were scored accurate, factually complete and not perceived as possibly harmful, especially with prompt 2. No numeric scores given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Ratings are pathologists' opinions, an indirect measure of patient understanding; patient comprehension was not measured.
evidence.quote: The vast majority were scored as accurate, factually complete, and not perceived as a possible cause of harm for the patients, especially when using prompt 2.

evidence.title: Leveraging large language models to improve patient education on dry eye disease
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified existing patient education materials (baseline readability)
evidence.outcome: Readability of rewritten PEMs (FKGL, SMOG) with misinformation and quality
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 and Gemini Advanced rewrote PEMs from baseline FKGL 8.0 ± 2.4 and SMOG 7.9 ± 1.7 to the targeted 6th-grade level; median Likert misinformation=1 (range 1-2)
evidence.tradeoff: Only ChatGPT-4 kept high quality and reliability (median DISCERN = 4) when rewriting; the abstract does not report this for Gemini Advanced.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 and Gemini Advanced rewrote existing PEMs (Prompt C) from a baseline readability level (FKGL: 8.0 ± 2.4, SMOG: 7.9 ± 1.7) to targeted 6th-grade reading level; rewrites contained little to no misinformation (median Likert misinformation=1 (range: 1-2)).

evidence.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence to Improve Readability of Otolaryngology Patient Education Materials
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified AAO-HNS online patient education articles
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL and FRES) of otolaryngology patient education materials; factual accuracy and content retention of the rewrites
evidence.effect: Average FKGL fell from 11.03 to 5.80 and FRES rose from 46.79 to 77.27 after ChatGPT4 conversion; no factual errors found and enough detail retained for patient education
evidence.quote: After conversion by ChatGPT4, the average FKGL across all articles was 5.80 and FRES was 77.27.

evidence.title: Improving Readability and Automating Content Analysis of Plastic Surgery Webpages With ChatGPT
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified plastic surgery webpage text, compared on six readability metrics
evidence.outcome: Readability metric scores (six metrics) of original versus ChatGPT-revised webpage text
evidence.effect: Significant improvement from baseline in all six readability metric scores with the specific-instruction prompt on ChatGPT 3.5 (all P ≤ 0.05); no further improvement with ChatGPT 4.0
evidence.quote: Significant improvements were achieved from baseline in six readability metric scores using a specific-instruction prompt with ChatGPT 3.5 (all P ≤ 0.05).

evidence.title: Enhancing Health Literacy: Evaluating the Readability of Patient Handouts Revised by ChatGPT's Large Language Model
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified ARS and AAFPRS patient handouts
evidence.outcome: Readability metrics and PEMAT understandability/actionability of patient handouts
evidence.effect: Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease 70.8 vs 43.9 (P < .05); Gunning Fog 10.2 vs 14.42 (P < .05); SMOG 9.9 vs 13.1 (P < .05); Coleman-Liau 8.8 vs 12.6 (P < .05); ARI 8.2 vs 10.7 (P = .06); PEMAT understandability 91 vs 74% (P < .05); actionability 42 vs 34% (P = .15)
evidence.tradeoff: Revised handouts averaged a seventh-grade level, not the 6th-grade target; actionability did not significantly improve; ARI difference not significant.
evidence.quote: LLM-revised handouts had better readability in nearly all metrics tested: Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease (70.8 vs 43.9; P < .05), Gunning Fog Score (10.2 vs 14.42; P < .05), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (9.9 vs 13.1; P < .05), Coleman-Liau (8.8 vs 12.6; P < .05), and Automated Readability Index (8.2 vs 10.7; P = .06).

evidence.title: Accuracy, readability, and understandability of large language models for prostate cancer information to the public
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified ChatGPT responses to prostate cancer questions
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient-facing text (Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog, Flesch Grade Level, Coleman Liau, SMOG, ARI); accuracy and sufficiency of simplified summaries
evidence.effect: Flesch Reading Ease 36.5(9.1) v. 70.2(11.2), p<0.0001; Gunning Fog 15.8(1.7) v. 9.5(2.0); Flesch Grade Level 12.8(1.2) v. 7.4(1.7); Coleman Liau 13.7(2.1) v. 8.6(2.4); SMOG 11.8(1.2) v. 6.7(1.8); ARI 13.1(1.4) v. 7.5(2.1). Summaries rated accurate in 8/9 and sufficient for decision-making in 8/9 scenarios; MTurk workers rated them correct (89.5-95.7%) and understood content (63.0-87.4%).
evidence.tradeoff: One of 9 simplified summaries was not rated accurate or sufficient for decision-making; comprehension among lay raters was as low as 63.0% in some scenarios.
evidence.quote: Mean readability of layperson summaries was higher than original GPT outputs ([original ChatGPT v. simplified ChatGPT, mean (SD), p-value] Flesch Reading Ease: 36.5(9.1) v. 70.2(11.2), <0.0001; Gunning Fog: 15.8(1.7) v. 9.5(2.0), p < 0.0001; Flesch Grade Level: 12.8(1.2) v. 7.4(1.7), p < 0.0001; Coleman Liau: 13.7(2.1) v. 8.6(2.4), 0.0002; Smog index: 11.8(1.2) v. 6.7(1.8), <0.0001; Automated Readability Index: 13.1(1.4) v. 7.5(2.1), p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Assessing the ability of large language models to simplify lumbar spine imaging reports into patient-facing text: a pilot study of GPT-4
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified lumbar spine MRI report text
evidence.outcome: Average reading level of reports (grade level)
evidence.effect: Reading level reduced from 11.47 to 8.50 (p < 0.001)
evidence.tradeoff: 34% of translations omitted at least one clinically relevant piece of information; 6% produced a clinically significant inaccuracy
evidence.quote: Of 93 included reports, GPT effectively reduced the average reading level (11.47 versus 8.50, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Enhancing Spanish Patient Education Materials: Comparing the Readability of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Spanish Patient Education Materials to the Society of Pediatric Dermatology Spanish Patient Brochures
evidence.comparator_used: Original Society of Pediatric Dermatology (SPD) Spanish patient brochures
evidence.outcome: Readability of Spanish patient education materials across seven readability measures
evidence.effect: Both ChatGPT 4.0 and Google Gemini, prompted for a 6th grade level, produced significantly improved readability scores compared with the SPD handouts (no numeric values in the abstract)
evidence.quote: Our results showed that when prompted to produce material at a 6th grade level, both AI ChatBots generated significantly improved readability scores when compared to the SPD handouts.

evidence.title: Online patient information on temporomandibular disorders provided by UK NHS hospitals: assessment and improvement of readability standards using AI-chatbots
evidence.venue: The British journal of oral & maxillofacial surgery
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified NHS hospital TMD patient information
evidence.outcome: Readability of TMD patient information (FKGL, GFI, CLI and FRES) against a sixth-grade target
evidence.effect: Originals: 12/31 met target by FKGL and 1/31 by GFI/CLI, mean FRES 64.68 (6.79). After Gemini: 96.8% met target by FKGL, 54.8% by GFI, 29.0% by CLI, mean FRES 82.59 (5.73) (p < 0.001).
evidence.tradeoff: Improvement depended on the readability tool: only 29.0% met the target by CLI and 54.8% by GFI after Gemini. Accuracy and completeness of the rewritten text are not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Gemini improved the mean (SD) score significantly to 82.59 (5.73) (p < 0.001) for FRES, meeting the target readability level.

evidence.title: Improving the Readability of Spasmodic Dysphonia Patient Education Materials Using ChatGPT-4o Mini: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.venue: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online spasmodic dysphonia patient education materials (38 PEMs)
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog, SMOG) and content fidelity of the revised text
evidence.effect: Original PEMs required about 10th grade to early college reading levels. ChatGPT-4o mini improved readability on all four indices (P <0.001; large effect sizes). Of 407 statement pairs, 57% of changes were dropped content, 29% were specificity reduction, and 5% were added content. Overall, 21% of PEMs were fully preserved, 50% partially preserved, and 29% not preserved.
evidence.tradeoff: Information loss: omitted clinical detail and reduced specificity, with 29% of PEMs not preserved. Expert oversight is needed to ensure accuracy and completeness.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o mini substantially improves the readability of SD-related PEMs but often at the cost of reduced clinical specificity or loss of essential information.

evidence.title: Rethinking Pediatric Asthma Education Through Large Language Model Generation and Simplification: Randomized Double-Blind Study
evidence.comparator_used: Unsimplified AI-generated responses (AI-GRs); AI-simplified responses (AI-SRs) were also compared with published expert-authored responses (PEARs)
evidence.outcome: Total score on the 19-item information adoption model questionnaire (acceptance) among medical professionals and pediatric patient families
evidence.effect: AI-SR mean total scores were 72.98 (SD 12.64) for medical professionals and 65.47 (SD 16.52) for families. AI-GR scores were 76.17 and 68.77, and PEAR scores were 72.97 and 64.18. AI-SR vs PEAR showed no significant difference (both Holm-adjusted P>.99). Simplification did not raise scores above the unsimplified AI-GRs.
evidence.quote: Additional language simplification did not improve acceptance in this predominantly highly educated sample, and the strong tendency to attribute materials to human authors highlights the importance of source transparency.

evidence.title: ChatGPT for improving postoperative instructions in multiple fields of plastic surgery
evidence.venue: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
evidence.comparator_used: Original postoperative instructions from four index procedures in plastic surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability, understandability, actionability, and safety of ChatGPT-rewritten postoperative instructions
evidence.effect: Original instructions averaged between the seventh and eighth grade levels; only one sixth-grade ChatGPT rewrite was lowered to the sixth-grade level; all fourth-grade ChatGPT rewrites were reduced to the sixth-grade level or below, but none achieved the fourth-grade level; understandability increased as reading levels decreased; actionability decreased for fourth-grade rewrites; safety was not compromised.
evidence.tradeoff: Actionability scores decreased for fourth-grade rewrites.
evidence.quote: While understandability increased for all ChatGPT rewrites, actionability decreased for fourth-grade-level instructions.

evidence.title: Patient Perceptions on Operative Reports Written by Surgeons versus Versions Simplified by Artificial Intelligence
evidence.comparator_used: Original surgeon-written operative reports
evidence.outcome: Patient preference, clarity, terminology accessibility and understandability of operative reports
evidence.effect: 55.4% (95% CI: 48.6%-61.2%) preferred GPT-simplified reports; clearer (mean = 1.53 ± 0.83 vs. 1.98 ± 1.92, P < 0.001); terminology more accessible (mean = 1.50 ± 0.70 vs. 2.31 ± 0.89, P < 0.001); more understandable (mean = 86.40 ± 18.07 vs. 73.70 ± 20.82, P < 0.001); bachelor's degree and below preferred GPT version in 59.6% (95% CI: 52.0%-67.0%)
evidence.tradeoff: Preferences varied by patient demographics, indicating a need for individualized approaches; only about 55% preferred the simplified version.
evidence.quote: The primary outcome showed that 55.4% (95% CI: 48.6%-61.2%) of participants preferred the GPT-simplified reports for being significantly clearer (mean = 1.53 ± 0.83 vs. 1.98 ± 1.92, P < 0.001), terminology being more accessible (mean = 1.50 ± 0.70 vs. 2.31 ± 0.89, P < 0.001), and overall, more understandable (mean = 86.40 ± 18.07 vs. 73.70 ± 20.82, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: [Making prostate cancer research accessible: chatGPT-4 as a tool to enhance lay communication]
evidence.comparator_used: Original layperson's summaries written by authors (unsimplified originals)
evidence.outcome: Readability, content quality and guideline adherence of LLM-generated layperson summaries
evidence.effect: Advanced prompt readability better than original LS (p < 0.001); content quality higher than original (p = 0.001 basic, p = 0.002 advanced); error-free LS rates 29.4% original, 76.1% basic, 92% advanced (p < 0.001)
evidence.quote: Content quality was comparable between the two ChatGPT‑4 prompts (p = 0.665) but was higher than that of the original summaries (p = 0.001 and p = 0.002, respectively).

evidence.title: Can artificial intelligence improve the readability of patient education information in gynecology?
evidence.venue: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified ACOG and UpToDate patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Readability (grade level across 8 formulas) of LLM-rewritten versions of existing patient education materials
evidence.effect: CoPilot and Gemini improved readability when prompted; none of the LLMs reached the sixth-grade benchmark; ChatGPT increased reading difficulty. Baseline: ACOG averaged ninth-grade and UpToDate 8.6-grade level.
evidence.tradeoff: ChatGPT increased reading difficulty. LLM text was shorter but used more difficult words (36.7% vs 27.4%), which may create an illusion of simplicity.
evidence.quote: Although CoPilot and Gemini improved readability when prompted, no large language model successfully reached the sixth-grade benchmark, and ChatGPT increased reading difficulty.

evidence.title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified EAU patient education materials (8 original PEMs vs 8 GPT-4-generated PEMs)
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKRE, FKGL) of patient education materials, plus accuracy, completeness and clarity ratings by urologists
evidence.effect: Mean FKRE 43.5 (original) vs 70.8 (GPT-4), p < .001; mean FKGL 11.6 vs 6.1, p < .001; no significant differences in accuracy, completeness and clarity for localized or metastatic cancers; mean GPT-4 creation time 52.1 seconds
evidence.quote: The readability scores for the 8 original PEMs were lower than for the 8 GPT-4-generated PEMs (Mean FKRE: 43.5 vs. 70.8; p < .001).

evidence.title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified radiology reports
evidence.outcome: Readability of radiology reports rated by 16 non-medical participants
evidence.effect: LLM-generated patient-centric reports significantly enhanced readability (P < 0.05); DeepSeek-R1 achieved the best performance
evidence.tradeoff: All models showed output instability, omitted information and risk-averse, generalized recommendations; patients' self-reported comprehension varied with demographic characteristics (age, education).
evidence.quote: Overall, large language models significantly enhanced the readability of radiology reports (P < 0.05), with DeepSeek-R1 achieving the best performance.

evidence.title: Enhancing patient and parent education in pediatric ophthalmology using artificial intelligence: a report by the AAPOS Public Information Committee
evidence.venue: Journal of AAPOS : the official publication of the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified AAPOS patient education materials (111 PEMs)
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG, FKGL) and PEMAT understandability of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Baseline PEMs averaged a 9th-grade level (SMOG 9.0 ± 1.6; FKGL 9.6 ± 2.1), with 3.6% meeting the 6th-grade recommendation. ChatGPT-4 rewrites reached a 7th-grade level and Gemini Advanced rewrites met the 6th-grade threshold. Understandability was 90.9% (ChatGPT-4) and 91.3% (Gemini Advanced), P < 0.001. Rewrites contained no misinformation (Likert = 1).
evidence.tradeoff: Gemini Advanced rewrites showed modestly reduced quality (DISCERN: 3; P < 0.001). The authors advise physician review of PEMs for safety.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 rewrites improved readability to a 7th-grade level without compromising quality, while Gemini Advanced rewrites met the 6th-grade threshold but showed modestly reduced quality (DISCERN: 3; P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Identifying Unmonitored Tone Drift in Patient Education Materials Transcribed to a Lower Reading Level by a Large Language Model
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified neurosurgical patient education materials (336 PEMs), compared before vs after GPT-4.0 simplification to a seventh grade level
evidence.outcome: Readability across 6 indices (Flesch-Kincaid Grade, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog, ARI, Coleman-Liau, SMOG)
evidence.effect: Substantial readability improvement across all 6 indices and all neurosurgical topics (P < .001); exact index values not given in the abstract
evidence.tradeoff: Unmonitored tone drift: sentiment shifted toward positivity (higher VADER compound scores, more positive tokens, fewer neutral tokens); disgust decreased significantly in every topic; sadness, surprise and joy increased modestly; fear and anger unchanged. Authors suggest a shift toward more persuasive language and recommend monitoring.
evidence.quote: Simplification produced substantial improvements in readability across all 6 indices and all neurosurgical topics (P < .001).

evidence.title: Patient-friendly simplification and translation of neuroradiology impressions using artificial intelligence
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified neuroradiology report impressions
evidence.outcome: Readability (reading grade and text complexity metrics) and sentiment of report impressions
evidence.effect: Reading grade fell from approximately college to approximately middle-school level; readability improved across several text complexity metrics; simplified impressions were classified as more neutral and less fearful. Exact figures are not given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Neuroradiologist raters found low rates of hallucinations, omissions, and imprecisions in the simplified impressions compared with the originals.
evidence.quote: The reading grade of the report impressions decreased from approximately college to approximately middle-school level, and readability improved across several text complexity metrics.

evidence.title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
evidence.comparator_used: Original author-written lay summaries (unsimplified research abstracts' existing lay summaries)
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKRE), factual accuracy, word count compliance, and composite high-quality rate
evidence.effect: Median FKRE extended prompt 47, simple prompt 36, original 20 (P<.001); median accuracy 5 for both AI vs 5 (IQR 4-5) for original (P<.001); wrong word count 19% extended, 20% simple vs 69% original (P<.001); high-quality 79.4% extended, 54.9% simple, 5.4% original (P<.001)
evidence.quote: The proportion rated as high-quality was 79.4% for the extended prompt, 54.9% for the simple prompt, and 5.4% for original summaries (P<.001).

evidence.title: Large Language Model Simplification of Open Access Pediatric Strabismus Literature: Cross-Sectional Validation of Readability and Clinical Fidelity
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified open access pediatric strabismus articles (baseline readability)
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL and SMOG) of LLM plain-language summaries versus the original articles; clinical fidelity rated by 2 specialists
evidence.effect: FKGL fell from 15.79 (SD 1.53) to 7.84 (SD 1.30), mean difference 7.95 (95% CI 7.52-8.38; P<.001). SMOG fell from 14.41 (SD 1.09) to 7.68 (SD 0.94), mean difference 6.73 (95% CI 6.42-7.04; P<.001). Fidelity was good in 81/85 (95.29%), moderate in 4 (4.71%), and poor in 0.
evidence.tradeoff: 4 summaries had only moderate clinical fidelity, all of review articles. Case reports kept slightly higher FKGL (mean 8.35, SD 0.89) than reviews (7.89) and original research (7.48) (adjusted P=.003).
evidence.quote: Following LLM simplification, the mean FKGL score significantly decreased from 15.79 (SD 1.53) to 7.84 (SD 1.30), representing a mean difference of 7.95 (95% CI 7.52-8.38; P<.001).

evidence.title: Advancing Patient Education in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: The Promise of Large Language Models
evidence.comparator_used: Original published/googled patient education materials on idiopathic intracranial hypertension left unchanged
evidence.outcome: Readability of prewritten patient education materials, with quality and accuracy maintained
evidence.effect: SMOG: 5.6 ± 0.6, FKGL: 5.7 ± 0.8, p < 0.001, DISCERN ≥4, Likert misinformation = 1
evidence.quote: Original published PEMs were rewritten to below a 6th-grade reading level with Prompt C, without a decrease in quality, understandability, or accuracy only by ChatGPT-4 (SMOG: 5.6 ± 0.6, FKGL: 5.7 ± 0.8, p < 0.001, DISCERN ≥4, Likert misinformation = 1).

evidence.title: Improving readability of shoulder and elbow surgery online patient education material with Chat GPT (Chat Generative Pretrained Transformer) 4
evidence.venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online patient education excerpts on shoulder and elbow surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG Index and ChatGPT-assessed reading grade level)
evidence.effect: Original SMOG average 10.1; after ChatGPT simplification SMOG 8.3 and ChatGPT-assessed 7.7 (P < .001)
evidence.tradeoff: Readability reached only near-recommended levels (not 6th-8th grade by SMOG); authors state human review remains necessary to ensure clinical accuracy of AI-simplified materials.
evidence.quote: Following simplification, both the SMOG readability score and ChatGPT significantly dropped to 8.3 and 7.7, respectively, aligning closer to recommended readability levels (P < .001).

evidence.title: Using ChatGPT to Improve the Presentation of Plain Language Summaries of Cochrane Systematic Reviews About Oncology Interventions: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.comparator_used: Original Cochrane plain language summaries (existing PLS formats) for the same oncology reviews
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG index) and word count of plain-language summaries, with conclusiveness category consistency
evidence.effect: Prompt 1 median SMOG 8.2 (95% CI 8-8.4) vs original 13.1 (95% CI 12.9-13.4); word count 240 vs 364; prompt 2 SMOG 11.4; prompt 3 SMOG 8.7; conclusiveness categorization of original abstracts unchanged in ChatGPT PLSs
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-generated PLSs using the first prompt (SMOG index 6) were the shortest and easiest to read, with a median SMOG score of 8.2 (95% CI 8-8.4), compared with the original PLSs (median SMOG score 13.1, 95% CI 12.9-13.4).

evidence.title: Improving patient communication and understanding of medical reports through text simplification with ChatGPT: a comparative study
evidence.comparator_used: Original physician-written, unsimplified medical reports
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, LIX), patient-rated clarity, structure and usefulness, and comprehension accuracy
evidence.effect: FRE 48.4 ± 5.0 vs. 22.9 ± 5.2 (p < 0.0001); LIX 48.3 ± 3.2 vs. 59.2 ± 2.5 (p = 0.004); comprehension e.g., MRI 80.3% vs. 53.7% (p < 0.001); ratings higher (p < 0.001); no loss of medical information observed
evidence.quote: Simplified reports achieved significantly higher readability (FRE 48.4 ± 5.0 vs. 22.9 ± 5.2; p < 0.0001; LIX 48.3 ± 3.2 vs. 59.2 ± 2.5; p = 0.004).

evidence.title: ChatGPT improves readability in validated spine patient-reported outcome measures
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unrevised validated spine PROMs before ChatGPT 4.0 revision
evidence.outcome: Readability of validated spine patient-reported outcome measures and preservation of validated content
evidence.effect: Eighteen of nineteen linguistic parameters improved significantly (p < .05); word count decreased by 18%; all readability indices improved (p < .001); about 7 of 9 grade-level metrics achieved NIH/AMA sixth-grade readability compliance following revision. However, 59.7% of PROMs contained at least one content-related error; alteration of validated response scales (23%), omission or simplification of recall timeframes (18%), and consolidation of multiple items into single prompts (16%).
evidence.tradeoff: Frequent content-related errors affecting validated instrument structure: 59.7% of PROMs had at least one content-related error, including altered response scales, omitted or simplified recall timeframes, and consolidated items.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT 4.0 substantially improved the readability of validated spine PROMs but frequently introduced structural modifications affecting validated content.

evidence.title: Comparing the Accuracy and Readability of Glaucoma-related Question Responses and Educational Materials by Google and ChatGPT
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified glaucoma procedural explanations (baseline ChatGPT-generated materials at grade 16.6)
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level of glaucoma procedural explanations and accuracy after LLM revision
evidence.effect: Average reading level reduced from grade 16.6 (college level) to grade 9.4 (high school level) (p < 0.001) without reducing accuracy
evidence.quote: When instructed to revise glaucoma procedural explanations to improve understandability, ChatGPT reduced the average reading level of educational materials from grade 16.6 (college level) to grade 9.4 (high school level) (p < 0.001) without reducing the accuracy of procedural explanations.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Commonly Utilized Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models in Optimizing Readability, Accuracy, and Comprehension of Orthopaedic Oncology Patient Educational Materials
evidence.venue: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
evidence.comparator_used: Original online orthopaedic oncology patient educational materials as written (baseline)
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient educational materials (FKGL, GFI, FRE), with accuracy (F1) and comprehension checked
evidence.effect: Baseline FKGL 8.7 ± 1.5, GFI 10.5 ± 1.9, FRE 53.9 ± 8.2. All five LLMs significantly improved readability (P < 0.001). ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek AI and Google Gemini produced the most readable outputs. Google Gemini had the highest F1 of 0.986 (range 0.765-0.986) and 100% comprehension.
evidence.tradeoff: Accuracy and comprehension were compromised for Meta AI when prompted below the sixth-grade level. F1 varied across LLMs, with a low of 0.765.
evidence.quote: All LLMs significantly improved readability (P < 0.001), and ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek AI, and Google Gemini conversion produced the most readable outputs.

evidence.title: Bridging Gaps in Health Literacy for Cleft Lip and Palate: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Educational Materials
evidence.venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified patient educational materials from ACPA-approved craniofacial team websites
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) and clarity score of patient educational materials
evidence.effect: Median reading level fell from 9th grade to 6th grade after ChatGPT-4 simplification; readability significantly improved and clarity was enhanced (no further numbers given in the abstract)
evidence.quote: Modifications using ChatGPT-4 significantly improved readability, achieving a median 6th-grade level and enhanced clarity.

evidence.title: Improving Doctor-Patient Communication Using Large Language Models - Results from an Experimental Study
evidence.comparator_used: Original medical notes written in clinical language (within-subjects, each participant viewed two original and two GPT-4 lay-language notes)
evidence.outcome: Objective comprehension, subjective understanding, perceived empathy, mental effort and negative emotions when reading medical notes
evidence.effect: Higher comprehension scores (effect size details not reported in abstract), greater subjective understanding, higher perceived empathy, reduced mental effort and negative emotions; significant improvements across all measured dimensions except average reading times
evidence.tradeoff: No significant difference in average reading times; accuracy validation and clinician workflow integration still need investigation
evidence.quote: LLM translation of medical notes significantly improved both objective and subjective patient understanding.

evidence.title: The ethics of simplification: balancing patient autonomy, comprehension, and accuracy in AI-generated radiology reports
evidence.comparator_used: Accuracy across prompted reading grade levels (1-17) of LLM-simplified versions of the original radiology reports; no unsimplified-report arm
evidence.outcome: Clinical accuracy (radiologist assessment, PubMed-BERTScore) of LLM-simplified radiology reports by target grade level
evidence.effect: Accuracy stable across grades 13-11 but declined significantly below grade 11; at 7th-grade level, 20% of reports contained inaccuracies with potential to alter patient management
evidence.tradeoff: Inaccuracies at lower reading levels were primarily due to omission, incorrect conversion, or inappropriate generalization.
evidence.quote: At the 7th-grade level, 20% of reports contained inaccuracies with potential to alter patient management, primarily due to omission, incorrect conversion, or inappropriate generalization.

evidence.title: Enhancing Access to Orthopedic Education: Exploring the Potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Improving Health Literacy on Rotator Cuff Injuries
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online patient education materials on rotator cuff injuries from 25 top-ranked orthopedic hospitals
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level and word count of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Reading-grade level fell by 4.33 ± 1.50 (p < 0.001) and word count fell by 442.68 ± 351.45 (p < 0.001) after ChatGPT-4 rewriting
evidence.quote: Analysis of the original and rewritten PEMs about RCI demonstrated significant reductions in reading-grade level and word count of 4.33 ± 1.50 (p < 0.001) and 442.68 ± 351.45 (p < 0.001), respectively.

evidence.title: Assessing ChatGPT vs. evidence-based online responses for polycystic ovary syndrome self-management and education: an international cross-sectional blinded survey of healthcare professionals
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified responses (ChatGPT and evidence-based online PCOS responses before simplification)
evidence.outcome: Readability of PCOS patient education responses
evidence.effect: Using ChatGPT to simplify the responses resulted in significant improvement in readability; no numeric values reported in the abstract. Before simplification, there were no statistically significant readability differences between ChatGPT and evidence-based responses.
evidence.quote: However, using ChatGPT for simplifying the responses resulted in significant improvement.

evidence.title: Can generative AI improve the readability of patient education materials at a radiology practice?
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified radiology group patient education documents (ARL 11.72)
evidence.outcome: Average reading level (ARL) of patient education materials after LLM simplification to a sixth-grade target
evidence.effect: Original ARL 11.72; ChatGPT-4 ARL 7.32 ± 0.76 (6/7 documents significant); Gemini ARL 6.55 ± 0.51 (7/7 significant). Word count reduced 15% ± 7% (ChatGPT) and 33% ± 7% (Gemini).
evidence.tradeoff: Neither tool reached the sixth-grade target on average. Some information was lost: 95% of ChatGPT outputs retained at least 75% of information versus 68% for Gemini. Gemini outputs were rated less appropriate (57% vs 95%), clear (67% vs 92%) and relevant (76% vs 95%), with lower interrater agreement (0.46 vs 0.91). The authors say ongoing expert review is needed.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT ARL was 7.32 ± 0.76 (6/7 significant) and Gemini ARL was 6.55 ± 0.51 (7/7 significant).

evidence.title: Evaluating the Use of Large Language Models in Improving the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials for Peripheral Nerve Surgery
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of peripheral nerve surgery patient education materials
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL fell from 11.3 (original) to 7.5 with ChatGPT rewrites and to 5.6 with Gemini rewrites (both p < 0.001)
evidence.tradeoff: Gemini rewrites had lower accuracy/quality (4.0/5.0 vs 4.5/5.0 for ChatGPT) and lower comprehensiveness (1.0/3.0 vs 2.0/3.0), both p < 0.001. The simpler Gemini text lost some content.
evidence.quote: The average FKGL of ChatGPT rewrites was significantly lower than that of OPEMs (11.3 vs. 7.5, p < 0.001), as was the average FKGL of Gemini rewrites (11.3 vs. 5.6, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models to Improve Spanish Patient Education on Childhood Glaucoma
evidence.venue: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified Spanish patient education materials on childhood glaucoma
evidence.outcome: Readability (INFLESZ score) of Spanish patient education materials, with expert-rated quality (helpfulness, truthfulness, harmlessness) as a safety check
evidence.effect: Mean INFLESZ rose from 56.6 ± 4.9 (8th-grade level) to 69.6 ± 2.3 (4th- to 6th-grade level), P < .001. Revised materials had fewer syllables, words and complex words, with no significant difference in sentence count. Quality was unchanged (median 15 in both groups, P = .74).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o can be used as a supplemental tool by health care professionals to improve the readability of existing Spanish PEMs on childhood glaucoma, without sacrificing the quality, accuracy, or reliability of their content.

evidence.title: Improving readability and comprehension levels of otolaryngology patient education materials using ChatGPT
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified otolaryngology patient education materials (ALA and AAO-HNS), scored before and after ChatGPT 3.5 rewriting
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education materials (Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch-Kincaid grade level)
evidence.effect: Overall FRE scores and FK grades improved significantly after ChatGPT translation (p < 0.001) for 37 ALA and 72 AAO-HNS topics. In Word scoring, AAO-HNS materials improved significantly overall (p < 0.001). Specific score values are not given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Word did not show significant improvement for individual topics or subspecialty categories. ChatGPT's own scoring significantly exaggerated the change in FRE and FK compared with Word (p < 0.001). Accuracy and completeness of the simplified text were not reported.
evidence.quote: Overall FRE scores and FK grades demonstrated significant improvements following translation of materials, as scored by ChatGPT (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: The Illusion of Understanding: A Randomized Controlled Trial of LLM-Generated Lay Summaries of Brain MRI Reports
evidence.comparator_used: Original brain MRI reports in native format without lay summary
evidence.outcome: Objective comprehension (correct classification of whether report explains headache); also satisfaction, subjective comprehension, anxiety
evidence.effect: Objective comprehension 58.3% vs 59.4% (OR 0.97; 95% CI 0.90–1.06; P = .54); satisfaction 64.9% vs 36.7% (OR 3.26); subjective comprehension 50.3% vs 24.0% (OR 3.17); high anxiety 25.1% vs 26.6% (OR 0.92; P = .037); symptom-explaining reports 42.4% vs 37.4%; normal reports 72.5% vs 76.6%
evidence.tradeoff: Gap between perceived and actual understanding; reduced objective comprehension for normal reports (72.5% vs 76.6%, P = .001)
evidence.quote: LLM-generated lay summaries appended to brain MRI reports improved patient satisfaction and subjective comprehension but did not improve objective comprehension, indicating a gap between perceived and actual understanding that should be addressed before clinical integration.

evidence.title: Can "AI" Be a Doctor? A Study of Empathy, Readability, and Alignment in Clinical LLMs
evidence.comparator_used: Original physician-authored answers and baseline LLM responses
evidence.outcome: Semantic similarity to physician answers, readability, affective extremity and patient preference
evidence.effect: Rephrase configurations reached semantic similarity up to mean = 0.93 and consistently improved readability and reduced affective extremity; patients consistently preferred rewritten variants for clarity and emotional tone
evidence.tradeoff: No model surpassed physicians on epistemic criteria in the dual stakeholder evaluation
evidence.quote: Rephrase configurations achieve the highest semantic similarity to physician answers (up to mean = 0.93) while consistently improving readability and reducing affective extremity.

evidence.title: Large Language Model-Based Simplification of Digital Therapeutics Explanations for Insomnia and Nicotine Dependence: Two Randomized Online Experiments
evidence.comparator_used: Original manufacturer-provided DTx explanatory materials (unsimplified)
evidence.outcome: Perceived understanding (pre/post change) and ratings of ease, clarity, and comprehensibility among lay participants
evidence.effect: Group×time interaction on perceived understanding: insomnia F1,498=24.8, P<.001; nicotine dependence F1,498=14.1, P<.001; simplified rated easier, clearer, more comprehensible (all P<.05), r=0.11-0.24
evidence.quote: Compared with manufacturer-provided original materials, LLM-simplified DTx explanations led to greater improvements in perceived understanding and subjective evaluations of readability among lay audiences, even after a single exposure.

evidence.title: Expanding Accessibility in Cleft Care: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Improving Literacy of Alveolar Bone Grafting Information
evidence.venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
evidence.comparator_used: Original online alveolar bone grafting patient education materials (unsimplified)
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ABG patient education materials
evidence.effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level improved from 8.0 ± 2.3 (original) to 6.1 ± 1.3 after ChatGPT rewriting (p < 0.0001); original was significantly above AMA recommended sixth grade level (p < 0.0001)
evidence.quote: PEM rewriting with ChatGPT improved Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level to 6.1 ± 1.3 (p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4 Can Help Hand Surgeons Communicate Better With Patients
evidence.venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unedited ASSH and BSSH website patient articles
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient-focused hand surgery articles across seven readability formulas
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 rewrites improved readability across all chosen formulas, reached a mean sixth-grade level on Flesch Kincaid Grade Level and SMOG, and increased the mean Flesch Reading Ease score. No numeric values given in the abstract.
evidence.tradeoff: Accuracy was not measured; the authors caution that ChatGPT-4 prioritises sounding natural over truth, so information accuracy may be sacrificed for readability and each response needs surgeon evaluation.
evidence.quote: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer version 4 was able to improve the readability across all chosen readability formulas and was successful in achieving a mean sixth-grade readability level in terms of the Flesch Kincaid Grade Level and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook calculations.

evidence.title: PRECISE framework: Enhanced radiology reporting with GPT for improved readability, reliability, and patient-centered care
evidence.comparator_used: Original radiology reports (500 chest X-ray reports) versus GPT-4 PRECISE-generated sixth-grade-level patient summaries
evidence.outcome: Readability of radiology reports (Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog Index, ARI), plus reliability and understandability ratings
evidence.effect: Flesch Reading Ease 38.28 to 80.82; Gunning Fog 13.04 to 6.99; ARI 13.33 to 5.86 (all p<0.001). Clinical volunteers found 95% of summaries reliable; non-medical volunteers rated 97% as fully understandable.
evidence.tradeoff: About 5% of summaries were not judged reliable by clinical volunteers. The authors state the approach adds no significant burden to radiologists.
evidence.quote: Readability scores significantly improved, with the mean Flesch Reading Ease score increasing from 38.28 to 80.82 (p-value < 0.001), the Gunning Fog Index decreasing from 13.04 to 6.99 (p-value < 0.001), and the ARI score improving from 13.33 to 5.86 (p-value < 0.001).

evidence.title: Online patient information on labour epidural analgesia provided by UK National Health Services hospitals: assessment of readability and improvement of readability standards using ChatGPT
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified UK NHS hospital online patient information on labour epidurals
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education text (mean grade level and proportion of texts meeting the sixth-grade target on two readability scores)
evidence.effect: Mean grade fell from 8.4 ± 2.1 to 7.7 ± 1.2 (P <0.001). Texts meeting target went from 14.5% and 23.2% to 24.6% and 27.5% on the two scores.
evidence.tradeoff: ChatGPT-rewritten texts still did not reach the sixth-grade target. Most texts still missed it on both scores, and the mean grade stayed above target.
evidence.quote: After AI-modification, 24.6% and 27.5% of the texts met targets using the same metrics, with the mean grade (7.7 ± 1.2) decreasing significantly (P <0.001), but still not meeting the target level.

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models in generating and optimizing educational materials for neonatal home oxygen therapy
evidence.comparator_used: Original human-authored WeChat NHOT health education articles (unsimplified)
evidence.outcome: Understandability (C-PEMAT), content quality (C-DISCERN) and actionability of LLM-rewritten vs original texts
evidence.effect: All models significantly enhanced understandability of original texts (p < 0.01); Grok and Qwen also improved content quality and actionability. Rewriting performed more reliably than de novo generation.
evidence.tradeoff: Prompt optimization decreased lexical richness. All AI-generated materials still require clinical professional review before distribution.
evidence.quote: In the rewriting task (Prompt C), all models significantly enhanced the understandability of original texts (p < 0.01), with Grok and Qwen additionally improving content quality and actionability.

evidence.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve the Readability of Patient Education Materials on Aortic Stenosis? A Pilot Study
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online aortic stenosis patient education materials (pre-conversion readability)
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education materials (FRE, FKGL, SMOGI, GFI) before vs after LLM rewriting
evidence.effect: Original materials were at about a 10th-12th grade level. ChatGPT-3.5 improved all four measures (p < 0.001) to about 6th-7th grade. Bard improved all measures (p < 0.001) except SMOGI (p = 0.729) to about 8th-9th grade. ChatGPT-3.5 outperformed Bard on post-conversion scores, percentage change and conversion time (all p < 0.001).
evidence.tradeoff: Neither platform produced materials below the recommended 6th-grade level. Bard did not improve SMOGI and was slower than ChatGPT-3.5. The abstract does not report accuracy or content checks of the simplified text.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-3.5 successfully improved readability across all four measures (p < 0.001) to the approximately 6th-7th grade reading level.

evidence.title: Enhancing the quality and trustworthiness of large language model-generated summaries of clinical oncology literature
evidence.comparator_used: Human-written/expert-written plain language summaries from BioLaySumm
evidence.outcome: Readability of plain language summaries
evidence.quote: Finally, LLM-generated PLS were more readable than human-written versions (FRE 42.3 [interquartile range, IQR 35.27-49.41] vs 28.8 [IQR 21.02-36.18]).

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4 in Neurosurgery: Improving Patient Education Materials
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unrewritten neurosurgical patient education materials from top US hospitals
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education materials (FRE, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, ARI, Coleman-Liau, SMOG) and accuracy after ChatGPT-4 rewriting toward an eighth-grade level
evidence.effect: Mean FRE score for rewritten PEMs was significantly lower than for nonrewritten materials on each topic (P < .01), except spinal stenosis (P = .104). Original PEMs scored significantly above an eighth-grade level on all measures (P < .01 to P < .001). Rewritten PEMs were validated for accuracy.
evidence.quote: The mean FRE score for rewritten PEMs on each topic were significantly lower than nonrewritten materials ( P < .01) except spinal stenosis ( P = .104) and were validated for accuracy.

evidence.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Enhance Patient Educational Resources in Rhinology
evidence.venue: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified ARS patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch Kincaid Grade Level and Reading Ease) of rhinology patient education materials
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL 8.6 for LLM-generated PEMs vs 10.28 for original ARS PEMs (P < .0001); Gemini best with mean FKGL 7.5 and FKRE 65.5
evidence.tradeoff: LLM outputs did not reach the sixth-grade target; authors advise cautious appraisal of LLM-generated content for accuracy.
evidence.quote: The original ARS PEMs had a mean FKGL of 10.28, while AI-generated PEMs demonstrated significantly better readability, with a mean FKGL of 8.6 (P < .0001).

evidence.title: Improving Accessibility to Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Patient Resources Using Artificial Intelligence: A Pilot Study in Patient Education Materials
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified AAFPRS patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Readability of facial plastic and reconstructive surgery patient education materials (FKGL, GFI, FKRE)
evidence.effect: Original PEMs mean FKGL 10.7, GFI 13.48, FKRE 50.8; AI-translated PEMs mean FKGL 8.41, GFI 10.62, FKRE 64.43 (p < 0.001)
evidence.tradeoff: AI-translated PEMs still did not reach the 6th-grade target (mean FKGL 8.41); authors specify physician supervision is needed.
evidence.quote: With physician supervision, AI platforms can improve the readability of PEMs for common FPRS procedures.

evidence.title: Evaluating the use of advanced large language models to improve readability of head and neck cancer patient education materials
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified head and neck cancer patient education articles (baseline FKGL and FRES)
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease Score) after LLM rewriting to a sixth-grade level
evidence.effect: Baseline mean FKGL 10.1 and FRES 51.5. FKGL ≤7 reached in 81.8% of articles for Gemini, 72.7% for Copilot and DeepSeek, and 18.2% for ChatGPT-4o. Claude met it in none. Gemini, Copilot, ChatGPT o3 and DeepSeek significantly reduced FKGL versus originals; ChatGPT-4o showed minimal change; Claude increased difficulty.
evidence.tradeoff: Effectiveness varied substantially across models, and Claude made text harder to read. Rewritten materials must still be reviewed for accuracy before public use.
evidence.quote: Gemini, Copilot, ChatGPT o3, and DeepSeek significantly reduced FKGL compared to originals, while ChatGPT-4o showed minimal change and Claude increased difficulty.

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence language model improves readability of burns first aid information
evidence.venue: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified burns first aid webpages (top 50 English-language pages), compared before and after ChatGPT-3 rewriting
evidence.outcome: Readability of burns first aid patient education materials across five validated readability tools
evidence.effect: PEMs meeting target on all tools rose from 4% to 18%; median grade 6.9 (SD=1.1, not significantly below target, p=.31) to 6 (SD=0.9, significantly below target, p<.001); all readability scores improved significantly (p<.001)
evidence.tradeoff: Even after AI rewriting, only 18% of PEMs met the target on all tools. The abstract does not report accuracy or completeness of the rewritten content.
evidence.quote: Once rewritten using AI, paired t-test demonstrated that all readability scores improved significantly (p < .001).

evidence.title: Implementing Generative AI to Enhance Patient Education on Retinopathy of Prematurity
evidence.venue: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
evidence.comparator_used: Original human-written ROP patient education materials found via Google search
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, SMOG) of LLM-rewritten PEMs versus original PEMs
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 and Gemini rewrites reduced readability from baseline FKGL 8.8 ± 1.9 and SMOG 8.6 ± 1.5 to the targeted 6th-grade level
evidence.tradeoff: Only ChatGPT-4 rewrites maintained high quality and reliability (median DISCERN = 4), so the Gemini rewrites did not keep quality and reliability.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 and Gemini rewrote PEMs (Prompt C) from a baseline readability level (FKGL: 8.8 ± 1.9, SMOG: 8.6 ± 1.5) to the targeted 6th-grade reading level.

evidence.title: A Reproducible Framework for Safe LLM-Based Simplification of ICU Discharge Summaries in Clinical Information Systems
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified ICU discharge summary sections from MIMIC-III
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease, grade level)
evidence.effect: Flesch Reading Ease rose from 51.2 ± 6.1 to 58.3–60.3; grade level fell from 9.4 ± 1.2 to 7.6–8.0 (all p < 0.0001)
evidence.tradeoff: Simplification carried omission risk: the best automated configuration (GPT-4o few-shot) still had 2.2% medication omission and 0.4% diagnosis omission. The authors state that patient-facing use needs section-aware constraints, explicit safety checks and human oversight.
evidence.quote: All six prompting conditions significantly improved readability versus the original notes (all p < 0.0001), increasing Flesch Reading Ease from 51.2 ± 6.1 to 58.3–60.3 and reducing grade level from 9.4 ± 1.2 to 7.6–8.0.

evidence.title: The Use of Large Language Models to Generate Education Materials about Uveitis
evidence.comparator_used: Original online uveitis health information from first-page Google results (mean FKGL 11.0 ± 1.4)
evidence.outcome: FKGL of rewritten versus original online uveitis health information
evidence.effect: ChatGPT lowered mean FKGL from 11.0 ± 1.4 to 8.0 ± 1.0 (P < 0.0001). Bard did not lower it (mean FKGL 11.1 ± 1.6).
evidence.tradeoff: ChatGPT's rewrites (mean FKGL 8.0) still did not reach the requested 6th-grade level. Bard did not simplify the text.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT lowered the FKGL to 8.0 ± 1.0 (P < 0.0001) when asked to rewrite the content.

evidence.title: Quantitative Evaluation of Large Language Models to Streamline Radiology Report Impressions: A Multimodal Retrospective Analysis
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified radiology report impressions (readability compared with LLM output)
evidence.outcome: Readability (average reading grade level of four readability indexes)
evidence.effect: All four LLMs (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Bard, Bing) simplified impressions across all three prompts, P < .001; differences between LLMs were found within prompts
evidence.quote: All four LLMs simplified radiology report impressions across all prompts tested (P < .001).

evidence.title: Readability of Orthopaedic Patient Educational Material: An artificial intelligence application
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical orthopaedics and trauma
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified hospital orthopaedic patient educational articles
evidence.outcome: Mean combined reading grade level of rewritten vs original articles (target 6th grade)
evidence.effect: All four GPT models lowered the mean combined grade level; GPT-3.5-Turbo was least consistent and least effective; GPT-4o-Mini and GPT-4o were most effective and consistent regardless of original difficulty. GPT-4o vs GPT-4o-Mini: 0.421% increase in effectiveness.
evidence.tradeoff: Cost: GPT-4o cost $0.61 for all 35 articles, a 175.38% higher cost than GPT-4o-Mini for the small gain in effectiveness. Accuracy screening found no falsified information or medical inaccuracies.
evidence.quote: All GPT AI models lowered the mean combined grade level (Table 2).

evidence.title: ChatGPT as a tool to improve readability of rheumatology patient education materials: a positive start with significant hurdles
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified ACR patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Readability (reading grade level) of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Mean reading level fell from 12th grade (12.02 ± 1.35) to 9.35 ± 1.12 after ChatGPT simplification; GFI 14.24 to 10.70, FKGL 11.50 to 8.29, CLI 13.31 to 10.18, SMOG 10.33 to 7.68. Simplified materials ranged from grades 7 to 13 and did not reach the 6th-grade target.
evidence.tradeoff: Output failed to reach the 6th-grade AMA target; the authors flag ChatGPT's inherent bias. Accuracy and completeness of the simplified text were not reported.
evidence.quote: The readability of ACR patient education materials exceeds AMA recommendations, and while ChatGPT significantly lowered the reading level, it failed to reach the 6th-grade level.

evidence.title: Currently Available Large Language Models Are Moderately Effective in Improving Readability of English and Spanish Patient Education Materials in Pediatric Orthopaedics
evidence.venue: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified English and Spanish pediatric orthopaedic patient education materials (baseline readability)
evidence.outcome: Proportion of articles at or below sixth-grade reading level (FKGL), plus GFI, SMOG, FRE and FHI scores
evidence.effect: Baseline ≤sixth FKGL was 5.8% for English and 10.0% for Spanish articles. After conversion, English reached 21.4% (ChatGPT-4.0) and 60.2% (Google Gemini). Spanish reached 52.5% (ChatGPT-4.0) and 77.5% (Google Gemini). Gemini outperformed ChatGPT-4.0 on GFI, English FKGL and Spanish SMOG (all P < 0.05).
evidence.tradeoff: Improvement was only moderate: many converted articles still missed the sixth-grade target, especially English articles converted by ChatGPT-4.0. The abstract does not report content accuracy or completeness after simplification.
evidence.quote: 21.4% and 60.2% of ChatGPT-4.0-converted and Google Gemini-converted English PEMs achieved ≤sixth FKGL, respectively.

evidence.title: From complexity to clarity: GPT-4 for patient-centered prostate cancer pathology reports
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified prostate cancer pathology reports (paired t-tests against both GPT-4-turbo simplified versions)
evidence.outcome: Text complexity/readability measured with TextEvaluator across eight text-complexity dimensions
evidence.effect: Overall text complexity significantly reduced (p < 0.001); below-6th-grade versions improved most: academic vocabulary mean 68.47 to 23.16, syntactic complexity p = 0.0018, concrete language 36.65 to 44.12
evidence.quote: GPT-4 significantly reduced the overall text complexity of the pathology reports (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Bridging Health Literacy Gaps in Spine Care: Using ChatGPT-4o to Improve Patient-Education Materials
evidence.venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified AAOS, NASS and AANS spine patient-education materials (paired comparison of readability scores)
evidence.outcome: Readability of spine patient-education materials (FKGL, SMOG Index, language complexity, passive voice)
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL fell from 10.2 ± 2.6 (original) to 6.6 ± 1.3 after ChatGPT-4o revision (p < 0.05). SMOG Index, language complexity and passive voice use also improved. Test-retest ICC was 0.91 to 0.98.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o generated articles with a significantly reduced mean FKGL of 6.6 ± 1.3 (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Pediatric Cataract Education Materials: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online pediatric cataract PEMs retrieved from Google
evidence.outcome: Readability (reading grade level) of patient education materials
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 reduced reading level from 10.59 ± 2.20 to 7.01 ± 0.91 (P < 0.001); original Google PEMs showed significantly improved readability after LLM conversion
evidence.quote: Original PEMs from Google showed significantly improved readability after LLM conversion, with DeepSeek-R1 achieving the greatest reduction in reading level from 10.59 ± 2.20 to 7.01 ± 0.91 (P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Bridging the Health Literacy Gap for Patients With Oral Cancer: Readability Enhancement With AI Chatbots
evidence.venue: Journal of oral pathology & medicine : official publication of the International Association of Oral Pathologists and the American Academy of Oral Pathology
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified NHS oral cancer patient information texts
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL, GFI, CLI, SMOG) of LLM-simplified vs original texts, with content fidelity
evidence.effect: LLM revisions significantly improved all five indices (p < 0.0001); mean FRES of originals 66.4 ± 7.7 vs Claude 81.6 ± 6.2 (only model above the 80 benchmark); proposed leaflet FRES 65.7 rose to 81.2 with Claude; LSA means 0.97, 0.94, 0.96; character 3-5-g cosine 0.85, 0.80, 0.82
evidence.tradeoff: Content fidelity was slightly reduced (character 3-5-g cosine 0.80-0.85), and only Claude reached the FRES 80 benchmark; authors note human oversight is needed.
evidence.quote: LLM-revisions significantly improved readability across all five indices (p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Enhancing readability of USFDA patient communications through large language models: a proof-of-concept study
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified USFDA drug safety communications and medication guides
evidence.outcome: Readability (grade level) of simplified vs original documents, with technical accuracy and key message retention
evidence.effect: Original DSCs grade level 13, MGs 22. Single prompt - DSCs: ChatGPT 4.0 10.1, Gemini 8; MGs: ChatGPT 4.0 7.1, Gemini 6.5. Multiple prompts - DSCs: ChatGPT 4.0 10.3, Gemini 7.5; MGs: ChatGPT 4.0 8, Gemini 6.8. LLM outputs retained technical accuracy and key messages.
evidence.quote: LLMs significantly improved readability, reducing the grade levels to more accessible readings (Single prompt - DSCs: ChatGPT 4.0© 10.1, Gemini© 8; MGs: ChatGPT 4.0© 7.1, Gemini© 6.5.

evidence.title: Tailoring glaucoma education using large language models: Addressing health disparities in patient comprehension
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified published glaucoma abstracts and patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL and FKRE) of GPT-4-simplified text versus original, plus semantic consistency by LSA cosine similarity
evidence.effect: Abstracts: FKGL decreased by 3.21 points (30%, P < .001), FKRE increased by 28.6 points (66%, P < .001). PEMs: FKGL decreased by 2.38 points (28%, P = .0272), FKRE increased by 12.14 points (19%, P = .0459). Mean cosine similarity 0.861 for abstracts and 0.937 for PEMs.
evidence.quote: The transformation of abstracts resulted in FKGL decreasing by an average of 3.21 points (30%, P < .001) and FKRE increasing by 28.6 points (66%, P < .001).

evidence.title: Can Generative Artificial Intelligence Enhance Health Literacy About Lateral Epicondylitis?
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified patient education materials on lateral epicondylitis from top orthopaedic institutions
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level and word count of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Significant reductions in reading grade level of 3.70 ± 1.84 (p<0.001) and word count of 346.72 ± 364.63 (p<0.001)
evidence.quote: Analysis of the original and edited PEMs about LE revealed significant reductions in reading grade level and word count of 3.70 ± 1.84 (p<0.001) and 346.72 ± 364.63 (p<0.001), respectively.

evidence.title: Readability of dermatology patient education materials: a comparative analysis of Turkish Dermatology Association brochures and texts generated by ChatGPT and Gemini
evidence.comparator_used: Original Turkish Dermatology Association brochures (68 PEMs)
evidence.outcome: Ateşman Readability Index score of AI-generated texts vs original brochures
evidence.effect: TDA brochures mean 59.08 ± 5.80 (medium difficulty); all four AI groups scored significantly higher (p < 0.05), with effect sizes r = 0.242 to 0.753.
evidence.quote: All AI-generated groups demonstrated significantly higher readability scores compared with the TDA brochures (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Validation of ChatGPT 3.5 as a Tool to Optimize Readability of Patient-facing Craniofacial Education Materials
evidence.venue: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified craniofacial patient education excerpts (readability scored by calculators)
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of patient education excerpts
evidence.effect: Simplified excerpts' scores were significantly lower than the originals (P < 0.001); mean of simplified excerpts was 7.78, below the maximum recommended 8.
evidence.quote: It was also able to simplify materials to the recommended grade levels.

evidence.title: Enhancing Readability of Online Patient-Facing Content: The Role of AI Chatbots in Improving Cancer Information Accessibility
evidence.venue: Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network : JNCCN
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified cancer patient education content from 34 NCCN Member Institution websites
evidence.outcome: Mean readability grade level (Fry, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG); content quality (DISCERN section 2) and similarity/accuracy as secondary outcomes
evidence.effect: Mean readability fell from grade 13±1.5 (university freshman) to grade 9±0.8 (high school freshman). F1 0.87, precision 0.934, recall 0.814. Cosine similarity to originals 0.915 (95% CI 0.908-0.922). Mean DISCERN of AI content 28.5±5 ("good"), with no significant difference from originals.
evidence.tradeoff: Recall of 0.814 versus precision of 0.934 suggests some original content was not retained in the rewrites. Quality (DISCERN) did not differ significantly from the originals.
evidence.quote: However, after ChatGPT's intervention, the AI-generated outputs had a mean readability score equivalent to a high school freshman education level (grade 9±0.8).

evidence.title: Using ChatGPT to Improve Readability of Interventional Radiology Procedure Descriptions
evidence.comparator_used: Original CIRSE interventional radiology procedure descriptions, left unsimplified
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, Gunning Fog, ARI) improved, but DISCERN credibility and reliability score fell
evidence.effect: FRE 47.2 to 78.4; GF 14.4 to 7.8; ARI 11.2 to 5.8 (p < 0.001); mean DISCERN 3.73 to 2.99 (p < 0.001); 73 procedures
evidence.tradeoff: Reliability and credibility (DISCERN) decreased after ChatGPT simplification, so human review and prompt engineering are suggested.
evidence.quote: The original FRE score was 47.2 (Difficult), improved to 78.4 (Fairly Easy) by ChatGPT.

evidence.title: Readability of Retina Patient Education Materials Generated With a Large Language Model
evidence.comparator_used: Original ASRS Retina Health Fact Sheets (unsimplified)
evidence.outcome: Readability (ARLCalc consensus grade level) of retina patient education text
evidence.effect: ASRS Enhanced (GPT-4 rewritten to sixth-grade level) 9.37 (± 1.09) vs original ASRS Fact Sheet 12.85 (± 0.89); significant difference across the 4 groups (P < .001)
evidence.tradeoff: Rewritten text still did not reach the sixth-grade target. The authors state that specialty-authored material remains the gold standard for accurate medical information.
evidence.quote: The ARLCalc scores for the ASRS Fact Sheet, GPT-4 Response, GPT-4 Enhanced, and ASRS Enhanced responses were 12.85 (± 0.89), 12.37 (± 0.97), 8.66 (± 0.87), and 9.37 (± 1.09), respectively.

evidence.title: Utilizing Large Language Models to Simplify Radiology Reports: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT3.5, ChatGPT4.0, Google Bard, and Microsoft Bing
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified radiology reports (readability indices before vs after LLM simplification)
evidence.outcome: Readability of radiology reports measured with four established readability indices
evidence.effect: All four LLMs (ChatGPT3.5, ChatGPT4.0, Google Bard, Microsoft Bing) significantly simplified the 254 reports; no numeric values given in the abstract; performance varied by prompt and model
evidence.tradeoff: Improvements are needed to ensure accurate clinical representation and optimal readability
evidence.quote: All LLMs significantly simplified the reports, but performance varied based on the prompt used and the specific model.

evidence.title: Assessing AI Simplification of Medical Texts: Readability and Content Fidelity
evidence.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified abstracts and patient education materials (before vs after GPT-4 transformation)
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Flesch Reading Ease) and content fidelity
evidence.effect: FKGL fell from 12th to 5th grade for abstracts and from 13th to 5th for PEMs (p < 0.001); FKRE improved similarly (p < 0.001). Mean LSA cosine similarity was 0.746 for abstracts and 0.953 for PEMs. Expert-rated mean topic similarity was 0.775 for abstracts and 0.715 for PEMs.
evidence.tradeoff: Some content was not preserved: expert topic similarity was 0.775 for abstracts and 0.715 for PEMs. LSA overestimated similarity for longer texts (correlation with experts -0.167 for PEMs; -0.20 above 450 words). The authors say expert validation is crucial.
evidence.quote: FKGL decreased from 12th to 5th grade for abstracts and 13th to 5th for PEMs (p < 0.001).

controls.question: Should our prompts tell the LLM the exact reading grade level or lay audience to write patient-facing text for?
controls.control: Specify a target grade level, readability formula, plain-language rules, or named lay audience in prompts for patient-facing LLM output.
controls.comparator: Default prompt with no reading-level or audience instruction
controls.aim: Bring patient-facing LLM output to a readable level for lay patients
variants: Audience persona such as patient, child, or carer
controls.family_label: native-language processing, translation or back-translation, simplification, reading-level control
tradeoffs: Output missed the requested fifth-grade target and did not get all materials below the recommended level.

evidence.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Increase the Readability of Patient Education Materials in Pediatric Otolaryngology
evidence.comparator_used: Original materials before the fifth-grade prompt (pre/post comparison; no default-prompt arm)
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level after prompting ChatGPT for a fifth-grade reading level
evidence.effect: AAO-HNS materials fell from 10.71 ± 0.71 to 7.9 ± 1.18 (P < .01); the combined set fell from 9.32 ± 1.82 to 7.68 ± 1.12 (P = .0598). The fifth-grade target was not reached.
evidence.tradeoff: Output missed the requested fifth-grade target and did not get all materials below the recommended level.
evidence.quote: However, it did not possess the capability to reduce all materials to be below the recommended reading level.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Utility in Biologic Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Google Web Search
evidence.comparator_used: Default ChatGPT-4o prompt with no reading-level instruction (FRE 11.7, FKGL 16.2 for default answers)
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT answers (Flesch Reading Ease / Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
evidence.effect: Readability 'significantly improved' when ChatGPT was asked to respond at a sixth-grade level; the abstract gives no numeric values for the sixth-grade condition. Default ChatGPT-4o answers had FRE 11.7 and FKGL 16.2 (college graduate level).
evidence.quote: When asking ChatGPT to respond at a sixth-grade level, the readability of the answers significantly improved.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT responses on obstructive sleep apnea for patient education
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
evidence.comparator_used: No prompting (default query with no reading-level or audience instruction)
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of ChatGPT answers
evidence.effect: Patient-friendly prompting mean grade level 12.45 ± 2.32 vs no prompting 14.15 ± 1.59 (physician-level 14.27 ± 2.09; statistics/references 15.00 ± 2.26); P < .0001. Correctness (at least correct) did not differ by prompt, P = .453.
